It feels like I've wandered into a tricky area and I want to do a general vibe check before spending more time on this. Any thoughts?

topics.name: `become` failing compilation inside `cfg(feature = "...")`
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：`become` 即使写在关闭的 `cfg(feature = "...")` 分支中，仍会导致编译失败。这是预期行为，因为相关语法会在宏展开（expansion）之前被拒绝；并非编译器 bug。
- **可行方案**：可以将使用 `become` 的代码放入单独的模块或文件中进行条件编译，也可以对宏本身使用 `cfg`。讨论者确认拆分到独立模块后可以正常工作。
- **性能观察**：在 Verilog 字节码解释器中用显式尾调用替代字节码求值循环，初步测试约提升 8%；在更快 CPU、`codegen-units=1` 和设置 `target-cpu` 后，墙钟时间提升约 35.5%。`rust-preserve-none` 及枚举判别值优化也引发了代码生成讨论；相关优化问题可能是 LLVM 的 missed optimization，建议提交 LLVM issue，期间可使用 `transmute`。
- **`become` 设计方向**：讨论认为仅依赖特殊调用约定（如 `extern "rust-tail"`）会带来可移植性问题；有人希望同时提供一种可移植、即使效率较低的尾递归保证，用于避免递归栈溢出。另一方向则是面向解释器等场景的、目标平台相关且更高效的 `extern "tail"`/`rust-tail`。
- **实现方案与进展**：有人提出将 `become` 转换为循环或 trampoline，处理自递归及互递归；讨论涉及 MIR shim、`ControlFlow`、函数参数打包以及函数指针支持。对于互递归是否需要强连通分量分析、如何表达带参数的 continuation 等仍有疑问。Folkert de Vries 最后提供了该思路的 PoC PR（#165044），但说明仍需完善并处理边界情况。

messages.en:
Question / observation? Does rust-preserve-none block a bunch of optimizations from LLVM? Looking at the codegen, I am frankly a bit surprised at what it is doing, which it is getting right without the rust-preserve-none.

For instance, it turned an `match` statement mapping from discriminant to enum repr (which is just a mov) into a jump table. It doesn't do this in the normal evaluation loop. It also doesn't seem to inline almost any functions not marked with `inline(always)`. Fixing these codegen issues manually, led to a 20% speedup and a 8% respectively.
messages.zh:
问题/观察？ rust-preserve-none是否阻止了LLVM的一系列优化？ 看着codegen ，坦率地说，我对它的作用有点惊讶，它在没有防锈保护的情况下是正确的。

例如，它变成了`match`将判别式映射到枚举repr （这只是一个mov ）的语句映射到跳转表中。它不会在正常评估循环中执行此操作。它似乎也没有内联几乎所有未标记的函数`inline(always)`。手动修复这些codegen问题，分别导致20%和8%的加速。

messages.zh: 如果您的小函数优化不佳，那么这将会有所帮助

wanna review an LLVM PR that implements `tailcc` `byval` for `aarch64` lol https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/206718? 

Using `become` with just `extern "Rust"` turns out to have really hard portability questions. The current idea is to focus on `extern "tail"` instead, which we specify a big vaguely as "do whatever makes tail calls efficient" and is explicitly target-specific (like e.g. `asm!`)

but it would be neat if at least `aarch64` also supported it, LLVM 23 will have good support on x86_64 (as in, I've found no further issues with it so far)
messages.zh:
想审查实施LLVM PR`tailcc` `byval`针对`aarch64`大笑https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/206718?使用`become`只需`extern "Rust"`事实证明，有非常困难的可移植性问题。目前的想法是专注于`extern "tail"`相反，我们模糊地将其指定为“do whatever makes tail calls efficient” ，并明确针对特定目标（例如，`asm!`)

但如果至少`aarch64`也支持它， LLVM 23将在x86_64上获得良好的支持（例如，到目前为止，我没有发现任何进一步的问题）

messages.en: I remember you mentioning something at RustNL about maybe making it a MIR (or one of the other Rust IRs) concept. Essentially guaranteeing it by using gotos. Is that completely off the table because it is too complex?
messages.zh: 我记得你在RustNL提到过将其作为一个MIR （或其他Rust IR之一）概念。基本上通过使用gotos来保证它。这是否因为过于复杂而完全不在考虑范围之内？

messages.en: there is an approach somewhere, but the issue with it really is that even in the best case, it's not what true users of tail calls want: they want the extra registers for passing arguments
messages.zh: 在某个地方有一种方法，但它的问题在于，即使在最好的情况下，它也不是真正的尾调用用户想要的：他们需要额外的寄存器来传递参数

messages.en: like I suspect you get some good use out of `preserve-none`, `extern "tail"` is supposed to be that and more (lifting the same-signature restriction)
messages.zh: 我怀疑你可以很好地利用`preserve-none`, `extern "tail"`应该是这样和更多（解除相同的签名限制）

@_**Gijs Burghoorn|644446** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/.60become.60.20failing.20compilation.20inside.20.60cfg.28feature.20.3D.20.22.2E.2E.2E.22.29.60/near/610901509):
```quote
Essentially guaranteeing it by using gotos. Is that completely off the table because it is too complex?
```

Personally, at least, I really want the answer to be "here's the subset of `become` that we can always do so you can write at least basic tail-recursive loops if you like that better than `for`/`loop` in some situation".

But that will need to be somewhat restricted.  That's ok, though!  If someone could find a reasonable set of restrictions that we can actually implement, great -- it intentionally wouldn't support the tricky things like the interpreter tricks.

I just don't want to [edit: only] ship "well we have `become` but only with a weird calling convention so you shouldn't use it if you care about portability".  I want at least "yes, you can write your functional programming TCE homework in portable rust".
messages.zh:
@_* * Gijs Burghoorn | 644446 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/.60become.60.20failing.20compilation.20inside.20.60cfg.28feature.20.3D.20.22.2E.2E.2E.22.29.60/near/610901509):
```quote

messages.en:
It'd be really good to avoid needing SCC for this, because that works poorly with queries and such.  (Notably even inlining doesn't use SCC, and that's sorta the poster child for obvious place that the SCC would be good.)

I was thinking that you can probably avoid the SCC because all you care about are functions that themselves use `become` -- if I mutally-recurse through something where one of the steps *isn't* `become` that doesn't need to work well.

So maybe:
- For anything using `become`, we always include the MIR in the rlib
- We used that MIR to on-demand emit a shim version of the MIR that (rather than actually making a tail call) returns `ControlFlow<T, fn()>` instead of `T` where the `fn` is the shim of the callee.
  - Hmm, that kinda wants a recursive type `ControlFlow<T, fn() -> ControlFlow<T, fn() -> ...>>` so I'm not sure what the type should actually be.
- Any non-`become` call into a `become`-using function emits a loop of calling the continuation until `Break`.

Which I think is thus doable in isolation.

That allows a rule of something like "you can `become` any *static* call with the same signature", which is also sufficient for `musttail` on targets with LLVM support.  And it's trivially true for tail-self-recursion.
messages.zh:
避免为此需要SCC真的很好，因为这对于查询等工作效果不佳。  （值得注意的是，即使是内联也不使用SCC ，这有点像是SCC会很好的明显位置的海报。）

我想你可能可以避免SCC ，因为你只关心自己使用的功能`become`--如果我相互递归某个步骤*不是*`become`不需要很好地工作。

因此，可能：
-对于任何使用`become`，我们始终将MIR包含在rlib中
-我们使用MIR按需发出MIR的垫片版本（而不是实际进行尾部调用）`ControlFlow<T, fn()>`而不是`T`在哪里`fn`是被叫方的垫片。
  -嗯，那有点想要一个递归类型`ControlFlow<T, fn() -> ControlFlow<T, fn() -> ...>>`所以我不确定实际上应该是什么类型。
-任何非`become`呼入`become`-using函数发出调用Continuation的循环，直到`Break`.

因此，我认为这是孤立可行的。

这允许这样的规则： “你可以`become`任何具有相同签名的*静态*调用"，这也足以`musttail`在LLVM支持的目标上。对于尾部自递归来说，这几乎是正确的。

topics.name: What session state is hashed for incremental?
topics.name_zh: 哪个会话状态为增量哈希？
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：讨论围绕增量编译中哪些 `Session` 状态会被哈希/跟踪，以及 AST lowering 从 AST 生成 HIR 时依赖 `lint store` 是否安全。`lint store` 目前似乎没有被增量系统直接哈希，但其变化可能影响生成的 HIR。
- **已跟踪的状态**：标记为 `TRACKED` 或 `TRACKED_NO_CRATE_HASH` 的选项发生变化时，会使增量编译会话目录失效；`StableCrateId`（crate 名称、`is_lib`、`-Cmetadata`）变化时会切换到不同的增量编译会话目录。其他状态只有在通过 `eval_always` 或可 feed 的 query 访问时才会被跟踪。
- **关于 `lint store`**：当前已经在缓存 query 中使用 `lint store` 生成 HIR，因此这些 query 相对于 `lint store` 的变化并非纯函数；但现阶段假定自定义 `rustc` driver 不会在未使缓存失效的情况下改变其提供的 `lint store`，否则属于 driver 的错误。
- **对 PR #164918 的结论**：AST lowering 目前总是执行，因此让它依赖 `lint store` 是可以接受的，PR #164918 不会额外引入问题。若未来希望让 `cargo clippy` 和 `cargo check` 共享产物，就需要将 `lint store` 纳入跟踪；届时这一问题需要进一步处理。
- **仍未解决/改进项**：有人认为应将“哪些 session state 会被增量系统跟踪、哪些状态可安全访问”的规则补充到 `rustc-dev-guide`；此外，未来更多流程进入 query 系统后，`lint store` 依赖是否仍然安全需要重新评估。

messages.en:
I've made a PR (https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/164918) that uses the lint store during AST lowering to HIR.

@**mejrs** pointed out in review that he's not sure that is correct. If the lint store changes between incremental sessions, for example because a hypothetical rustc driver only sometimes register lints, this could affect the outputted hir. And the lint store does not seem to be hashed anywhere for incremental. I think this specific case is fine (at least until more parts become querified), because AST lowering is before the query system becomes active.

However this did make me realize that one can also just access the lint store later in the compiler where the query system is active, and this would not be correctly tracked by the query system. So I guess my questions are: 

1. Is it documented anywhere what parts of the session state are tracked by the query system, and are safe to access for incremental purposes?
2. Is it fine for AST lowering to depend on the lint store, both now and in the future?

cc @**Alejandra González** @**Jack Huey** as you have worked on https://goals.rust-lang.org/2026/incremental-system-rethought.html and might know this?
messages.zh:
我已经做了公关（https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/164918)在AST降至HIR期间使用棉绒商店。

@ * * mejrs * *在评论中指出，他不确定这是否正确。 如果lint存储在增量会话之间发生变化，例如因为假设的rustc驱动程序有时只注册lint ，这可能会影响输出的hir。 而且， lint商店似乎没有在任何地方进行增量哈希处理。我认为这种特殊情况是可以的（至少在更多的部分被查询之前） ，因为AST降低是在查询系统变为活动之前。

然而，这确实让我意识到，人们也可以稍后在查询系统处于活动状态的编译器中访问lint存储，而查询系统将无法正确跟踪。 所以我想我的问题是： 

1.它是否在任何地方记录了会话状态的哪些部分由查询系统跟踪，并且可以安全地进行增量访问？
2.现在和将来，降低AST是否可以依赖于棉绒店？

topics.name: Things missing from rustc internal API docs?
topics.name_zh: Rustc内部API文档中缺少的内容？
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：`rustc` 内部 API 文档存在不完整或异常情况。搜索 `InstanceKind` 时能看到部分结果，但对应的实际类型页面似乎缺失或显示不正常。
- **具体表现**：文档页面显示的是正确类型的 re-export，但链接指向 `use` 而非原始定义；相关 `use` 甚至不是公开项。尽管启用了记录私有项的选项，这种展示仍然很奇怪。
- **更广泛影响**：讨论者指出这类“文档合并”问题很多，例如搜索 `rustc_middle::traits::ImplSource` 也可能难以找到目标，并表示通常会自行生成文档来规避。
- **关于原因的讨论**：有人猜测问题可能与 PR #163582 的文档合并变更有关；Michael Howell 认为这不像该 PR 引起的问题，因为完整路径搜索仍能找到条目，且 beta 文档中没有复现同样问题。
- **当前结论与未解决事项**：Michael Howell 随后表示发现了问题，并指向 PR #165024，但聊天记录没有进一步说明该 PR 的具体原因、修复内容或最终解决状态。

topics.name: GEP constant 0 in `gpu_offload.rs`
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：`compiler/rustc_codegen_llvm/src/builder/gpu_offload.rs` 中多处使用了常量偏移为 `0` 的 `gep`/`inbounds_gep`；由于这在 LLVM 中通常是 no-op，Bee 询问是否存在特殊用途、能否安全移除。
- **地址空间因素**：workingjubilee 询问这些 GEP 是否涉及特殊的 address space；Bee 检查后表示，相关指针看起来都是普通的 `alloca`，没有发现这一因素。
- **可能的历史原因**：scottmcm 推测这可能是 typed pointers 时代的遗留写法，例如对 `[4 x u32]*` 做 GEP 可以得到 `u32*`，当时可能比 `bitcast` 更清晰。
- **当前判断**：Manuel 表示 Offload 开始得较晚，已经是在 typed pointers 之后；这些 GEP 很可能只是最初参考 Clang 生成 LLVM IR 时保留下来的写法，之后尚未彻底清理。
- **未解决事项**：Manuel 尚未仔细确认是否可以移除这些常量 `0` 的 GEP；他表示可以提交 PR 并指定他参与审查。

topics.name: ✔ optimize_for_size
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：`optimize_for_size` 是供标准库/`compiler-builtins` 使用的 `cfg`，可让代码在“快速实现”和“小体积实现”之间选择；而 `-Os`/`-Oz` 是编译器整体优化级别，不能直接替代这种源码级选择。讨论认为可以考虑在启用 `-Os` 或其他 size 优化级别时自动启用相关 `cfg`，但会改变标准库算法，需谨慎。

- **`-Os` 与 `-Oz` 并非简单的“温和/激进”关系**：实际效果高度依赖目标平台和代码，尤其在嵌入式平台上，`-Oz` 可能因极低的 inlining threshold 阻止后续优化，最终比 `-Os` 更大或更慢。Rust 代码依赖内联实现良好 codegen，而 LLVM 当前 `-Oz` 的 inline threshold（5）被认为对 Rust 过于保守。

- **优化范围存在分歧**：现有 `optimize_for_size` 主要通过 `no_builtin_lookup_tables` 等方式移除会膨胀二进制的 lookup table；而 `compiler-builtins` 中更小但明显更慢的 `memcpy`/`memset`/`memcmp` 实现属于更激进的 size-for-speed 权衡。有人建议增加 `optimize_for_size_aggressive`，也有人倾向拆分为更具体的 `slim_mem_ops` 等 feature/cfg，以避免一个总开关隐含过多不可预测的优化。

- **嵌入式使用场景与标准库默认值**：不同嵌入式项目对 flash、性能、向量化和中断时限的需求差异很大，不能简单地为整个 target tuple 更改标准库默认优化级别。用户可能希望使用 `-O3` 保留 vectorizer，同时选择小型 `memcpy`。标准库实现是否随 opt-level 自动切换，也可能造成难以预期的性能下降。

- **结论与未解决问题**：讨论推动了为更激进优化建立 ACP；后续曾改为 `slim_mem_ops` 方案，并建议将讨论转移到 libs ACP `#907`，但该 ACP 后来被关闭，话题标记为 resolved。仍未解决的问题包括：应采用通用的 `optimize_for_size_aggressive` 还是具体的 `slim_mem_ops`、如何制定和测试 size 优化准则，以及 Rust 对 `memcpy` 等 compiler-builtins 的覆盖机制、weak linking 和 externally implementable items（EII）仍存在文档和实现限制。

messages.en: Why is `optimize_for_size` a feature, rather than picking up -Os/-Oz?
messages.zh: 为什么`optimize_for_size`一个功能，而不是拿起-Os/-Oz ？

messages.en: First of all, it’s important to note that -Oz increases binary size over -Os in many scenarios. It really depends on the target and the specific code you are compiling, and the overall experience has been that you should try both and use whichever is better (at the moment). I think there was a RustWeek talk discussing this as well (will look it up in a moment)
messages.zh: 首先，重要的是要注意-Oz在许多情况下会增加二进制大小超过-Os。这实际上取决于目标和您正在编译的特定代码，总体体验是，您应该尝试两者并使用（目前）更好的代码。我认为RustWeek也在讨论这个问题（稍后会查找）

messages.en: Secondly, I am not aware of any way of detecting `-C opt_level` from code, and I’m not sure that’s a good idea in general?
messages.zh: 其次，我不知道有任何方法可以检测`-C opt_level`从代码中，我不确定这是否是一个好主意？

messages.en: This feels like something that has wide ramifications.
messages.zh: 这感觉就像是具有广泛影响的东西。

messages.en: opt-levels are for the compiler, optimize_for_size is for the standard library.
messages.zh: opt-levels用于编译器， optimize_for_size用于标准库。

@_**kleines Filmröllchen|1174750** [schrieb](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/optimize_for_size/near/629921868):
```quote
First of all, it’s important to note that -Oz increases binary size over -Os in many scenarios. It really depends on the target and the specific code you are compiling, and the overall experience has been that you should try both and use whichever is better (at the moment). I think there was a RustWeek talk discussing this as well (will look it up in a moment)
```

This means that we can’t just go to the more aggressive size optimization mode (e.g. using my much slower but 10x more compact memcpy versions) on -Oz, since e.g. in my use case with PebbleOS, other parts of the code increase in size more than the savings we get from this. It is really not as simple as that, unfortunately

@_**Kevin Reid (kpreid)|608145** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/optimize_for_size/near/629932955):
````quote
@_**Jonathan Keller|887758** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/optimize_for_size/near/629928744):
```quote
-Oz turns the inlining threshold very low, which prevents a lot of optimizations that could have happened after inlining
```

This feels like a thing that’s just fundamentally incorrect for Rust, due to the frequency of supposed-to-be-zero-cost-wrappers in Rust code. Could this be fixed somehow?

* If the inlining threshold were *not* lowered, would `-Oz` still mean something?
* If libraries routinely marked trivial functions `#[inline(always)]`, would this work better?
* Could we have an `#[inline(almost_certainly_inlines_to_almost_nothing)]` that expresses the thing that optimizing-for-size needs to know while having fewer negative effects on other cases?
````

I think ideally we'd have an optimizer that speculatively inlines, performs a bunch of optimizations and then checks if the overall size went down, if yes try inlining some more, otherwise roll back to the previous results.

Java Hotspot's C2 compiler does this, but that's a JIT which can afford burning a lot of CPU-time on small areas of code (it's called hotspot for a reason). Doing this for an AOT compiler would probably be prohibitive in most cases... but for a constrained embedded device the total amount of code to crunch through has to be fairly small in the first place...

messages.en: In my mind this is not dissimilar to the search problem for game moves: you look ahead N moves and evaluate which board state is the best (in that case given the best possible play from the opponent, but that isn't relevant here). You could do a lookahead N possible inlining decisions. But I guess that doesn't work well in a bottom up approach.

messages.en:
The basic engineering problem IMO is that you first need an IR that can efficiently represent “rolling back” changes or otherwise support exploring multiple possibile rewrites. This ends up being fairly expensive both in engineering effort and compile time compared to only representing the current state. And it’s not clear that this is very useful and thus worth it, compared to the status quo of greedy rewrites with possibly quite involved heuristics for profitability.

For the kinds of optimizations that Cranelift does in its e-graph, it [turned out](https://cfallin.org/blog/2026/04/09/aegraph/) that the “explore multiple possibilities and pick best” part wasn’t actually useful in their context, but other aspects (sea of nodes approach, unifying many traditionally distinct passes) were.

On the other hand, loop vectorization in LLVM does have a little bit of “IR with ability to explore multiple options” (VPlan, Sandbox IR) because that optimization is arguably to complex to implement as single-shot IR rewrite. Although I’m not sure if there is any consensus yet about how successful the “try multiple rewrites and pick best one” part. (I’m not even sure if that part is used in the default pipeline yet)
messages.zh:
我认为，根本的工程问题是，首先得有一种 IR，能高效表示对修改的“回滚”，或者以其他方式支持探索多种可能的重写。与只表示当前状态相比，这会带来相当高的工程成本和编译时间开销。相比目前采用贪心重写、并可能使用复杂启发式方法判断收益的做法，尚不清楚这种机制是否足够有用、值得投入。

对于 Cranelift 在 e-graph 中进行的那类优化，[实践发现](https://cfallin.org/blog/2026/04/09/aegraph/)，“探索多种可能并选择最佳结果”这一部分在它们的场景中其实没有用，反而是其他方面发挥了作用，例如 sea of nodes 方法，以及统一许多传统上分离的优化遍。

另一方面，LLVM 的循环向量化确实包含一点“能够探索多个方案的 IR”机制，例如 VPlan 和 Sandbox IR，因为这种优化可能过于复杂，难以通过一次性的 IR 重写来实现。不过，我不确定大家是否已经就“尝试多种重写并选出最佳结果”的效果形成共识；我甚至不确定默认优化流水线是否已经在使用这一部分。

messages.en: basically: the memcpy and other stuff compiler-builtins offers is all weak linking since we don't want to conflict with an existing libc if it exists, so, you can always redefine them

messages.en: so, the main reason why we replied the way we did was, if the issue is *just* memcpy, it is a rare enough use case you should just be able to provide it in your own code, but if that doesn't work or there are other functions in std you'd want it for we would be happy to help out
messages.zh: 所以，我们那样回复的主要原因是：如果问题仅仅在于 memcpy，这是个足够少见的需求，你应该可以在自己的代码中提供实现；但如果这行不通，或者你还希望 std 中其他函数提供这种能力，我们也很愿意帮忙。

messages.en: (note: memcpy is sufficiently weird with LLVM because if you're not careful it will just look at your memcpy impl and decide it's close enough to memcpy to just replace with a call to memcpy, creating an infinite stack overflow. it's supposed to not do this but it sometimes does anyway)
messages.zh: （注意：memcpy 与 LLVM 的交互相当特殊。如果不小心，LLVM 可能看到你的 memcpy 实现，认为它足够像 memcpy，就把它替换成对 memcpy 的调用，从而导致无限递归和栈溢出。它本不该这样做，但有时确实会发生。）

messages.en: this is exactly why the mechanisms for actually overriding these functions is either bad or underdocumented
messages.zh: 这恰好说明，实际覆盖这些函数的机制要么不好用，要么缺乏足够的文档。

messages.en: the way this entire situation looks like to me is basically just that there’s nothing embedded Rust can do to improve the language side, and wg-embedded might be right by barely engaging with the compiler itself and just write a few useful libraries and call it a day
messages.zh: 在我看来，这整件事就像是在说，嵌入式 Rust 无法对语言层面做出任何改善；wg-embedded 也许是对的：基本不与编译器本身打交道，只写几个有用的库，然后就这样算了。

messages.en: say what you want but the discussion on this topic clearly displayed a second-class-citizen attitude towards embedded systems, especially smaller ones. anything that could even just barely hurt other systems is unacceptable. meanwhile regular rust constantly makes decisions, especially in compiler optimizations, that hurt some or many parts of embedded, and that’s totally fine
messages.zh: 随你们怎么说，但这个话题的讨论显然体现了将嵌入式系统、尤其是小型嵌入式系统当成二等公民的态度。任何哪怕稍微可能影响其他系统的事情都不可接受；与此同时，普通 Rust 却不断作出会伤害某些乃至许多嵌入式场景的决定，尤其是在编译器优化方面，而这又完全没问题。

messages.en: I mean, you make a valid point, and you have every reason to be salty about that being the status quo
messages.zh: 我的意思是，你指出的问题确实成立。对于这样的现状，你完全有理由感到不满。

messages.en: like to be clear, we have added a number of small changes that help for cases like this. for example, we have a cfg flag that just removes floating-point formatting entirely from libcore because the rust for linux folks wanted it. it's just really difficult to quantify what "optimize for ___" means since while your case is extremely straightforward it is also not intuitive, since for example indexing into strings at all imports all the unicode formatting machinery
messages.zh: 说明一下，我们确实已经加入了一些帮助这类场景的小改动。例如，应 Rust for Linux 开发者的要求，我们增加了一个 cfg 开关，可以从 libcore 中彻底移除浮点格式化功能。只是，“为某个目标优化”究竟意味着什么，实在很难量化。你的场景虽然非常明确，但其中的行为并不直观：例如，只要对字符串进行索引，就可能把整套 Unicode 格式化机制引入进来。

messages.en: Do realize that I won’t change any minds here, but I know it’s not just me who is upset about the state of Rust embedded — it’s really amazing in some ways, but also embarassingly bad in other ways, and usually there are clear paths to improvement (i.e. the language foundations are well-designed such that it can be a great fit). To me embedded is still the most important area of application for Rust, but everyone here seemingly only cares about writing web servers in the hundredth new language since 1995
messages.zh: 我知道我在这里改变不了谁的想法，但对 Rust 嵌入式现状感到不满的并不只有我。在某些方面它确实非常出色，另一些方面却差得令人尴尬，而且通常明明有清晰的改进路径——语言基础的设计本来很好，完全可以非常适合这个领域。对我而言，嵌入式仍然是 Rust 最重要的应用领域，但这里的人似乎只关心用自 1995 年以来出现的第不知道多少门新语言来写 Web 服务器。

messages.en: I actually think a lot of people share that mentality, since unfortunately a lot of low-level code is written in C and that makes reasoning about its correctness is impossible
messages.zh: 我其实觉得很多人都认同这种想法。遗憾的是，大量底层代码仍用 C 编写，这让对其正确性进行推理变得不可能。

messages.en: Yup removing or replacing fmt is a big thing, but even embedded doesn’t care since most systems only need it for logging and defmt solves this on most platforms that have proper debug probes/serial support. (Not Pebble though.)
messages.zh: 对，移除或替换 fmt 是件大事，但即使在嵌入式领域，人们也往往不太关心，因为大多数系统只在日志中需要它；在具备合适调试探针或串口支持的平台上，defmt 已经解决了这个问题。（不过 Pebble 不行。）

messages.en: for embedded the only new language in the last 40 years has been C++, slightly, and maybe Simulink if you count it (counterexamples welcome, but I can’t think of anything right now)
messages.zh: 对嵌入式而言，过去 40 年唯一算得上新语言的，多少也就是 C++；如果算上 Simulink，也许还可以加上它。欢迎举反例，不过我现在确实想不出别的。

messages.en: tbqh a big part of this is that LLVM itself is still rooted in C, and so primitives like memcpy just want to pretend you're linked against libc instead of being part of the language
messages.zh: 说实话，一个很大的原因是 LLVM 本身仍根植于 C。因此，像 memcpy 这样的基础操作仍倾向于假定你会链接 libc，而不是将它们视为语言本身的一部分。

messages.en: wasn’t there a linux-unknown target which doesn’t link against a C library? and so has to ship all of its own primitives (as well as syscall interfaces)
messages.zh: 不是有一个不链接 C 库的 linux-unknown 目标吗？因此，它必须自行提供所有基础操作以及系统调用接口。

messages.en: yes, it's just that LLVM itself has trouble with such targets because it still assumes libc is present, and that's why stuff like compiler-builtins exists
messages.zh: 是的，只不过 LLVM 本身处理这种目标时还有问题，因为它仍假定 libc 存在；这也正是 compiler-builtins 之类组件存在的原因。

messages.en: anyways improving EII for memcpy and friends would still help us, since we could just ship that in our library and noone will complain. but since this is a relatively complex feature it might take a while to even be usable on nightly
messages.zh: 无论如何，改进 memcpy 及相关函数的 EII 支持仍然会帮到我们，因为这样就能直接把实现放进自己的库里，也不会有人抱怨。但这是一项相对复杂的功能，可能还要过一段时间，才能在 nightly 上真正可用。

messages.en: yeah, and to be clear *hopefully* if you just define `extern "C" memcpy(…)` with the definition you added in your crate it *should* work, but I'm not 100% on that. unfortunately we are currently just dealing with the annoying hands dealt to us, and fixing compiler implementations to stop assuming everything is C
messages.zh: 对，说明一下：如果你在自己的 crate 中定义 `extern "C" memcpy(…)`，并使用你添加的那个函数体，那么我希望它应该能起作用，不过我并不完全确定。遗憾的是，我们现在只能应对这些棘手的既有条件，同时修正编译器实现，让它们不要再假定一切都是 C。

messages.en:
to clarify for our platform:
- we (have to) link against a specific static library that provides *some* standard c functions
- the linker invocation also pulls in *some* libc which may provide other symbols
- as far as i can tell, compiler-builtins’ memcpy/memcmp are always pulled in and preferred, even though we ask cargo to build a static library (that is allowed to depend on libc)
messages.zh:
说明一下我们的平台情况：
- 我们必须链接一个指定的静态库，它提供部分标准 C 函数。
- 链接器命令还会引入某个 libc，它可能提供其他符号。
- 据我观察，compiler-builtins 的 memcpy/memcmp 总是会被引入并优先使用，即使我们要求 Cargo 构建的是允许依赖 libc 的静态库。

messages.en:
@_**Ben Kimock (Saethlin)|120827** [schrieb](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/optimize_for_size/near/637934803):
```quote
LLVM has facilities to support writing your own builtins and it has intrinsics like `llvm.memcpy.inline`.
```

I’m actually aware of LLVM intrinsics but I don’t even know where to start with overwriting those. As we’ve demonstrated this is an issue on the Rust level, since the problem is Rust’s implementation of those intrinsics, not LLVM’s or the platform’s. So in my opinion Rust should provide a solution, not LLVM or the platform.
messages.zh:
@_**Ben Kimock (Saethlin)|120827** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/optimize_for_size/near/637934803):

LLVM 提供了支持自行编写内建函数的机制，也有 `llvm.memcpy.inline` 这样的 intrinsic。
```

我其实知道 LLVM 的 intrinsic，但完全不知道该从哪里入手覆盖它们。正如我们已经展示的，这是 Rust 层面的问题：问题出在 Rust 对这些 intrinsic 的实现上，而非 LLVM 或平台的实现。因此，我认为解决方案应该由 Rust 提供，而不是 LLVM 或平台。

messages.en: For example, the distributed sysroot builds c-b with a lot of CGUs because that helps most linkers resolve what symbols they need when c-b is injected at the end of the linker arguments, except that for embedded platforms often people want to not compile all of the helpers again and again in every CGU so the CGU count gets set to 1 and now the symbol preference trick doesn't work
messages.zh: 例如，分发的 sysroot 会用很多 CGU 来构建 c-b，因为当 c-b 被加到链接器参数的末尾时，这样有助于大多数链接器解析所需符号。但在嵌入式平台上，人们通常又不希望在每个 CGU 中反复编译所有辅助函数，于是把 CGU 数量设为 1，结果优先选择符号的那套技巧就失效了。

messages.en: > This indicates that the callee function at a call site is not recognized as a built-in function. LLVM will retain the original call and not replace it with equivalent code based on the semantics of the built-in function, unless the call site uses the builtin attribute. This is valid at call sites and on function declarations and definitions.
messages.zh: > 这表示调用点的被调用函数不被识别为内建函数。LLVM 会保留原始调用，而不会根据该内建函数的语义将其替换为等价代码，除非调用点使用了 builtin 属性。该属性可用于调用点，也可用于函数声明和定义。

messages.en: Unfortunately there are also a couple other things we do with the crate attr in rustc, and someone would have to be motivated to figure out what and why and how to untangle those things
messages.zh: 遗憾的是，rustc 还会根据这个 crate 属性做另外几件事。得有人有动力去弄清楚这些事情分别是什么、为什么这样做，以及如何将它们拆分开。

messages.en: Clang also does this at the CGU level, using `-fno-builtin(-X)` applies the LLVM attribute to all functions in the CGU, and they similarly don't expose a way to do it per-function.
messages.zh: Clang 也在 CGU 层面这样处理：使用 `-fno-builtin(-X)` 会把对应的 LLVM 属性应用到该 CGU 中的所有函数，而且它同样没有提供按函数设置的方法。

messages.en: and I think similarly, `-fno-builtin` has other implications as well
messages.zh: 而且我想，`-fno-builtin` 同样还会产生其他影响。

messages.en: Also LLVM has an exception that non-mangled symbols with the names corresponding to various functions won't get replaced. So as long as the actual implementation is in a function called `memcpy`, LLVM won't eat it.
messages.zh: 另外，LLVM 有个例外：如果某些不经过名称修饰的符号恰好对应这些函数名，就不会替换它们。所以，只要真正的函数实现位于名为 `memcpy` 的函数中，LLVM 就不会把它吃掉。

messages.en: But I think that's more of a concession to "this is how people have been doing this for 50 years, we have to try to not break things too bad" rather than an intended feature.
messages.zh: 不过，我觉得这更像是在迁就“人们已经这样写了 50 年，我们得尽量别把它破坏得太严重”这一事实，而不是有意设计的功能。

messages.en:
@_**Clar Fon|330161** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/optimize_for_size/near/637909287):
```quote
like earlier today apparently folks from compiler clarified that externally implementable items are actually further along than we thought so we might just end up offering that for more stuff in std if it'd help for stuff like this, since it means other crates can just give you your code changes easily. but if that's not the case we'd be happy to change our mind
```

EIIs without default impls are IMHO fully ready for use in the standard library once https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/159843 lands, which is hopefully within the next couple of weeks.

EIIs with default impls are blocked on either fixing weak symbols on all targets we support or implementing an alternative way to handle them on targets were weak symbols are broken.
messages.zh:
@_**Clar Fon|330161** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/optimize_for_size/near/637909287):
```quote
比如，今天早些时候编译器团队的人似乎澄清了，可由外部实现的项的进展比我们原先以为的更成熟。因此，如果有助于这类场景，我们最终可能会为 std 中更多内容提供这种机制，因为其他 crate 就能方便地提供你需要的实现改动。但如果实际情况并非如此，我们也很愿意改变看法。
```

我认为，不带默认实现的 EII 已经完全可以供标准库使用，只需等待 https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/159843 合并，希望就在接下来的几周内。

带默认实现的 EII 则还受阻：要么修复所有受支持目标上的弱符号问题，要么在弱符号无法正常工作的目标上实现替代机制。

messages.en: FWIW I don’t think weak symbols should be broken on embedded ARM with a standard GCC toolchain but what do I know
messages.zh: 供参考，我认为在使用标准 GCC 工具链的嵌入式 ARM 上，弱符号本不应该有问题；不过也许是我了解得不够。

messages.en: unfortunately they might be
messages.zh: 遗憾的是，它们可能确实有问题。

messages.en: It's only Windows-GNU with some rough edges around MacOS, as far as I am aware. And at least some of the bigger bugs on Windows were fixed in more recent binutils versions, we just don't have that in CI
messages.zh: 据我了解，主要只有 Windows-GNU 有问题，macOS 也有一些边角问题。而且 Windows 上至少有一些较大的 bug 已在较新的 binutils 中修复，只是我们的 CI 还没使用这些版本。

messages.en: I don't follow the problem with symbol preferences? If you're defining a new `memcpy` symbol without marking it weak, then that's the version that should wind up getting used. I don't know why you're getting duplicate symbol errors, where is that coming from?
messages.zh: 我不太理解符号优先级的问题。如果你定义了一个新的 `memcpy` 符号，而且没有把它标为弱符号，那么最后就应该使用这个版本。我不知道你为什么会遇到重复符号错误；那个错误是从哪里来的？

messages.en: And `-Clto` also has some issues around weak linkage I believe that are preventing compiler-builtins from participating in LTO. Not sure if those apply to EIIs specifically though.
messages.zh: 此外，我认为 `-Clto` 在弱链接方面也有一些问题，导致 compiler-builtins 无法参与 LTO。不过我不确定这些问题是否也会具体影响 EII。

messages.en: And in any case we can't really use EII defaults for the standard library while they are broken on some targets.
messages.zh: 无论如何，只要 EII 默认实现在某些目标上仍有问题，我们就不能真正把它用于标准库。

messages.en: I'm not entirely convinced things like `memcpy` would be a good use for EII anyway
messages.zh: 而且我也并不完全认同 memcpy 这类东西适合使用 EII。

messages.en: Either way the end result will still be that three billion libraries ship slightly different versions of memcpy because they need the small size but nobody can agree on anything in the ecosystem (and the standard library is explicitly choosing not to solve the problem, *which is the whole thing you all are doing right here all the time since forever*)
messages.zh: 不管怎样，结果仍会是几十亿个库分别携带略有不同的 memcpy，因为它们都需要小体积，但生态里谁也无法达成共识；而标准库则明确选择不解决这个问题——可这恰恰一直就是你们在这里所做的事情。

messages.en: For me this solution still feels a little bit like saying “`#![no_core]` exists, you can implement your own lang items” and pretending like that solves all the problems with `core`
messages.zh: 对我来说，这种方案仍然有点像在说：“已经有 `#![no_core]`，你可以实现自己的 lang item。”然后就假装这样解决了 core 的所有问题。

messages.en: The reason I found my implementation reasonable in the first place is that there are only a few worthy tradeoffs for these functions, the standard library already has two, and I’m adding the third. EIIs solve that problem by allowing you to have an infinite number of tradeoffs even though that’s entirely unnecessary
messages.zh: 我最初认为自己的实现合理，是因为这些函数值得考虑的取舍其实只有几种：标准库已经提供了两种，我是在添加第三种。而 EII 的解决方法是让你能够作出无限多种取舍，尽管这完全没有必要。

messages.en: Also, to clarify: Noone has to argue with me about this, I’m simply realizing that all my prejudices about how the Rust project treats embedded are in fact entirely true, while I hoped they were incorrect assumptions from a lack of understanding internal processes.
messages.zh: 另外说明一下：谁都不必就这件事和我争论。我只是逐渐发现，自己原先对 Rust 项目如何对待嵌入式的种种偏见竟然都是真的；而我本来希望，那只是因为不了解内部流程而产生的错误猜测。

messages.en: to be clear, we're all very amenable to the situation you're in, just, when you have a most-volunteer project at the whims of external projects like LLVM, we end up accidentally inheriting a lot of their priorities even though we don't want to
messages.zh: 说明一下，我们都很理解你的处境。只是，对于一个主要由志愿者推动、又受到 LLVM 这类外部项目左右的项目而言，我们最终难免无意中继承它们的许多优先级，尽管我们并不愿意这样。

messages.en: and agree, `no_core` is not really a solution to this. we just kinda don't know what the optimal way is. now that we have folks working actively on build-std though that is the obvious path forward, we just have no idea what features we want to offer
messages.zh: 而且我同意，`no_core` 确实不是这个问题的解决方案。我们只是不太清楚最佳做法是什么。现在终于有人积极推进 build-std，这显然是一条可行的方向，但我们还不清楚该提供哪些功能。

messages.en: no_core was a comparison of trying to solve a specific problem with too generic and cumbersome of a hammer
messages.zh: 我用 no_core 打比方，是想说你们在用一种过于通用、也过于笨重的工具来解决一个具体问题。

messages.en: I guess the reason why I see it as not a solution is we effectively never want people to use `no_core`. we want core to always be usable for everyone
messages.zh: 我觉得它算不上解决方案，是因为我们实际上从来都不希望用户使用 `no_core`。我们希望 core 始终能为所有人所用。

messages.en: and so, if that's not the case, we should fix that
messages.zh: 所以，如果做不到这一点，我们就应该修复它。

messages.en: but clearly noone thinks optimize_for_size_aggressive is important enough to warrant its existence for just a few functions
messages.zh: 但显然，没有人认为 optimize_for_size_aggressive 重要到值得仅仅为了几个函数而存在。

messages.en: it's not that it isn't important, it's that we don't really know what guidance to give people for reviewing changes to it, so, it risks becoming a new confusing, undocumented addition
messages.zh: 并不是它不重要，而是我们确实不知道，该给审查这类改动的人什么指导。因此，它有可能成为一个新的、令人困惑又没有文档说明的功能。

messages.en: now, I could definitely come up with a few functions that can get more code size improvements, probably won’t be practically relevant, just to satisfy this requirement in letter but not in spirit, and noone will be happy. also a massive waste of time. so I won’t
messages.zh: 当然，我完全可以再找出几个能够缩减代码体积的函数，也许根本没有实际意义，只是在字面上而非实质上满足这个要求，结果谁也不会满意，还会浪费大量时间。所以我不会这样做。

messages.en: I mean, to be clear, the theoretical idea of there being other functions that could benefit from this satisfies that clause
messages.zh: 说明一下，只要在理论上存在其他可能受益的函数，就已经满足那一条了。

messages.en: I guess the main question is, at what point is size optimization too aggressive, or is that literally impossible
messages.zh: 我想，主要问题是：体积优化在什么程度上才算过于激进？还是说根本不存在“过于激进”的情况？

messages.zh: 我觉得，仅仅为了让自己真正关心的改动合并，就去寻找其他用途，是在极大地浪费我的时间，也不过是在做一些让别人满意的杂活。

messages.en: am speaking as someone who was at that meeting who partook in that decision, which is why I'm saying all this. like, the general vibe is that we're worried about people implementing a new feature in libs and not knowing how it fits in with this existing feature, and what we should do about that. maybe you're right and the answer is we've done more for less and we should just add the flag and not worry about it

messages.en:
@_**Clar Fon|330161** [schrieb](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/optimize_for_size/near/637977899):
```quote
I guess the main question is, at what point is size optimization too aggressive, or is that literally impossible
```

I don’t think that’s impossible, the ACP has plenty of examples of embedded systems with vast processor speeds (which is basically free on semi-modern semiconductor nodes) and extremely limited memory (which is *not at all free* even on modern nodes). 24KB is 1980s levels of memory (even less if you consider that the instructions are larger now), while 100-200MHz is 1990s levels of processor speed
messages.zh:
@_**Clar Fon|330161** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/optimize_for_size/near/637977899):
```quote
我想，主要问题是：体积优化在什么程度上才算过于激进？还是说根本不存在“过于激进”的情况？
```

我不认为这种需求不存在。ACP 中举了很多嵌入式系统的例子：处理器速度很高——在较现代的半导体工艺上，这基本不怎么增加成本——但内存极其有限；即使使用现代工艺，内存也绝对不是免费的。24KB 内存还是 20 世纪 80 年代的水平，如果考虑到如今指令更大，甚至还不如当年；而 100–200MHz 的处理器速度则是 90 年代的水平。

messages.en: @**Trevor Gross** You’re sort of correct, ultimately I don’t care that much, but previous feedback has been "we don’t currently see how this flag is useful for other code". By renaming it, we avoid the generalization and point out that it won’t be useful for other code, since it’s not supposed to be used there. Now you’re steering in the opposite direction, so clearly not everyone agrees on whether this name is too generic or too specialized.
messages.zh: @**Trevor Gross** 你说的有一定道理。说到底，我对名字并没有那么在意，但此前的反馈是：“目前看不出这个开关对其他代码有什么用。”改名之后，我们就避免了这种泛化，并明确指出它不会对其他代码有用，因为它本来就不该用于那里。现在你又在把方向往另一边引，所以显然大家对于这个名字是过于通用还是过于专用，并没有形成一致意见。

messages.en: I also really like @**Clar Fon** ’s suggestion (on the ACP) of splitting optimize_for_size itself. If we do that I would be in favor of subsuming all smaller flags below that big one, with clear documentation that the flag may enable some undesired size optimizations which perform worse. But how that is split up exactly doesn’t really matter for this right now, we could add `slim_mem_ops`, not have it implied by `optimize_for_size` initially, and figure out the rest later
messages.zh: 我也非常喜欢 @**Clar Fon** 在 ACP 中提出的建议：把 optimize_for_size 本身拆开。如果这样做，我赞成让那个大的总开关涵盖所有较小的开关，并明确写进文档：它可能启用某些用户并不想要、且性能更差的体积优化。不过，具体如何拆分，目前其实无关紧要。我们可以先加入 `slim_mem_ops`，最初不让 `optimize_for_size` 自动启用它，剩下的以后再定。

messages.en: (issue with subsuming everything is of course that you need to enable tons of flags once you disable the "big flag", but that’s already true in many large libraries with default crate features; as soon as you don’t want one single default feature, you have to enable the 300 other ones you do actually want)
messages.zh: （当然，把所有选项都合并到一个总开关下的问题是：一旦关掉这个总开关，就得手动启用一大堆小开关。但许多提供默认 crate feature 的大型库已经是这样了：只要不想要其中某一个默认 feature，就得手动打开另外 300 个自己确实想要的 feature。）

messages.en: :vi_fon: and importantly, this also makes the strategy for testing obvious: we can just enable pretty much all of the options unless there are conflicting ones, to make sure they all compile and pass the tests
messages.zh: :vi_fon: 而且重要的是，这样一来测试策略也很明确：只要没有相互冲突的选项，就基本上把所有选项都启用，确保它们都能编译并通过测试。

messages.en: I can’t think of a case right now where we would want to have two different tiers of size optimization within one function, so that would work, yes

topics.name: Adding `<A: Allocator = Global>` to String, ByteString, ...
topics.name_zh: 增加 `<A: Allocator = Global>`to String, ByteString,...
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：讨论是否应为 `String`、`ByteString` 以及其他基于 `Vec` 或堆存储的集合添加 `Allocator` 类型参数（如 `<A: Allocator = Global>`）。`HashMap` 已经支持 allocator 参数。
- **主要阻碍**：为原本非泛型的 `String` 添加参数会影响类型推断；`String` 会从表示 `String<Global>` 变为 `String<_>`，导致现有代码和泛化后的 impl（例如涉及 `Borrow<str>` 的 impl）出现推断问题。有人指出这类改动可能需要语言/编译器支持，并提到等待 edition redirects（#160227）。
- **`ByteString` 方案**：普遍倾向于在 `ByteString` 稳定化前就加入 allocator 参数，以避免重蹈 `String` 的覆辙。对于 `ByteString<A != Global>` 转换为当前不带 allocator 参数的 `String`，无法像 `Global` 情况下一样直接复用内部 `Vec`；暂时可仅为 `ByteString<Global>` 提供相关方法。
- **已知进展/结论**：`ByteString` 的 allocator 支持 PR（#146219）已经准备就绪，因此建议不要在该 PR 之外重复修改 `ByteString`。新增方法本身可在 `String` 获得 allocator 参数后再添加，但事后新增泛型参数会造成 breaking change。
- **仍未解决的问题**：尚未确定如何为 `String` 安全加入 allocator 参数，以及未来新的 trait solver 或默认类型参数改进是否能缓解类型推断问题。

topics.name: splatting primitive `mem::splat` or `ptr::fill`
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：Rust 目前没有将单个值按位广播到整个 slice/未初始化区域的通用 primitive。现有方案包括 `ptr::write(ptr::read)`、`ptr::copy_nonoverlapping`、循环，以及可能使用 `write_bytes`；`<[T]>::fill` 通过 `Clone`，对 `T: TrivialClone` 的按位复制只是优化而非保证。Voxell 提议在 `core::mem` 或 `core::ptr` 中增加 `splat`。
- **接口与语义仍在讨论**：候选形式包括 `T -> T` 或 `Src -> Dst`，接收 raw slice pointer 或 `ptr + len`。其设想的 `unsafe fn splat<T>(value: T, target: *mut T, len: usize)` 要求目标可写、对齐且有效，并要求 `T` 的值可依据 `Drop` 语义进行按位复制；即使 `T: !Copy`，在 `T: TrivialClone` 情况下也会执行按位复制。
- **关于性能依据的讨论**：Voxell 最初比较了循环变量形式、寄存器数量、代码大小等差异；Hanna Kruppe 指出 LLVM 优化后的寄存器压力和 copy 指令数量不一定能直接代表实际收益，相关差异可能只是启发式和上下文造成的随机波动。因此 Voxell 同意不再把寄存器压力/代码大小作为主要动机。
- **更明确的动机是复用实现、避免代码重复**：`Vec::<T>::extend_with` 的 `T: TrivialClone` 特化需要操作 `Vec` 的未初始化区域，不能直接复用要求安全 `&mut [T]` 的 `<[T]>::fill`。两者的特化类型集合和底层广播操作相同，因此可以考虑用基于 raw pointer 的 `splat` 同时实现它们；Hanna 认为共享代码比复制特化逻辑更合理。
- **intrinsic 方案的限制与未决问题**：如果 LLVM 存在适合的特定构造，可以考虑 intrinsic；`llvm.experimental.memset.pattern` 仅支持最多 16 字节的重复模式，且是否有利取决于目标平台，因此若加入 Rust intrinsic，可能只限于 16 字节模式，其余类型使用 library 实现。`splat` 的最终 API、放在 `core::mem` 还是 `core::ptr`、特化范围，以及是否确实应引入该 primitive，仍未确定；为消除 unrolled loop 尾部而根据向量宽度调整长度的方案也被认为复杂且缺乏依据。

messages.en:
My first thought after skimming the comment you linked is that I don't understand why we'd be interested in code size, stack frame size, register pressure, etc. under `-Copt-level=3 -Cno-prepopulate-passes`. When people compile with opt-level=3 they are asking for LLVM optimizations. It can be useful to look at initial LLVM IR to understand if we do something very silly in rustc's codegen, or as part of investigating why LLVM optimizations don't go the way we want. But anything that LLVM can reliably optimize well seems fine for optimized builds.

A library function might still make sense to reduce code duplication, especially for tricky tweaks like specializations or selectively dropping unnecessary UB checks for better debug-mode codegen. But I'd need to take more time to look at all the code in context to form an opinion. Sometimes there are reasons to e.g. skip UB checks in one code path but not in another, even though they mostly do the same operation.
messages.zh: 浏览您链接的评论后，我的第一个想法是，我不明白为什么我们会对下面的代码大小、堆栈帧大小、寄存器压力等感兴趣`-Copt-level=3 -Cno-prepopulate-passes`。当人们使用opt-level = 3进行编译时，他们要求LLVM优化。 查看最初的LLVM IR以了解我们是否在rustc的codegen中做了一些非常愚蠢的事情，或者作为调查为什么LLVM优化没有按照我们想要的方式进行的一部分，可能会很有用。 但是， LLVM可以可靠地优化的任何内容似乎都适合优化构建。库函数对于减少代码重复可能仍然有意义，特别是对于棘手的调整，如专业化或有选择地删除不必要的UB检查以获得更好的调试模式代码生成。但我需要花更多的时间在上下文中查看所有代码才能形成意见。有时有理由跳过一个代码路径中的UB检查，但不在另一个代码路径中，即使它们大多执行相同的操作。

messages.en:
the register pressure point applies to `-Copt-level=3`, not `-Copt-level=3 -Cno-prepopulate-passes`.

the stack copy concerns were raised by mark simulacrum over a version using `ptr.write(ptr::read)`. that can be ignored.

the loop prologue is the main difference between variations that use a pointer induction variable vs an index induction variable. they both vectorize and unroll appropriately and have identical hot loops
messages.zh:
校准压力点适用于`-Copt-level=3`不`-Copt-level=3 -Cno-prepopulate-passes`.

堆栈副本问题是由Mark Simulacrum针对使用`ptr.write(ptr::read)`.这是可以忽略的。

循环序幕是使用指针感应变量与指数感应变量的变体之间的主要区别。它们都适当地矢量和展开，并且具有相同的热循环

messages.en: An actual intrinsic might make sense if LLVM has some specific construct or intrinsic that we'd like to emit from rustc instead of open-coding the operation and hoping LLVM recognizes it. There is [`llvm.experimental.memset.pattern`](https://llvm.org/docs/LangRef.html#llvm-experimental-memset-pattern-intrinsic) but I think it's target-dependent whether it's a good idea (at least some LLVM passes check target info to decide whether to introduce calls to it). It's also limited to short repeating patterns up to 16 bytes, and we shouldn't add an intrinsic to rustc that has to emit very complicated LLVM IR for some types `T`, so if we add an intrinsic it should probably be limited to 16 byte patterns and everything else stays library code.
messages.zh: 实际的内在可能是有意义的，如果LLVM有一些特定的结构或内在的，我们希望从rustc发出，而不是开放编码的操作，并希望LLVM识别它。有[`llvm.experimental.memset.pattern`](https://llvm.org/docs/LangRef.html#llvm-experimental-memset-pattern-intrinsic)但我认为这是否是一个好主意取决于目标（至少一些LLVM通过检查目标信息来决定是否引入调用）。它也仅限于最多16个字节的短重复模式，对于某些类型，我们不应该为必须发射非常复杂的LLVM IR的rustc添加固有的`T`，因此，如果我们添加一个内部函数，它可能应该限制为16个字节模式，其他所有内容都将保留库代码。

messages.en: that changes depending on autovectorization. i've observed that when pointer induction is used (start ptr and end ptr), llvm just calculates the trip count by subtracting the pointers, leaving 3 values that are alive. for fallibly iterative fills (`<[T]>::fill where T: Clone`), pointer induction might be the better choice as it might not be vectorized, but for the constraints of `splat` (which is strictly bitwise copying), i think it's better to lean on the pointer + index variation.
messages.zh: 这取决于自动矢量化。我观察到，当使用指针感应（ start ptr和end ptr ）时， llvm只是通过减去指针来计算行程计数，留下3个有效的值。对于易出错的迭代填充（`<[T]>::fill where T: Clone`） ，指针归纳可能是更好的选择，因为它可能不会被矢量化，但对于`splat`（严格按位复制） ，我认为最好依靠指针+索引变化。

messages.en: Yeah the pointer pair approach needs more work to compute the length, e.g., for checking if the unrolled (including, but not limited to, vectorized) loop can be entered and when it can be left. But usually that is a short-lived temporary, not another value live across the entire loop, so it doesn't necessarily increase register pressure
messages.zh: 是的，指针对方法需要更多的工作来计算长度，例如，用于检查是否可以输入展开（包括但不限于矢量化）循环以及何时可以离开。但通常这是一个短暂的临时值，而不是整个循环中的另一个值，因此不一定会增加寄存器压力

messages.en: Of course that's the idealized setting, in reality LLVM does silly things all the time, but I don't think the silliness in these cases is predictable enough to make bikeshedding and extensive experiments useful. If a real application spends enough time in splat loops that it's worth worrying about, then either the loops run enough that any spills in surrounding code are a good trade-off, or it's a lot of tiny splats, in which case it's more important to look at everything else other than the loop.
messages.zh: 当然，这是理想化的设置，实际上LLVM一直在做愚蠢的事情，但我不认为这些情况下的愚蠢是可预测的，足以使自行车脱落和广泛的实验有用。如果一个真正的应用程序在splat循环中花费了足够的时间，值得关注，那么循环要么运行得足够多，以至于周围代码中的任何溢出都是一个很好的权衡，要么就是很多微小的splat ，在这种情况下，更重要的是查看循环之外的其他所有内容。

messages.en: (Also, in the latter case the splat code really ought to be inlined and not in its own function, in which case any experiments on the splat operation in isolation are unlikely to be representative.)

messages.en: i see. then i'll drop the register pressure/code size claims as the motivating evidence, and focus more on the code duplication part. currently, my PR cannot reuse the `<[T]>::fill` primitive as that requires a safe `&mut [T]` and in `Vec::<T>::extend_with` specialized for `T: TrivialClone` i'm operating over the uninitialized part of a vector. could that serve as a motivating use case to pursue `splat`, implementing both `<[T]>::fill` and `Vec::extend_with` in terms of it?

topics.name: hashbrown/backtrace subtrees
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：`hashbrown` 因依赖 `alloc`/`core` 内部实现，无法作为普通 Cargo 依赖直接用于 `std` 构建；讨论了使用 git submodule、git subtree，或将代码直接纳入 `rust-lang/rust` 的方案。`backtrace` 也存在类似的仓库与 `std` 集成问题。
- **`hashbrown` 方案**：最终倾向于仿照 `stdarch`，将 `hashbrown` 放在 `library` 下作为子目录，并通过 `#[path]` 以模块方式包含，而不是作为 Cargo 依赖。Trevor Gross 认为对大型仓库使用实际的 `git subtree` 不可行；相关实现可先在 subtree 分支上测试，再单独提交 PR。
- **`backtrace` 方向**：多数参与者支持取消 `backtrace` submodule，将其开发完全移入 `rust-lang/rust`，甚至归档原 `backtrace-rs` 仓库；这样可以统一处理方式、改善 in-tree 开发和 CI 协调，并减少 `libc → std → backtrace` 的同步延迟。
- **已达成的条件与迁移安排**：迁移后仍需支持按需发布 crates.io 版本，不能绑定到 Rust 发布周期；等待已获批准的 PR 进入队列被认为可以满足“随时发布”。计划保留现有 issue，在切换前处理完现有 PR，之后将新 issue/PR 导向 `rust-lang/rust`，并在 README、可能的 Rust 博客文章及 crate 仓库链接中明确迁移。
- **仍未解决的问题**：`backtrace` 完全移入主仓库后的发布、CI 和测试负担仍需具体落实；从 `rust-lang/rust` 发布 crate 不能与仓库内依赖新版本原子完成，虽然目前实际需要这种同步的主要是 `ui_test`。此外，`backtrace` 当前 CI 经常因目标平台、工具链或测试环境变化而损坏，如何在迁移后维持或改善覆盖率仍有讨论。

Two thoughts on this:
- If we do this, we should put a big fat warning into backtrace's README that the crate just moved places (and ideally also post a Rust blog post about it in advance), otherwise people might be worried that the crate stops being maintained when its repo got archived (we should also repoint the repo of the crate to `rust-lang/rust`, ofc)
- I remembered now what was one of the issues with having crates.io crates published from `rust-lang/rust`. You can't atomically publish a new release and depend on that version in-tree. So either bumping the version and depending on it needs a PR -> merge -> PR -> merge cycle, or library (and everything in-tree that wants to have `backtrace` atomic updates) would have to depend on backtrace via `path = "..."`.
messages.zh:

- 我现在想起了从 `rust-lang/rust` 发布 crates.io crate 的一个问题：不能原子地发布新版本并让仓库里的代码依赖该版本。因此，提升版本号并更新依赖需要经过 PR -> 合并 -> PR -> 合并 的流程；或者 library（以及仓库中所有希望与 `backtrace` 原子更新的部分）必须通过 `path = "..."` 依赖 backtrace。

Hello! Just wanted to ask about `hashbrown` side of this topic.
From the conversation it looks like it shouldn't be a submodule. @**Clar Fon** expressed support for it being a subtree [here](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/164852#issuecomment-6384366735). topics.name: Miri vs tests in std
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：当前 `rust-lang/rust` CI 只运行部分 `std` 测试，且测试中零散使用 `cfg(miri)`/`cfg(not(miri))`，导致 Miri 难以准确发现哪些 `std` API 缺少 shim；不同平台覆盖范围也不一致：Linux 排除 `fs::`、`net::`、`process::`、`sys::`，macOS/Windows 仅运行 `time::`、`sync::`、`thread::`、`env::` 的部分测试。
- **主要区分**：因 Miri 运行过慢而缩小循环或跳过的测试可以长期保留；因缺少 shim（如 `unlinkat`、Unix domain socket 等）而跳过的测试则应视为 Miri 的待支持事项，不应被普通 `cfg(miri)` 隐藏。随机添加 `cfg(not(miri))` 还会掩盖本来可以在 Miri 中运行的测试。
- **讨论中的方案**：一是减少甚至取消 `rust-lang/rust` CI 中的 `std` Miri 测试，仅保留 `core`/`alloc` 或少数稳定模块，同时由 `miri-test-libstd` 负责更广泛测试；二是引入独立于 `cfg(miri)` 的 cfg（讨论过 `miritest`、`skip_unsupported_miri_shims` 等名称），只在需要避免缺少 shim 的默认 CI 配置中跳过测试，而让其他 Miri 测试暴露失败。也有人建议使用带理由的 `ignore`、tidy 检查或外部 skip list。
- **阶段性结论/进展**：倾向于使用单独的 cfg 来区分“缺少 shim”和“过慢”，并在 `std-dev-guide` 中记录规则；`cfg(miri)` 应主要用于全局排除或调整过慢的测试。相关 PR 已将部分原先基于 `--skip` 的模块级排除改为更细粒度的 cfg，TCP 测试已重新启用，UDP 支持预计完善后再启用。
- **仍未解决的问题**：尚未最终确定独立 cfg 的名称、启用位置及完整基础设施；`std` doctest 如何按需跳过仍有实现问题，但 RalfJ 认为可以跳过这些 doctest（它们仍会在 `miri-test-libstd` 中运行）。另外，如何在不增加维护负担的情况下保持 `rust-lang/rust` CI 的 Miri 失败信号，以及如何确保新增 compiler 特性暴露到 `std` 时得到 libs/Miri 方面的审查，仍需进一步明确。

messages.en:
The current situation around Miri and tests in std is not great. Tests randomly get `cfg`d away under `miri`, but not consistently so, making it quite hard for me to track which features miri is missing. Some subset of std tests gets executed in miri by CI, but apart from me probably nobody knows which subset. And even if they do, it becomes unclear what to do with a test failure.

The status quo is that we run the following std tests in Miri under CI:
- on Linux: everything except for `fs::`, `net::`, `process::`, `sys::`
- on macOS and Windows: only the parts in `time::`, `sync::`, `thread::`, `env::`

If possible, I'd like to avoid `cfg`d tests in std as it becomes hard to keep track of them. (I mean tests that are disabled for "miri does not have the shim" reasons. tests that are disabled because Miri is too slow are entirely fine.) But obviously new features shouldnt be blocked on Miri support. So it would probably be better to reduce the test coverage so that CI still allows new features to land.
I can imagine two variants of that:
- We reduce std test coverage to just `time::`, `sync::`, `thread::`, `env::` in general. new things seem rare there.
- We entirely remove std testing from CI, only keeping alloc and core. Those extremely rarely need Miri patches and when they do (new intrinsics) it's probably good to get a Miri implementation early to help figure out the spec.

Either way, miri-test-libstd will still run all the tests CI currently runs. And the miri test suite runs in CI so for existing features that miri covers, we'd notice when they stop working.

Thoughts, ideas?
Cc @**The 8472|330154**, @*T-miri*  as we just ran into this with the fd-views PR.
messages.zh:
Miri周围的现状和STD中的测试不太好。测试随机获取`cfg`d离开以下`miri`，但并非始终如一，因此我很难跟踪miri缺少哪些功能。 一些std测试的子集由CI在miri中执行，但除了我之外，可能没有人知道哪个子集。 即使他们这样做了，也不清楚如何处理测试失败。

现状是，我们在CI下在MIRI中运行以下STD测试：
-在Linux上：除了`fs::`, `net::`, `process::`, `sys::`-在macOS和Windows上：仅`time::`, `sync::`, `thread::`, `env::`如果可能的话，我想避免`cfg`在STD中进行测试，因为很难跟踪它们。 （我的意思是由于“miri没有垫片”原因而被禁用的测试。由于Miri太慢而被禁用的测试完全没有问题。） 但显然， Miri支持不应阻止新功能。 因此，减少测试覆盖范围可能更好，以便CI仍然允许新功能登陆。
我可以想象有两种变体：
-我们将性病测试的覆盖范围缩小到`time::`, `sync::`, `thread::`, `env::`一般来说，那里的新事物似乎很少见。
-我们从CI中完全移除STD测试，只保留ALLOC和CORE。 那些极少需要Miri补丁的人，当他们这样做（新的内在因素）时，尽早获得Miri实现以帮助找出规格可能是件好事。

无论哪种方式， miri-test-libstd仍将运行当前运行的所有测试。Miri测试套件在CI中运行，因此对于miri覆盖的现有功能，我们会注意到它们何时停止工作。

想法，想法？
Cc @ * * The 8472 | 330154 * *, @ * T-miri * ，因为我们刚刚在fd-views PR中遇到了这个问题。

messages.en:
I'm not familiar with std-specific issues here, but instead of writing `#[cfg]`s you can write conditional ignores:
```rust
#[test]
#[cfg_attr(miri, ignore = "slow-under-miri")]
fn foo() {
```
The advantages of this are:
* the reason is attached to the test in the syntax tree, not just a commenting convention, so it is preserved under reformatting and refactoring
* the test harness output reports that ignored tests exist, so it isn’t a silent lack of coverage
* the current number of each kind of ignored tests can be measured by examining the test harness output
* if desired, the test can be run despite the `ignore`, without changing the source code
* it's not the same thing as an `allow(reason = ...)` but it's close, and thus more familiar
messages.zh:
我不熟悉这里的性病特定问题，但不是写`#[cfg]`您可以编写条件忽略：```rust
#[test]
#[cfg_attr(miri, ignore = "slow-under-miri")]
fn foo() {
```这样做的好处是：
*原因附加到语法树中的测试，而不仅仅是注释约定，因此它在重新格式化和重构下保留
*测试线束输出报告存在被忽略的测试，因此它不是无声的缺乏覆盖
*可以通过检查测试线束输出来测量每种被忽略测试的当前数量
*如果需要，可以运行测试，尽管`ignore`，无需更改源代码
*它与`allow(reason = ...)`但它很近，因此更熟悉

messages.en: It would be kinda nice to allow multiple ignores to make that more ergonomic (https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2024&gist=f29ed884b58400e0f8fe277282a7a293)... and it runs into some issues with doc tests. But I like the ignore pattern too.

so far two options came up for resolving this:
- running fewer / no std tests in miri so that people dont have to add as many cfg (and make it more consistent so its easier to document & remember where cfg is needed)
- add a separate cfg for these tests so its easier to track separately and so it doesnt interfere with miri-test-libstd. cfg(miri) would only be used for tests that we want to exclude everywhere, e.g. as they are just too slow.

目前有两种解决思路：
- 减少或停止在 Miri 下运行 std 测试，这样人们就不必添加那么多 cfg（同时让规则更一致，便于记录和记住哪里需要 cfg）。

topics.name: Capping float strings to a sane value
topics.name_zh: Capping float strings to a sane value
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：浮点字符串解析（`dec2flt`）在输入长度极端大时会触发一些小 bug；需要在“略微减慢数学计算”与“限制输入长度”之间取舍。截断输入并不总是正确，因为很深处的非零数字可能影响舍入结果，尤其是恰好处于 halfway 的情况。
- **主要方案**：PR #165163 提议对可解析的字符串长度设置上限，默认上限为 `1 << 50`（约 1 PB），超出则返回错误。该方案保留正常输入的快速路径，避免为极端输入维护更复杂或更慢的算法；已有观点认为 `dec2flt` 即使只保留足够计算舍入的数字，也仍可能在极端十进制位数相关计算中溢出。
- **关于上限大小的讨论**：有人倾向更小的 `2^16`、`2^32`、`i32::MAX` 或 `i32::MAX >> 1`；支持较大上限的一方认为 `2^50` 基本属于“除非主动制造，否则现实中不可触及”的边界，能减少合法用户输入因限制而失败的可能。代码据 PR 作者称可正确处理到 `2^58`，因此 `2^50` 也被视为留有算法调整余量。
- **重要兼容性考量**：过去曾存在更小、实际可触及的浮点解析限制，后来被修复；很多代码默认“通过浮点词法检查后，`std` 就能解析”，而输入可能来自不可信用户，因此过小的新增限制可能导致 `parse::<f64>().expect(...)` 因合法词法输入而 panic。也有人建议明确记录限制并提供专用错误变体，但这可能带来兼容性和使用预期问题。
- **当前状态与未决事项**：讨论中没有人明确反对采用长度上限，整体对 PR 的方向较认可；但具体应采用 `2^50` 还是更小的 `i32` 级别上限，以及是否需要文档说明或专用错误变体，仍未形成明确结论。

messages.en:
Technically user-facing but pretty impossibly so, anyone have an objection to https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/165163?

Quick summary is we have to pick between slightly slower math and an input length cap to fix some small bugs. I suggested the latter, this PR caps max string length at 1<<50 (~1PB) and errors beyond that.
messages.zh:
严格来说这会影响用户，不过实际遇到的可能性几乎为零。有人反对 https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/165163 吗？

简要来说，为了修复一些小问题，我们必须在稍慢的数学运算与输入长度上限之间做选择。我建议后者，这个 PR 将字符串最大长度限制为 1<<50（约 1PB），超出就报错。

messages.en: You can still safely parse all known digits of pi to an `f16` if desired https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chronology_of_computation_of_pi#2009%E2%80%93present
messages.zh: 如果愿意，你仍然可以安全地把所有已知的圆周率数字解析成一个 `f16`：https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chronology_of_computation_of_pi#2009%E2%80%93present

messages.en: Note that 2^50 bytes is larger than would fit in the memory of an x86-64 machine at the time of Rust going 1.0
messages.zh: 注意，在 Rust 1.0 发布的时候，2^50 字节比一台 x86-64 机器能容纳的内存还大。

messages.en: Clearly we need to test this with `Zettalinux`, mapping a small data center as part of the address space
messages.zh: 显然我们得用 `Zettalinux` 测试一下，把一个小型数据中心映射成地址空间的一部分。

messages.en: I guess it's actually smaller than that, apparently you can store 1PB in just ~10 drives https://nimbusdata.com/products/exadrive/. That's actually pretty crazy
messages.zh: 我猜实际上用不了那么大规模：显然只需大约十块硬盘就能存下 1PB，https://nimbusdata.com/products/exadrive/。这还真挺惊人的。

messages.en: Presumably you would still have difficulties slotting that much RAM, but you simply could not use the addresses needed to read the entire string.
messages.zh: 想必把那么多内存插进机器仍然困难，不过关键在于，你根本无法使用读取整个字符串所需的地址。

messages.en: I think `mmap` can actually handle reading files way larger than ram without too much overhead
messages.zh: 我觉得 `mmap` 实际上能以不太大的开销读取远大于内存的文件。

messages.en: right, that's why I mentioned the CPU limits.
messages.zh: 对，所以我才提到 CPU 的限制。

messages.en: because the CPU would simply reject the attempt to use the addresses necessary.
messages.zh: 因为 CPU 会直接拒绝访问所需的那些地址。

messages.en: the requirement that `str` is a contiguous string of bytes is not something that `mmap` would change, so you would have to start with a very, very low address indeed. fortunately, the alignment requirement is trivial, at least.
messages.zh: `str` 必须是连续字节串，这一点不会因为 `mmap` 而改变，所以你确实必须从非常非常低的地址开始。好在至少对齐要求很简单。

messages.en: it would be a... while... before you got to the last byte.
messages.zh: 等你读到最后一个字节，恐怕得花……好一阵子。

messages.en: hm.
messages.zh: 嗯。

messages.en: you can get 2^50 bytes of `b'0'` if you e.g. make a 1GiB memfd and then mmap it 2^20 times, if you're on one of those 5-level paging x86 cpus it should be possible -- you don't even need more than a few GiB of ram.
messages.zh: 例如，创建一个 1GiB 的 memfd，再将它 mmap 2^20 次，就能得到 2^50 字节的 `b'0'`。如果使用支持五级页表的 x86 CPU，应该能做到，甚至只需要几 GiB 内存。

messages.en: if you can read at 50GiB/s sustained, that comes out to 5.8 hours
messages.zh: 如果能持续以 50GiB/s 读取，大约需要 5.8 小时。

messages.en: I think Jubilee's original point was that "at the time of Rust going 1.0" there were no x86-64 CPUs with five-level paging (it was introduced in Ice Lake, which launched in 2019)
messages.zh: 我觉得 Jubilee 原本的意思是，“Rust 1.0 发布时”还没有支持五级页表的 x86-64 CPU（这是 2019 年发布的 Ice Lake 才引入的）。

messages.en: yeah, I got that, I'm just pointing out a 2^50 byte string can be achieved with reasonable space and time
messages.zh: 对，我明白。我只是指出，用合理的空间和时间就可以构造一个 2^50 字节的字符串。

messages.en: For some value of “reasonable”
messages.zh: 这得看怎么定义“合理”。

messages.en: Anyway, regarding the original question, I have no objections to this limit. If a program can be convinced to accept or create a petabyte-sized slice, then that program have worse problems than not being able to parse a float out of it.
messages.zh: 总之，回到最初的问题，我不反对这个限制。如果一个程序能被诱导接收或创建 PB 大小的切片，那它的问题可比无法从中解析浮点数严重得多。

messages.en: What even is the current behavior for such strings?
messages.zh: 目前对这样的字符串究竟会有什么行为？

messages.en: fun fact: I say this as the person responsible for std’s float parsing having a [much smaller, actually possible-to-hit limit](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/31407) from 2016 to 2021. While I'm glad that issue was fixed, we didn't get too many people hitting it in practice, so I guess even that limit was mostly fine in practice. It turns out programs mostly don’t parse floats that have very excessive precision :woman_shrugging:
messages.zh: 有趣的是，我正是让 std 的浮点解析在 2016 到 2021 年间存在一个[小得多、实际可能触及的限制](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/31407)的人。虽然我很高兴那个问题修好了，但实际遇到它的人并不多，所以我猜那个限制在实践中也基本没问题。事实证明，程序大多不会解析精度极其夸张的浮点数 :woman_shrugging:

messages.en: And I guess truncating doesn't work either because one can somehow construct cases where some arbitrarily deep digit matters?
messages.zh: 我猜也不能简单截断，因为总能构造某种情况，让任意靠后的一位数字都影响结果？

messages.en: e.g. `1.0000000000000001110223024625156540423631668090820312500...001` rounds up, but if the last digit is zero it's exactly half way so rounds to `1.0`
that's `1.0 + 2.0f64.powf(-53.0)` plus the one at the end
messages.zh: 它就是 `1.0 + 2.0f64.powf(-53.0)` 再加上末尾那个 1。

messages.en: Note that these kinds of inputs can be handled correctly by looking at all input digits but only actually parsing/calculating with enough digits to determine the right result modulo such half-way cases, and remembering whether you truncated non-zero trailing digits (which means it's not a halfway case). However, that's already what the dec2flt slow path is doing. The problem is that even the truncated representation still requires some calculations in units of "number of decimal digits" (i.e., log10 scale) and those calculations can still overflow if the input is excessive enough, unless you go out of your way to use otherwise excessive precision and/or complicate the logic. Making sure you caught all such problems and handle them correctly is a huge hassle, for no real world benefit.
messages.zh: 注意，可以检查所有输入数字，但实际上只解析和计算足够确定正确结果的位数，并记住被截去的尾数是否包含非零数字，从而正确处理这类输入；若尾部存在非零数字，就不是恰好中点的情况。不过 dec2flt 的慢速路径本来就是这么做的。问题在于，即使截断后的表示仍然需要按“十进制位数”（即 log10 尺度）进行一些计算；如果输入足够夸张，这些计算仍可能溢出，除非特意使用本来用不着的高精度，或使逻辑更复杂。确保找出并正确处理所有这类问题非常麻烦，却没有实际收益。

messages.en: :clar_fon: is there a reason why 2^50 is chosen? I feel like we could offer substantially less than that without any issues
messages.zh: :clar_fon: 为什么选 2^50？我感觉可以把限制设得低很多，也不会出问题。

messages.en: I think 2^32 would be fine, but even parsing 2^16 feels like "what are you doing here?"
messages.zh: 我觉得 2^32 就够了，甚至解析 2^16 都让人想问“你到底在干什么？”

messages.en: the largest parsable float string length up to equivalence should be a computable thing but it seems annoying to compute
messages.zh: 按等价性归类后，可解析浮点字符串的最大长度应该是可计算的，但算起来似乎很麻烦。

messages.en: in the other direction, we do limit width and precision to `u16` in format strings
messages.zh: 反过来看，我们确实把格式字符串中的宽度和精度限制在 `u16` 范围内。

messages.en: I’d be up for a much smaller limit if it buys us something tangible (like the fmt limits did), but otherwise it’s nice if the limit is so large that if someone(‘s overeager LLM) reports it as a bug, we don’t have to think twice about closing as WONTFIX and can have a sensible chuckle about it
messages.zh: 如果更小的上限能带来具体收益（就像 fmt 的限制那样），我会支持。否则，把上限设得大到即使有人（或者他过于积极的 LLM）将它报告为 bug，我们也可以毫不犹豫地以 WONTFIX 关闭，并合理地笑一笑，也挺好。

messages.en: 2^32 is "only" 4GB and while that's extreme for a single input, things do routinely use that much memory (total). 2^50 is so far out of the realm of possibility that it's effectively "dont explicitly try to break this" rather than any sort of "real" implementation limit.
messages.zh: 2^32 “只有”4GB，虽然单个输入达到这个大小很夸张，但程序总内存使用达到这个量很常见。2^50 则远离现实可能性，实际上表达的是“别刻意尝试把它搞坏”，而非真正的实现限制。

messages.en:
@_**Trevor Gross|532317** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Capping.20float.20strings.20to.20a.20sane.20value/near/636176424):
```quote
Quick summary is we have to pick between slightly slower math and an input length cap to fix some small bugs.
```

We could also choose the former but split into a `#[cold]` path, so we still do the fast thing for "reasonable" inputs
messages.zh:
@_**Trevor Gross|532317** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Capping.20float.20strings.20to.20a.20sane.20value/near/636176424):
```quote
简要来说，为了修复一些小问题，我们必须在稍慢的数学运算与输入长度上限之间做选择。
```

也可以选择前者，但拆出一条 `#[cold]` 路径，这样“合理”的输入仍走快速路径。

messages.en: I personally would rather just explicitly document it and tell people to read, even though I know people hate reading
messages.zh: 我个人更愿意明确写进文档，然后告诉大家去读，尽管我知道大家不喜欢读文档。

messages.en:
@_**Josh Stone (cuviper)|138448** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Capping.20float.20strings.20to.20a.20sane.20value/near/636368498):
```quote
We could also choose the former but split into a `#[cold]` path, so we still do the fast thing for "reasonable" inputs
```

If by that you mean implementing and maintaining a separate code path and having it add to binary size, I don't think that's worth it for something as silly as "you did enough mmap crimes to pass a 2^50 byte slice to dec2flt".
messages.zh:
@_**Josh Stone (cuviper)|138448** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Capping.20float.20strings.20to.20a.20sane.20value/near/636368498):
```quote
也可以选择前者，但拆出一条 `#[cold]` 路径，这样“合理”的输入仍走快速路径。
```

如果你的意思是实现并维护一条独立代码路径，还增加二进制体积，我觉得为“你干了太多 mmap 坏事，把一个 2^50 字节的切片传给 dec2flt”这么荒唐的情况付出这些代价并不值得。

messages.en: fair
messages.zh: 有道理。

messages.en: yeah, I would much rather just limit to 2^16 and tell people they should read the docs which say this limit exists
messages.zh: 是啊，我更愿意直接限制在 2^16，并告诉大家去读说明了这个限制的文档。

messages.en: we could even add a dedicated error variant for it. plenty of bits to add more of those
messages.zh: 甚至可以为它添加专门的错误变体，还有足够多的位可以添加更多变体。

messages.en: generally if your float literal is more than 65k you have done something horribly wrong and we are demonstrating mercy by choosing to stop you there
messages.zh: 通常，如果你的浮点字面量超过 65k，就说明你做了非常离谱的事；我们选择在这里阻止你，已经算手下留情了。

messages.en: btw, did we document the fmt `u16` limit anywhere? the [syntax](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fmt/index.html#syntax) section only says the integers must fit in `usize`
messages.zh: 顺便问一下，我们在哪儿记录过 fmt 的 `u16` 限制吗？[语法](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fmt/index.html#syntax)一节只说整数必须能放进 `usize`。

messages.en: If you make the limit 2^16, someone's eventually going to find a way to induce a panic in an application that does `input.parse::<f64>().expect("should be valid because the regex matched")` and they're going to file an issue about it and I will sigh and concede that they technically have a point and we should consider fixing it (at least if it's as simple as raising a hard-coded limit somewhere, rather than significantly complicating the code and making it slower).
messages.zh: 如果把上限设成 2^16，总会有人找到办法，让一个使用 `input.parse::<f64>().expect("should be valid because the regex matched")` 的应用发生 panic，然后提交 issue。我就会叹口气，承认从严格意义上说他们有道理，我们应该考虑修复（至少如果只需调高某个硬编码限制，而无需显著增加代码复杂性、降低速度）。

messages.en: there isn't a limit atm, the proposal is to add one
messages.zh: 目前没有限制，这个提议才是要添加一个。

messages.en: There's a limit for parts of the placeholders in `fmt::Arguments`
messages.zh: `fmt::Arguments` 占位符的部分内容有上限。

messages.en: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/136932
messages.zh: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/136932

messages.en: the proposal would be to redefine the spec: we parse float literals under 2^16-1 bytes long, and if it's over that we throw a dedicated limit error variant. if someone runs into that limit their only defence is not reading the docs imo
messages.zh: 这个提议可以重新定义规范：我们解析长度少于 2^16-1 字节的浮点字面量，超过则返回专门的长度限制错误变体。如果有人遇到这个限制，我觉得只能说他没读文档。

messages.en: not even f128 can hold that many digits. not even close
messages.zh: 连 f128 都放不下那么多位数字，差得远。

messages.en: We never documented such a limit in the past 11 years, and from past experience/bug reports, quite a lot of code assumes that "if I checked that it conforms to the lexical syntax of floats, std will be able to parse it". Nobody's very *likely* to hit it, but the strings being parsed are often user inputs, so this does sometimes leads to "panic reachable from untrusted inputs"
messages.zh: 过去十一年我们从未在文档中写过这样的限制。根据以往经验和错误报告，相当多的代码假设“只要检查它符合浮点数的词法语法，std 就能解析”。人们通常不太可能碰到上限，但待解析字符串往往来自用户输入，因此有时会导致“不可信输入可以触发 panic”。

messages.en: Even the rust compiler used to ICE if a valid float literal in the source code couldn't be parsed by `FromStr` (not sure if this was ever fixed properly or the ICEs just got fixed by improving the dec2flt code)
messages.zh: 就连 Rust 编译器以前也会因为源码中合法的浮点字面量无法被 `FromStr` 解析而 ICE（不确定后来是否彻底修复，还是仅仅改进 dec2flt 代码后那些 ICE 就消失了）。

messages.en: Again, I could see the case for a lower limit than the proposed 2^50 if it actually bought us anything (like how the limit for fmt width and precision made `fmt::Arguments` encoding smaller and simpler). But as far as I know there's no problem with supporting the proposed 2^50 limit, making it lower just seems to increase the odds that the limit can actually be hit in the real world.
messages.zh: 再说一次，如果比提议的 2^50 更低的限制确实能带来收益，我能理解这样做的理由（例如 fmt 宽度和精度限制让 `fmt::Arguments` 编码更小、更简单）。但据我所知，支持提议的 2^50 上限并没有问题；进一步降低它，只会增加现实中真的触及限制的概率。

messages.en: fair, I guess my main concern is wasting that much time parsing a float literal that will probably fail anyway. but of course, being 65kB is much more reasonable than 2^50 B
messages.zh: 有道理。我想我主要担心的是，花那么多时间解析一个很可能最终仍会失败的浮点字面量。不过当然，65kB 比 2^50 B 现实得多。

messages.en: If someone's concerned by that, they can impose a limit that makes sense for their application, and they should probably impose it before they even get the point of parsing individual floats.
messages.zh: 如果有人担心这个，可以自行施加适合其应用的限制，而且大概应该在开始解析单个浮点数之前就限制好。

messages.en: also fair
messages.zh: 这也有道理。

messages.en: I guess my preference would be maybe `f64::MAX_EXACT_INTEGER` which is like 2^54 and somewhat less arbitrary, but, it's also still arbitrary, so
messages.zh: 我可能更偏向 `f64::MAX_EXACT_INTEGER`，大约是 2^54，看起来没那么随意。不过它终究也还是随意选的。

messages.en: That seems equally or more arbitrary to me because it's a float-related integer of roughly the right magnitude, but it doesn't actually have anything to do with the reasons why we're imposing a limit. Basically numerology.
messages.zh: 我觉得它同样随意，甚至更随意：它只是一个与浮点数有关、数量级大致合适的整数，却与我们设置限制的原因毫无关系。基本上就是数字玄学。

messages.en: yes
messages.zh: 是的。

messages.en: it's an arbitrary decision regardless
messages.zh: 无论如何，这都是个任意的决定。

messages.en: Might as well pick an actually arbitrary number instead of one that might mislead by seeming less arbitrary
messages.zh: 与其选一个看起来没那么随意、可能误导人的数字，不如直接选个确实任意的数字。

messages.en: To me, I think limiting the floats we parse to `u32::MAX` or `i32::MAX` bytes seems fine. I suspect, as @**Hanna Kruppe** suggested, that `u16::MAX` will be reasonably hittable by some strange person using a theorem prover of some kind.
