messages.en: Anyway, the longest output you'll get with the `Display` impl (without requesting extra padding/precision) if it existed should be a little less than 5k decimal digits (smallest positive subnormal is ca. 10^-4966), which isn't great but also not "galactic time"
messages.zh: 总之，如果存在 `Display` 实现，在不额外要求填充或精度的情况下，最长输出应该略少于五千位十进制数字（最小正次正规数大约为 10^-4966）。这虽然不短，但也不至于要花“银河系尺度的时间”。

messages.en: yes I was only wondering about whether we had veered into galactic time for `2^50`
messages.zh: 是的，我只是好奇 `2^50` 是否已经进入银河系时间尺度。

messages.en: Regarding the specific limit: the code is correct for lengths up to 2^58, per the PR author, so giving us a small margin under there to fiddle with the algorithm seems reasonable. I don't think there are any significant benefits between there and a limit that fits into an i32, which would mostly help 32-bit platforms parsing to an `f32`. But as mentioned, that would bring us down to limits of what your allocator can happily create
messages.zh: 关于具体上限：按照 PR 作者的说法，代码对于最高 2^58 的长度都是正确的，因此在它以下留一点余量方便调整算法很合理。我觉得再降到能放进 i32 的限制之前，不会有什么显著收益；i32 限制主要有利于 32 位平台解析 `f32`。不过正如之前提到的，这就降到了分配器完全可以正常分配的范围。

messages.en: $$2^{48} - 1$$ or $$2^{56} - 1)$$ would probably also be reasonable, since they give us a power of 2 unused top bits (not a useful property here, just a round number)
messages.zh: $$2^{48} - 1$$ 或 $$2^{56} - 1)$$ 可能也合理，因为这样空出的高位数量是 2 的幂（这个性质在这里没什么用，只是看起来比较整齐）。

messages.en: I'd suggest $$2^{48} - 1$$ except it can't fit all the digits of pi known today :slight_smile:
messages.zh: 我本来想建议 $$2^{48} - 1$$，但它连目前已知的圆周率所有位数都装不下 :slight_smile:

messages.en:
@_**Trevor Gross|532317** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Capping.20float.20strings.20to.20a.20sane.20value/near/636419108):
```quote
which would mostly help 32-bit platforms parsing to an `f32`.
```

well we're inherently limited to `isize::MAX` anyway
messages.zh:
@_**Trevor Gross|532317** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Capping.20float.20strings.20to.20a.20sane.20value/near/636419108):
```quote
这主要有利于 32 位平台解析 `f32`。
```

反正我们本来就受 `isize::MAX` 限制。

messages.en: I think we'd need a few spare bits beyond that still, but I guess I haven't analyzed much
messages.zh: 我觉得在此之外仍需留几个额外位，不过我还没仔细分析。

messages.en:
I rather like the `i32::MAX` limit, I think.  A `str` can't be bigger than that on 32-bit anyway, so it's even (kinda) a portability "fix".

And it gives me the same kind of vibe as "look, over a billion variants in an enum isn't a real scenario" that also uses 32-bit-ish restrictions.
messages.zh:
我觉得我挺喜欢 `i32::MAX` 这个上限。毕竟在 32 位平台上，`str` 本来就不能超过它，所以这甚至算某种可移植性“修复”。

而且它给我的感觉类似于“枚举超过十亿个变体不是真实场景”，后者也采用了接近 32 位的限制。

messages.en: yes, it has the desirable quality that it's well beyond what you should be doing and have any realistic need for.
messages.zh: 是的，它有一个很好的特点：远远超过你应当做的事情以及任何现实需求。

messages.en: 65535 is like, a number you can easily memorize.
messages.zh: 65535 是个很容易记住的数字。

messages.en: It's a number people know.
messages.zh: 大家都知道这个数字。

messages.en: which means that it's also kinda "ehn" as a limit, I'd be happy with it but as stated it could possibly be reached by someone doing really hardcore math, whereas `2_147_483_647` is like...
messages.zh: 所以把它作为上限也有点“嗯……”：我能接受，但如前所述，做极端数学计算的人确实可能碰到它；而 `2_147_483_647` 就是……

messages.en: ...I do not.
messages.zh: ……我记不住。

messages.en: I cannot remember it. I keep mentally rounding it to "2 billion, right?"
messages.zh: 我记不住它，脑子里总会四舍五入成“大概二十亿，对吧？”

messages.en:
I *could* memorize it but I only would because I'm a weirdo who has enjoyed committing a few too many digits of pi to permanent long-term memory.

whereas I knew about the "magic" of 65536 well before I ever touched programming in earnest.
messages.zh:
我当然可以背下来，但那只是因为我是个喜欢把太多位圆周率永久记进长期记忆的怪人。

而早在真正接触编程之前，我就已经知道 65536 的“魔力”了。

messages.en: If you're fine with a limit around there, what about `i32::MAX >> 1`? Which would allow us to actually use `i32` for the math (needs to be able to do an addition without overflow)
messages.zh: 如果你能接受这个数量级的限制，那么 `i32::MAX >> 1` 怎么样？这样就能真正使用 `i32` 进行计算（需要保证一次加法不溢出）。

messages.en: 1 billion digits is still more than people need so sure.
messages.zh: 十亿位数字仍然超过人们的需要，所以可以。

messages.en: though can't we do the math on u32?
messages.zh: 不过不能用 u32 做运算吗？

messages.en: or is it signed math.
messages.zh: 还是说这是有符号运算？

messages.en: Yeah it's signed, e.g. need to add the exponent to the number of zeros after `.`
messages.zh: 对，是有符号的，例如需要把指数加到 `.` 后零的数量上。

messages.en: *nods* yeah I was thinking "hmm wait of course it's signed, it's a float"
messages.zh: *点头* 是啊，我刚也在想：“嗯，等等，这当然是有符号的，因为这是浮点数。”

messages.en: and yeah, the exponent.
messages.zh: 对，还有指数。

messages.en: interestingly, this is also the amount that you can store into a Postgres TEXT column, per row, before it is forced to use a fully-out-of-line representation.
messages.zh: 有意思的是，在 Postgres 每行的 TEXT 列中，这也是强制改用完全行外存储表示之前所能存储的数据量。

messages.en: toasted floats!
messages.zh: TOAST 过的浮点数！

messages.en: Or huh is this something different? I thought toast happened with way smaller values
messages.zh: 或者这是另一回事？我以为值小得多时就会触发 TOAST。

messages.en: @**Trevor Gross** emphasis on *forced*
messages.zh: @**Trevor Gross** 重点是“强制”。

messages.en: TOASTing that pushes the value out-of-line can happen basically to any "dynamically-sized" value aiui but in some cases Postgres will do its best to use a fully in-line representation when the data is "detoasted".
messages.zh: 据我理解，基本上任何“动态大小”的值都可能经过 TOAST 放到行外，不过某些情况下，Postgres 在“解 TOAST”时会尽量使用完全行内的表示。

messages.en: though thinking about it I might be misremembering something anyways.
messages.zh: 不过仔细想想，我也可能记错了一些内容。

topics.name: bti in compiler-builtins' aarch64 outline-atomics
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：AArch64 `compiler-builtins` 的 outline atomics 使用 `naked_asm!`，需要在函数入口加入 BTI（Branch Target Identification）提示指令（`hint #34`），否则在启用 `-Zbranch-protection=bti` 时，作为间接调用目标可能触发异常。由于 naked function 不应由编译器随意修改，且 BTI 不是 `target_feature`，现有 `cfg(target_feature = "bti")` 无法直接使用。
- **主要方案讨论**：倾向于暴露一个可供代码查询的 `cfg`，类似 panic strategy；候选形式包括与选项一一对应的 `cfg(branch_protection = "bti")`，或更通用的 target modifier cfg。也讨论过无条件加入 BTI 指令，但虽然不支持 BTI 的 CPU 会将其视为 nop，仍会带来代码尺寸和指令缓存开销，且自动修改 naked function 令人不安。
- **扩展观点**：多个 target modifiers 可能改变 ABI，naked asm、甚至普通 inline asm 可能需要知道这些配置；Alice Ryhl 和 Jacob Lifshay 认为，许多 target modifiers 都可能受益于 cfg 查询能力。不过目前尚未决定是否为所有 target modifiers 提供通用机制，相关方向由 `#152038` 提交给了 t-lang 讨论。
- **阶段性结论**：outline-atomics 的启用一度计划回滚，等待 cfg 机制落地，因为在 `compiler-builtins` 中解析 rustflags 并不理想。随后 `compiler-builtins` commit `f626afc2fc1fec64f205dda3e016eefe79d06066` 已落地，相关实现应已解决。
- **验证结果**：使用 `RUSTFLAGS=-Zbranch-protection=bti` 检查生成的汇编时，`__aarch64_cas1_relax` 入口出现了 `hint #34`；LLVM IR 中虽然看不到该指令，但汇编输出确认 BTI 提示已生成。

messages.en:
I'd like to be able to add a hint instruction to the `naked_asm!` in the compiler-builtins implementations for outline-atomics (e.g. [in this body](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/94a0cd15f5976fa35e5e6784e621c04e9f958e57/library/compiler-builtins/compiler-builtins/src/aarch64_outline_atomics.rs#L183)). This hint instruction is for BTI, which is a hardware feature that guards against the execution of instructions that aren't the intended target of a branch. The hint instruction we want to add here indicates that this is expected to be the target of a call, as otherwise an exception is thrown and we don't want that.

The compiler normally adds these automatically when `-Zbranch-protection=bti` is enabled, but it wouldn't be appropriate to do this for naked functions. We also only want to add this when BTI is enabled, not unconditionally, but only the compiler knows that. LLVM does this conditionally when they generate their implementations ([here](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/737db63fafa273a840d84594ca7c96fef113c8f2/compiler-rt/lib/builtins/assembly.h#L104-L108)), because they have a define they can check. BTI isn't a target feature, so there's no `cfg(target_feature = "bti")` that we could use to cfg this in compiler-builtins.

This is a bit of a #**t-libs** question and a bit of a #**t-compiler** question, so asking here and will cross-link. I'm not especially familiar with `naked_asm!` and compiler-builtins, so unsure is this the type of issue you've come across before and have a solution to that I could re-use, or  if I'll need to go find a way to expose this as a cfg in the language to use here? (or add a perma-unstable attribute or some other mechanism that the compiler could pick up on and do this in the naked function codegen)
messages.zh:
我希望能在 compiler-builtins 的外联原子操作实现中的 `naked_asm!` 添加一条提示指令（例如[这里的函数体](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/94a0cd15f5976fa35e5e6784e621c04e9f958e57/library/compiler-builtins/compiler-builtins/src/aarch64_outline_atomics.rs#L183)). 这条提示指令用于 BTI：一种防止执行非预期分支目标指令的硬件特性。我们想在这里添加的提示指令表示，此处预期是调用的目标，否则硬件会抛出异常，而我们不希望发生这种情况。

启用 `-Zbranch-protection=bti` 时，编译器通常会自动添加这些指令，但对裸函数这么做并不合适。我们也只想在启用 BTI 时添加，而非无条件添加，但只有编译器知道它是否启用。LLVM 生成对应实现时会进行条件判断（[见这里](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/737db63fafa273a840d84594ca7c96fef113c8f2/compiler-rt/lib/builtins/assembly.h#L104-L108)），因为它们有可检查的宏定义。BTI 不是目标特性，所以没有可用于 compiler-builtins 条件编译的 `cfg(target_feature = "bti")`。

这个问题既涉及 #**t-libs**，也涉及 #**t-compiler**，因此先在这里询问，再交叉链接。我不太熟悉 `naked_asm!` 和 compiler-builtins，不知道你们以前是否遇到过这类问题、是否有可以复用的解决办法，还是我需要想办法将它作为语言中的 cfg 暴露出来？（或者添加一个永久不稳定的属性或其他机制，让编译器识别它，并在裸函数代码生成时处理。）

messages.en: It's probably appropriate to expose this as a cfg, just like how we expose panic strategy as a cfg. In the end it's something that the user may want to know about to emit the correct asm.
messages.zh: 或许应该把它暴露为 cfg，就像我们把 panic 策略暴露为 cfg 一样。毕竟用户可能需要知道这项信息，才能生成正确的汇编。

messages.en: That makes sense to me
messages.zh: 我觉得有道理。

messages.en: How bad is it to unconditionally add the BTI indications? There are variants that are a nop on unsupported cpus, right?
messages.zh: 无条件添加 BTI 标记会有多糟？有些变体在不支持的 CPU 上就是空操作，对吧？

messages.en: I'm uncomfortable with automatically adding things to naked functions. Fundamentally, these are used when you're using a custom calling convention that can't be represented with a normal function signature.
messages.zh: 我对自动给裸函数添加内容感到不安。从根本上说，裸函数用于采用无法用普通函数签名表示的自定义调用约定的场合。

messages.en: Even if we didn't automatically add it in rustc, and just unconditionally manually added it to the asm for the relevant builtins: you're right that it's a hint instruction so if the CPU doesn't support it then it'll be ignored, the only other cost is code-size and whatever overhead the no-op represents (e.g. instruction cache pressure).
messages.zh: 即使我们不在 rustc 中自动添加，而只在相关内建函数的汇编中无条件手动添加：你说得对，它是提示指令，因此 CPU 不支持时会忽略它。其他代价只有代码体积，以及空操作本身造成的开销（例如指令缓存压力）。

messages.en: If it changes how functions are called that's basically changing the ABI, so shouldn't it be a target modifier?
messages.zh: 如果它改变函数调用方式，基本上就是改变 ABI，那么难道不该是目标修饰符吗？

messages.en: `-Zbranch-protection` will be a target modifier
messages.zh: `-Zbranch-protection` 会成为目标修饰符。

messages.en: Since users can also write their own naked functions it's not specific to compiler-builtins
messages.zh: 用户也能编写自己的裸函数，所以这并不是 compiler-builtins 特有的问题。

messages.en: (it's also motivating our work on build-std for similar reasons)
messages.zh: （出于类似原因，它也在推动我们开展 build-std 的工作。）

messages.en: and target modifiers are exposed as some sort of cfg, right?
messages.zh: 目标修饰符会以某种 cfg 的形式暴露，对吧？

messages.en: I don't believe so
messages.zh: 据我所知没有。

messages.en: perhaps they should be?
messages.zh: 也许应该这样？

messages.en: it doesn't seem right to map every target modifier to a cargo feature
messages.zh: 把每个目标修饰符映射为一个 Cargo feature，似乎不太合适。

messages.en: I don't think it makes sense to be able to cfg on everything that's a target feature, that we need all code to be compiled with the modifier is a different concern than whether we want different code to be compiled because of it
messages.zh: 我认为并非每个属于目标特性的东西都值得支持 cfg。要求所有代码都使用某个修饰符编译，与是否希望据此编译不同的代码，是两件不同的事。

messages.en: aiui naked functions mean that users have to do this manually, which means they need a way to query that information.
messages.zh: 据我理解，裸函数意味着用户必须手动处理这些内容，因此需要一种查询这项信息的方式。

messages.en: It's a bit off-topic, but: target modifiers don't necessarily need to be mapped to Cargo features either, in the yet-to-be-posted-follow-up build-std RFCs, we intend to introduce mechanisms for Cargo - without knowing about rustc flags more generally - to ask rustc if std has the same target modifiers as the user's code will and then recompile std if it does. Target modifiers will always be rustc flags, how Cargo exposes those to users, whether that's a generic `rustflags` option or a dedicated switch or whatever, is up to t-cargo - neither target modifiers or build-std prescribe anything in that regard.
messages.zh: 稍微偏题一下：目标修饰符也不一定要映射为 Cargo feature。在尚未发布的后续 build-std RFC 中，我们计划引入一种机制，让 Cargo 无需普遍了解 rustc 参数，就能询问 rustc：std 的目标修饰符是否与用户代码将采用的一致，然后按需重新编译 std。目标修饰符始终是 rustc 参数；Cargo 如何向用户暴露它们，是通用 `rustflags` 选项、专用开关还是其他方式，由 t-cargo 决定。目标修饰符和 build-std 都不规定这一点。

messages.en: I mean rustc cfgs, like `cfg(target_feature = ...)`
messages.zh: 我指的是 rustc cfg，比如 `cfg(target_feature = ...)`。

messages.en:
@_**The 8472|330154** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/bti.20in.20compiler-builtins'.20aarch64.20outline-atomics/near/570358950):
```quote
aiui naked functions mean that users have to do this manually, which means they need a way to query that information.
```

hence the cfg for this particular modifier, but I'd need to think more about whether every modifier would have similar implications for authors of naked functions
messages.zh:
@_**The 8472|330154** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/bti.20in.20compiler-builtins'.20aarch64.20outline-atomics/near/570358950):
```quote
据我理解，裸函数意味着用户必须手动处理这些内容，因此需要一种查询这项信息的方式。
```

因此这个特定修饰符需要 cfg，但我还得考虑每个修饰符是否都会对裸函数作者产生类似影响。

messages.en: currently `-Zfixed-x18`, `-Zindirect-branch-cs-prefix`, `-Zreg-struct-return`, `-Zregparm`, `-Zretpoline`, `-Zretpoline-external-thunk`, `-Zsanitizer` and `-Zsanitizer-cfi-normalize-integers` and `-Zbranch-protection` (though we've not actually made it one yet, should do that) are target modifiers
messages.zh: 目前 `-Zfixed-x18`、`-Zindirect-branch-cs-prefix`、`-Zreg-struct-return`、`-Zregparm`、`-Zretpoline`、`-Zretpoline-external-thunk`、`-Zsanitizer`、`-Zsanitizer-cfi-normalize-integers` 和 `-Zbranch-protection`（虽然最后一个实际上还没改成目标修饰符，应该处理）都是目标修饰符。

messages.en: I'm not familiar enough with some of these to know if you'd need to change your asm given knowledge of them
messages.zh: 我对其中一些不够熟悉，不知道了解它们之后是否需要调整汇编。

messages.en: I'm open to the possibility that what we actually need is a target modifier cfg
messages.zh: 我不排除真正需要的是一个目标修饰符 cfg。

messages.en: @**Alice Ryhl** do you know if this is something other target modifiers would benefit from?
messages.zh: @**Alice Ryhl** 你知道其他目标修饰符是否也能从这个机制中受益吗？

messages.en: many of those change the ABI, so naked asm should know about them
messages.zh: 其中很多会改变 ABI，所以裸汇编应该知道它们。

messages.en: or even just ordinary inline asm
messages.zh: 甚至普通内联汇编也需要。

messages.en: Yeah many target modifiers probably would benefit from the ability to cfg on them.
messages.zh: 是的，很多目标修饰符大概都能从支持 cfg 查询中受益。

messages.en: Is there any reason not to basically 1:1 match the flag here, so `cfg(branch_protection = “bti”)`?
messages.zh: 有什么理由不让这里的 cfg 基本与参数一一对应，比如 `cfg(branch_protection = “bti”)`？

messages.en: Alternatively there could be something like `#[add_bti_landing_pads]`that applies to  naked functions. But a config would still be useful
messages.zh: 另一种办法是提供类似 `#[add_bti_landing_pads]` 的属性，用于裸函数。不过 cfg 仍然有用。

messages.en: We're going to revert the outline-atomics enablement because of this. I think we'll have to wait for some kind of cfg to re-land, since parsing rustflags in https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-builtins/pull/1063 isn't ideal
messages.zh: 我们将因此撤销启用外联原子操作的改动。我认为得等某种 cfg 可用后才能重新合入，因为 https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-builtins/pull/1063 中解析 rustflags 的做法并不理想。

messages.en: I think the main question is whether one should have a more general way to `cfg` like we do for target features.
messages.zh: 我觉得主要问题是，是否应该像目标特性那样提供更通用的 `cfg` 查询方式。

messages.en: I think that would be fine, but I'd expect the CLI option to also be spelled `-Ctarget-whatever=branch_protection=bti` in that case. Similar to `-Ctarget_feature=+sse` / `cfg(target_feature = "sse")`
messages.zh: 我觉得可以，不过那样的话，我也会期望命令行选项写成 `-Ctarget-whatever=branch_protection=bti`，类似 `-Ctarget_feature=+sse` / `cfg(target_feature = "sse")`。

messages.en: I don't think any of our target modifiers are stable so there's still a chance to do that
messages.zh: 据我所知，目标修饰符目前都还没稳定，因此仍有机会这样做。

messages.en: Huh, I hadn't noticed actually compiler-builtins#1063 or the issues around this upstream, it was raised to me internally at Arm
messages.zh: 咦，我还真没注意到 compiler-builtins#1063 和上游相关问题；这是 Arm 内部向我提出的。

messages.en: #152038 is asking t-lang about a target modifier cfg
messages.zh: #152038 正在向 t-lang 询问目标修饰符 cfg 的问题。

messages.en:
https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-builtins/commit/f626afc2fc1fec64f205dda3e016eefe79d06066 landed so this *should* be resolved, but how can I verify this? Checking `RUSTFLAGS=-Zbranch-protection=bti cargo asm -p compiler_builtins --lib --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu --features=compiler-builtins,unmangled-names __aarch64_cas1_relax -Zbuild-std=core` and the same thing with `--llvm` gives me:

```asm
.section .text.compiler_builtins::aarch64_outline_atomics::__aarch64_cas1_relax,"ax",@progbits
        .hidden compiler_builtins::aarch64_outline_atomics::__aarch64_cas1_relax

topics.name: `clippy::wrong_self_convention` doesn't check return type
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：`clippy::wrong_self_convention` 目前不检查返回类型，而 `as_`、`to_`、`into_` 的命名约定本身并不完全一致。API Guidelines 提到成本、所有权和抽象层级等因素，但成本无法仅从方法签名判断，标准库中也存在多个反例。
- **主要观点**：`as_` 通常表示仅重新解释或提取数据，`into_` 表示消耗 `self` 的转换，`to_` 的语义最宽泛，可进行更复杂或成本更高的转换。不过，`as_secs`、`f64::to_radians`、`Ipv6Addr::to_bits`、`u8::to_ascii_lowercase` 等例子表明这些规则会相互冲突；尤其不能仅依据方法签名或函数体可靠判断命名是否正确。
- **关于可能的 Clippy lint**：讨论认为可以增加检查缺少返回类型的方法，例如 `{as,into,to}_*(&self)` 或 `(&mut self)`，并考虑检查名称中包含 `mut` 但返回值不包含可变引用、可变拥有值或相应 guard 的方法。
- **已达成的结论**：提议的 `missing_return_type` 和 `misleading_mut_method_name` 得到了认可；后者应检查 `*_mut`、`*_mut_*`、`mut_*` 等 snake_case 单词边界，并考虑递归检查 `Option`、`Result` 等嵌套容器中的返回类型。`wrong_as_return_type` 因规则复杂、容易产生误报，暂时放弃。
- **仍未解决的问题**：无法确定一套普遍适用且低误报的规则来判断 `as_` 返回非引用类型是否错误；函数体分析也很难建立明确标准。`as_`、`to_`、`into_` 的 API conventions 仍较模糊，且相关 API Guidelines 已多年未更新。

messages.en:
:wave: Hi, with risk of posting into the wrong channel and anoying people.
There has been an concearn raised on [clippy#7676](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-clippy/issues/7676) that would likely benefit a bit of lib attention regarding how this clippy lint SHOULD work.

Concretely, when something should be named `as_*` vs `to_*` vs `into_*`, where we seem to be a bit self-inconsistent in the stdlib, so designing an lint is a bit hard :laughing:
messages.zh:
:wave: 大家好，冒着发错频道、打扰大家的风险问一下。
[clippy#7676](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-clippy/issues/7676) 中有人提出一个问题，需要库团队关注一下，确定这个 Clippy lint 应该如何工作。

具体来说，什么时候该命名为 `as_*`、`to_*`、`into_*`。标准库自身在这方面似乎有些不一致，所以设计 lint 有点困难 :laughing:

messages.en: I think the truth of it is that we are inconsistent, and that it's mostly vibes-based, and I'm not certain a concrete rule for this exists. That said, I think some of the cases given there are cases where we genuinely got it wrong though (for example `u8::to_ascii_lowercase` should take `self` not `&self`). I will say: I don't generally think about cost for `as_` vs `to_`, I think about whether or not it's the same value conceptually.
messages.zh: 我觉得实际情况就是我们不一致，而且大多凭感觉，并不确定存在明确规则。不过，我认为里面举的一些例子确实是我们做错了（例如 `u8::to_ascii_lowercase` 应该接收 `self` 而不是 `&self`）。我想说：判断 `as_` 和 `to_` 时，我一般不考虑成本，而是考虑它在概念上是否仍是同一个值。

messages.zh: 我觉得 Copy 类型超过某个大小后，接收 &self 是合理的（不过不是必须），但大体同意。

messages.en:
@**Frank (CommanderStorm)** We are fallible and thus do not get it right all the time, that much is inevitable.

To add to what @**Thom Chiovoloni** said, and somewhat restate the API guidelines which are already being referenced in that issue:
- `as_` is supposed to be something that is achievable by merely "reexamining" the data. It should not really be generating additional data, merely giving you a different view of it.
- `into_`  is a conversion that must be consuming (it essentially is trying to match intuitions from use of `From` and `Into::into`... so it should be going from `T` to `U`), and generally is not a significant modification... `into_inner` is a common function in `std`, where it just yields  `T` from `WrapperType<T>`, so yeah, not doing jack.
- `to_` is the most... wibbly of these, where as mentioned, it is a "full conversion" to a possibly very different type and possibly very different view of the data, so it's allowed to chop it up and rearrange it and do complex mathematical formulae.

I think it's Not That Surprising that `as` is often used with a `Copy` return type when the operation is basically a copy of data (as in `Duration::as_secs`) and returns an owned `Copy` of the inner data, because it's adhering to the more important idea: "nothing significant happened to get you this data, it's just basically what is behind this type".
messages.zh:
@**Frank (CommanderStorm)** 我们会犯错，所以不可能总是做对，这不可避免。

补充 @**Thom Chiovoloni** 的说法，也稍微重述一下该 issue 已引用的 API 指南：
- `as_` 应当只需“重新审视”数据就能实现。它不该真正生成额外数据，只是提供不同的视图。
- `into_` 是必须消耗输入的转换（本质上是试图符合人们使用 `From` 与 `Into::into` 时的直觉，也就是从 `T` 到 `U`），而且通常不涉及显著修改。`std` 中常见的 `into_inner` 只是从 `WrapperType<T>` 取出 `T`，所以基本什么也没做。
- `to_` 是其中最……模糊的。如前所述，它是向可能完全不同的类型和数据视图进行“完整转换”，因此允许拆解、重组数据，甚至执行复杂数学公式。

操作基本上只是复制数据时，`as` 经常返回 `Copy` 类型（如 `Duration::as_secs`），返回内部数据的一个有所有权的 `Copy` 值。我认为这并不奇怪，因为它符合更重要的观念：“获得这些数据没有发生什么显著操作，它基本上就是这个类型内部已有的东西。”

messages.en:
basically it's not surprising that this happened:
> * `f64::to_radians(self) -> f64` violates the cost convention. Looking into the source code, it only divides and multiples which is cheap. However, it follows the "same abstraction level different representation" convention. So these conventions can clearly contradict with each other.
> * `u8::to_ascii_lowercase(&self) -> u8` violates the "borrowed -> owned (non-Copy types)" convention.
> * `Ipv6Addr::to_bits(self) -> u128` violates the cost because it is a cheap `from_be_bytes` conversion.

because `to_` is the most "it can do whatever" here.

I would say that generally it's wrong to have `as_` for `T -> U` where it isn't `&T -> &U` if the types involved are not Copy, though, and I don't think that people should really be in the habit of it for Copy types either.
messages.zh:
基本上，出现这些情况并不奇怪：
> * `f64::to_radians(self) -> f64` 违反成本约定。源码只进行廉价的乘除运算，但符合“同一抽象层次、不同表示”的约定，所以这些约定显然会互相冲突。
> * `u8::to_ascii_lowercase(&self) -> u8` 违反“借用 -> 有所有权值（非 Copy 类型）”的约定。
> * `Ipv6Addr::to_bits(self) -> u128` 违反成本约定，因为它只是廉价的 `from_be_bytes` 转换。

因为这里 `to_` 是最能“随便做什么”的前缀。

不过我认为，涉及非 Copy 类型时，用 `as_` 表示 `T -> U` 而非 `&T -> &U` 通常是错误的；即使是 Copy 类型，我也不认为大家应该养成这样命名的习惯。

messages.en: I don't know when the API guidelines were cooked up though, they might have been partially a response to debates about functions like these.
messages.zh: 不过我不知道 API 指南是什么时候制定的；它可能部分就是对这类函数争论的回应。

messages.en: :clar_fon: have been meaning to eventually revive the API conventions but that is like, bottom of the list of priorities
messages.zh: :clar_fon: 我一直打算找机会重新推动 API 约定的维护，不过这件事几乎排在优先事项的最底部。

messages.en:
From the issue:

> The [C-CONV](https://rust-lang.github.io/api-guidelines/naming.html#ad-hoc-conversions-follow-as_-to_-into_-conventions-c-conv) API guideline suggests a number of conventions:
> - **Cost**: Free (`as_`), expensive (`to_`), variable (`into_`) cost. This cannot be determined using the method signature.
> - **Ownership**: Borrowed (reference) or owned (copy vs non-copy) type. This can be determined. However, there are several counter example in the std library.
> - **Abstraction**: The `as_` and `into_` *typically* decrease abstraction while the `to_` *typically* stays at the abstraction level but change its representation. I am not sure how to enforce this or worth enforcing it.
> - **Qualifiers**[+types]: If the `mut` in the conversion name, then the return type should be mutable. This is the most straightforward from the conventions. (Although, it could be more complicated if we add the `ref`, `slice`, `vec` and other qualifiers.)

Of those, clippy can reason about ownership, mutability/types, but cost is subjective and context dependent.

From what was written in this thread, could we for example say as a subset of things that we can agree on are:
- no return type -> lint
- `as_` with `Result<T>` or `Option<T>`-> lint,
- (maybe controversial) `as_` with an non-reference Copy type?
- `mut` in the conversion name, but return type not mutable -> lint

Some of this  under "don't break public API" setting by default I think, so would not lint on std, unless std opts into this :wink:.
messages.zh:
来自该 issue：

> [C-CONV](https://rust-lang.github.io/api-guidelines/naming.html#ad-hoc-conversions-follow-as_-to_-into_-conventions-c-conv) API 指南提出几项约定：
> - **成本**：零成本（`as_`）、高成本（`to_`）、可变成本（`into_`）。无法从方法签名判断。
> - **所有权**：借用（引用）或有所有权的类型（Copy 与非 Copy）。可以判断，但标准库有几个反例。
> - **抽象层次**：`as_` 和 `into_` 通常降低抽象层次，而 `to_` 通常维持抽象层次、改变表示。我不确定如何强制执行，也不确定是否值得。
> - **限定词**与类型：转换名称含 `mut` 时，返回类型应该可变。这是最直接的约定。（加入 `ref`、`slice`、`vec` 等限定词后可能会更复杂。）

其中，Clippy 可以判断所有权、可变性和类型，但成本具有主观性且依赖上下文。

根据本话题的讨论，我们能否先就以下一部分达成一致：
- 没有返回类型：触发 lint。
- `as_` 返回 `Result<T>` 或 `Option<T>`：触发 lint。
- （可能有争议）`as_` 返回非引用的 Copy 类型？
- 转换名称含 `mut`，但返回类型不可变：触发 lint。

我觉得其中一部分默认受“不破坏公共 API”的设置限制，所以除非 std 主动启用，否则不会对 std 报 lint :wink:。

messages.en:
I don't think we're in the habit of running clippy on std without being selective about lints we choose to enforce anyways?

1. well yes, "obviously".
2. see [`Option::as_ref`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/option/enum.Option.html#method.as_ref) for a counterexample that is... probably not a mistake ^^;
3. I would personally say `as_` with a sig that isn't `&T -> &U` should be something that something like *clippy*, which is allowed to take a stronger normative stance, should feel comfortable linting on regardless of whether the signature is instead `fn(T) -> U where U: Copy`, and yes it is pretty clearly not something that should happen when `U: !Copy` (barring, like, `&mut` for `as_mut`, obviously, but that's... look, just because we can't be generic over `&` and `&mut` easily doesn't mean I'm not gonna speak like we can)
4. On the last one, "return type not mutable or owned"... owned implies mutable, but sometimes folks forget! I'm just noting that because it shouldn't lint on returning a custom `RefMut<'a, T>` handle.
messages.zh:
我们运行 Clippy 检查 std 时，本来就会有选择地决定强制哪些 lint，对吧？

1. 是的，这“显然”应该检查。
2. [`Option::as_ref`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/option/enum.Option.html#method.as_ref) 就是一个……大概不是错误的反例 ^^;
3. 我个人认为，只要 `as_` 的签名不是 `&T -> &U`，像 Clippy 这样可以采取更强规范立场的工具就可以放心给出 lint，无论签名是否为 `fn(T) -> U where U: Copy`；而且当 `U: !Copy` 时，这显然不是该做的事情（当然，`as_mut` 对应的 `&mut` 除外；只是因为我们不容易同时对 `&` 和 `&mut` 泛型化，不代表我不能像可以那样讨论）。
4. 最后一项应该是“返回类型既不可变也不拥有所有权”……拥有所有权就意味着可变，但有时大家会忘记！我提这一点，是因为返回自定义 `RefMut<'a, T>` 句柄不应该触发 lint。

messages.en: :clar_fon: fwiw clippy tries to only take uncontroversial stances in its default lints, and something like `as_` is I believe not the default
messages.zh: :clar_fon: 顺便说一下，Clippy 的默认 lint 尽量只采取没有争议的立场，而 `as_` 这个 lint 我记得不是默认启用的。

messages.en: I'd expect default clippy lints to be at least a bit opinionated. If a lint is entirely uncontroversial then it should be a rustc lint, imho.
messages.zh: 我会期望默认的 Clippy lint 至少带一点倾向。如果某个 lint 完全没有争议，我觉得它就应该成为 rustc lint。

messages.en: I mean I'm pretty much in agreement with the other clippy maintainer(?) that linting based on the name that also looks at the return type should be its own lint.
messages.zh: 我的意思是，我基本同意另一位 Clippy 维护者（？）的意见：根据名称并结合返回类型进行检查，应该是独立的 lint。

messages.en: I have grumbled about clippy's opinions before, but to be super clear, I *want* clippy to continue having opinions.
messages.zh: 我以前抱怨过 Clippy 的某些主张，但要说清楚，我希望 Clippy 继续有自己的主张。

messages.en: because clippy was always designed around the idea that some of its lints you would just allow or silence.
messages.zh: 因为 Clippy 从一开始就是基于这个想法设计的：有些 lint，你就是可以选择允许或屏蔽。

messages.en: and to a certain extent what drives me mad about the way the community interacts with clippy is them subordinating their psychic authority over things that are firmly within their domain... "how code is written in my repo"... to a robot.
messages.zh: 从某种程度上说，社区与 Clippy 互动的方式让我抓狂：大家把本来完全属于自己决定的事情……“我的仓库里代码该怎么写”……的判断权交给了机器人。

messages.en: YOU CAN DISAGREE WITH A MACHINE.
messages.zh: 你可以不同意机器！

messages.en: anyway
messages.zh: 总之。

```quote
I'd expect default clippy lints to be at least a bit opinionated. If a lint is entirely uncontroversial then it should be a rustc lint, imho.
```

topics.name: on_broken_pipe eii to fix SIGPIPE
topics.summary:
- 该话题围绕通过 `std::io::on_broken_pipe() -> std::io::OnBrokenPipe`（EII）解决 `SIGPIPE` 问题；当前 EII 在部分目标平台上因 weak linkage 不工作而存在问题。
- 讨论指出，如果 `on_broken_pipe` 不放在 `std::os::unix` 中，就必须能在 Windows 等平台上定义。一个方案是仅在 Unix 目标上使用 `#[eii(on_broken_pipe)]`，其他平台提供无法被覆盖的普通函数。
- 有观点认为不应直接忽略 Windows（尤其是 MinGW）的链接问题：新版 Binutils 可能已修复部分 weak symbols 处理，LLD 也可能已经支持或较容易支持，因此相关情况需要重新评估。
- Zack Weinberg 指出示例 API 中 `SIG_IGN` 与 `SIG_DFL` 对应的枚举项文档效果写反了：应明确区分忽略 `SIGPIPE` 后通过 `ErrorKind::BrokenPipe` 报错，以及保留默认行为导致进程终止。
- 目前已在 tracking issue 的 Steps 中加入处理跨平台默认实现/链接支持的事项，但 Windows/MinGW 等目标上的 EII 支持及最终 API 方案仍未解决。

messages.en: This topic is for discussions in the context of [Tracking Issue for externally implementable item `std::io::on_broken_pipe() -> std::io::OnBrokenPipe`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/150588) which solves the [SIGPIPE](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/46016) problem with an [externally implementable item (eii)](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/125418).
messages.zh: 本话题用于讨论[可由外部提供实现的项 `std::io::on_broken_pipe() -> std::io::OnBrokenPipe` 的跟踪 issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/150588)：它通过[可由外部提供实现的项（EII）](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/125418)解决 [SIGPIPE](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/46016) 问题。

I think you are referring to [this](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1b4325211c3228dd10eea12e9b3f749f87363d95/tests/ui/eii/codegen_cross_crate.rs#L6)?

messages.en: Unless you want to put `on_broken_pipe` in `std::os::unix` it would have to be possible to define it on Windows too.
messages.zh: 除非你打算把 `on_broken_pipe` 放到 `std::os::unix` 中，否则 Windows 上也必须能够定义它。

messages.en:
Maybe we can do something like this?

```rs
#[cfg_attr(target_family = "unix", eii(on_broken_pipe))]
pub fn on_broken_pipe() -> OnBrokenPipe {
    OnBrokenPipe::Default
}
```

So that on e.g. mingw it would be a regular function that can't be overriden. Same thing on external implementations. Admittedly it would be a bit annoying, but ...

topics.name: Looking for reviewer for an OsStr + Pattern related change
topics.name_zh: Looking for reviewer for an OsStr + Pattern related change
topics.summary:
- 该工作旨在恢复并扩展一个已停滞数年的 PR：一部分将 `core::str::Pattern` 参数化/泛化，使其可用于更多类型；另一部分基于此为 `OsStr` 增加类似 `&str` 的 pattern API，并适配新的不稳定 `OsStr` API。
- 主要待讨论的设计问题包括：是否不必将全部 API gate 在 `pattern` feature 下，以便先稳定与稳定版 `&str` API 对应的部分；`OsStr` 无法直接使用闭包形式的 `Pattern`，目前考虑通过 `predicate` 函数绕开 `OsString` 位于 `std` 的限制；字符数组/切片 matcher 是否需要公开内部 trait，或改用 sealed trait、迁移部分实现到 `std`、以及使用 `AsRef<[char]>`（可能有性能代价）。
- 多位参与者认为原始 PR 过于庞大，建议按逻辑上的独立变更拆成 stacked pull requests，而不是简单保留一个巨型 PR；代码移动最好单独放在只包含移动的 commit 中，以便 review。作者已拆分出多个相互依赖的 PR，并确认各 commit 的测试曾通过，但部分中间 commit 会暂时引入性能回归，后续 commit 再恢复优化。
- 关于 PR 流程曾出现混淆：建议只有当前可 review 的首个 PR 保持 ready，其余依赖尚未合并的 PR 标为 draft；某个 PR 准备接受 review 时再 rebase 并取消 draft，否则 draft PR 通常不会进入 review 队列。作者已根据意见处理格式、缺失注释、代码移动和 `Pattern<str>` 等修改，收到过部分 review。
- 目前仍未解决的是后续 PR 的完整 review 和合并。`libs` 团队说明 reviewer 资源比预期更紧张，大型变更需要较长时间；社区 review 是否适用于 `libs` 也被提出，但由于涉及 API stability，不能直接照搬 Clippy 的模式。作者仍在等待对较早未合并 PR（尤其从 #161606 开始）的进一步 review，并询问还能做什么来推动进展。

Anyway, open questions:
1. Right now it gates everything into "pattern" feature even though API closely maps what you get on `&str` in stable. I think it can use something else that it can be stabilized before the pattern stuff.
2. &str gives a way to access patterns with closures (s.strip_prefix(|c| c == 'x')). This works because Pattern, &str and FnMut all living in core. For OsStr you have to use `predicate` function `(os.strip_prefix(predicate(|c| c == 'x')))` to get around the fact that OsString lives in std.
3. I added matchers by array/slice/etc of chars, this required to make an internal trait public. Can make it sealed/whatever, can probably do some shenanigans to move some of the code into std (right now it all lives in one place), or get rid of the custom trait, use AsRef<[char]> - this costs some performance, I have benchmark results somewhere.
messages.zh:
总之，目前的问题是：
1. 现在所有内容都受 “pattern” 特性门控，虽然 API 与稳定版 `&str` 上的接口非常接近。我觉得可以用另一个特性来门控，让它有机会早于 pattern 相关内容稳定。
2. &str 支持用闭包作为模式（s.strip_prefix(|c| c == 'x')）。这是因为 Pattern、&str 和 FnMut 都在 core 中。对于 OsStr，必须使用 `predicate` 函数 `(os.strip_prefix(predicate(|c| c == 'x')))`，绕过 OsString 位于 std 中这一限制。
3. 我添加了使用字符数组、切片等的匹配器，因此需要把一个内部 trait 公开。可以把它设为 sealed；也可以想办法把部分代码移到 std（现在全部位于同一处）；或者去掉自定义 trait，改用 AsRef<[char]>，但这会损失一些性能，我有相关的基准测试结果。

messages.en: 5th PR reverts an optimization, 10th PR re-adds it back reimplemented in terms of a new Pattern. That's 5 commits, plus one with tests... I could probably try to keep it in and propagate all the changes, but it will make some of the diffs bigger.
messages.zh: 第 5 个 PR 撤销了一项优化，第 10 个 PR 再基于新的 Pattern 重新实现并加回来。这中间隔着 5 个提交，外加一个测试提交……我大概可以尝试保留这项优化，并一路同步所有改动，但这样一些差异会变大。

messages.en: Or will add more PRs. Dunno what's the best approach.
messages.zh: 或者会多出一些 PR。不知道哪种方式最好。

messages.en: It's been two weeks since the last comment I got and two weeks since my last push (well, will be in a few hours). I adjusting some wording in a few places and tried harder to minimize the changes - mostly avoiding changes to lifetimes (plus rebased all the commits on top to take that into account).
messages.zh: 距离我收到最后一条评论和上次推送都已经两周了（准确说再过几个小时）。我调整了几处措辞，并进一步尽量缩小改动，主要是避免修改生命周期；也把后续所有提交都变基了，以适配这些调整。

messages.en:
I have done another review, resolved the comments that have been fixed, and noted a safety comment and some formatting nitpicks that would be good to fix.

I've also explained how to make code moves easier to review, by putting them entirely in their own commit, without any comment changes (or trivial compilation fix changes). Sometimes this speeds up reviews, because reviewers can see in git that the commit diff is all moves.
messages.zh:
我又审阅了一遍，关闭了已经解决的评论，并指出了一处安全性注释和一些值得修正的格式细节。

我还解释了怎样让代码移动更容易审阅：把移动单独放在一个提交里，不要夹杂任何注释修改（或简单的编译修复）。有时这样可以加快审阅，因为审阅者能在 git 中直接看到整个提交的差异都是代码移动。

messages.en: Will check the missing bits. Originally code move commit was just the code move but it seems it drifted a bit across multiple rebases/revisions. Will make sure it's just the move again.
messages.zh: 我会检查遗漏的部分。最初那个移动代码的提交确实只做了移动，但多次变基和修改后似乎混进了别的内容。我会确保它重新变成纯粹的移动。

messages.en: Fixed formatting, fixed missing comment, extracted the moving part from the commit that used to mostly rehome Pattern to a different module - that commit doesn't compile.
messages.zh: 修正了格式，补上了缺少的注释，并从原先主要把 Pattern 移到另一个模块的提交中拆出了代码移动部分；这个移动提交无法编译。

messages.en: No stress, it is fine to have a commit that does a simple code change operation like a move or a search and replace, then fix it up in the next commit 🙂
messages.zh: 不用担心，一个提交只做移动、查找替换之类的简单代码操作，然后在下一个提交中修复编译问题，是可以的 🙂

topics.name: Request releasing new version of backtrace
topics.name_zh: Request releasing new version of backtrace
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：Windows 上运行 Rust 仓库的 `.\x check` 时，`backtrace 0.3.76` 在 `--cfg=windows_raw_dylib` 下出现函数调用约定类型不匹配错误：期望 `unsafe extern "C" fn`，实际为 `unsafe extern "system" fn`。该问题通常编译 Windows 版本的 `backtrace 0.3.75` 时不会触发。
- **重要观点与方案**：该问题已在 `backtrace-rs` 的 PR #744 中修复，但修复后尚未发布到 crates.io。使用 `[patch.crates-io]` 指向 backtrace Git 仓库可以绕过编译错误；相关发布请求也已有 issue #770。
- **已达成结论**：`backtrace 0.3.77` 已发布。手动将锁定版本更新为 `0.3.77` 后，`.\x check` 可以正常运行。
- **补充情况**：最新的 `priroda` 重构后使用了 Miri 的 `Cargo.lock`，默认锁定 `backtrace 0.3.75`；因此首次验证成功主要使用的是旧版本，手动更新到 `0.3.77` 后仍能正常工作。

messages.en:
That compile error only triggers under rustflags `--cfg=windows_raw_dylib`. It's added by bootstrap. Normally compiling backtrace 0.3.75 in windows is fine. 

After adding 
```
[patch.crates-io]
backtrace = { git = "https://github.com/rust-lang/backtrace-rs" }
```
to priroda `Cargo.toml` that compile error vanished.

So it seems that backtrace should release a new version to crates.io . (there is already an issue asking for that https://github.com/rust-lang/backtrace-rs/issues/770 )
messages.zh:
这个编译错误只在使用 rustflags `--cfg=windows_raw_dylib` 时触发，该选项由 bootstrap 添加。正常情况下，在 Windows 上编译 backtrace 0.3.75 没有问题。

在 priroda 的 `Cargo.toml` 中加入以下内容后，编译错误消失了：

```
[patch.crates-io]
backtrace = { git = "https://github.com/rust-lang/backtrace-rs" }
```

因此，backtrace 似乎应该向 crates.io 发布新版本。（已经有人提出了这个请求：https://github.com/rust-lang/backtrace-rs/issues/770 ）

topics.name: Some UEFI and Command security bugs
topics.name_zh: Some UEFI and Command security bugs
topics.summary:
- 有人提交了多个与 UEFI 和 `Command` 相关的问题：UEFI 问题主要涉及行为异常的 UEFI drivers；`Command` 问题涉及攻击者可控制传给 `Command::new` 的可执行文件路径。Manish 认为它们不属于私下安全报告范围，风险也不算特别高，但可以进行加固。
- 讨论者认为这些问题不应按 security issue 处理。`Command` 问题曾由旧的 libs-api 讨论过，未来可能接受改进 patch 作为 QOL（quality of life）改进，也可能因负担过大而拒绝；该问题目前的安全性表述不恰当。
- 对提交内容的质量存在批评：部分建议可能有细微错误，例如主张静默忽略用户请求的参数，而不是 panic 或返回错误；另一个问题虽然看起来合理，但严重性和优先级尚不明确。`unimplemented!()` 加 `fixme` 也被认为缺乏说服力。
- 相关人员已要求提交者遵守 LLM policy，但对方没有听从，导致额外的审查时间浪费；团队认为后续在转交此类报告时可能需要更明确、更谨慎地强调该政策。提交者的 GitHub 用户名似乎也已从 `JoelBinu` 改为 `cueballcipher`。

messages.en:
https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues?q=is%3Aissue+state%3Aopen+author%3AJoelBinu

These were reported to us, I deemed them out of scope for private reporting. The UEFI ones are mostly around misbehaving UEFI drivers, and the Command one is about situations where an attacker can control the path to an executable passed to Command::new. Neither seem particularly dangerous, but all could use hardening.
messages.zh:
https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues?q=is%3Aissue+state%3Aopen+author%3AJoelBinu

这些问题是向我们报告的，我判断它们不属于需要私下报告的范围。UEFI 的问题主要涉及行为异常的 UEFI 驱动，Command 的问题则涉及攻击者能够控制传给 Command::new 的可执行文件路径的情况。两者似乎都没有特别危险，不过都可以做一些加固。

topics.name: Impl Partial/Ord for Discriminant
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：是否应为 `Discriminant<T>` 提供排序能力。直接实现 `PartialOrd`/`Ord` 可能过于隐式，且会暴露枚举变体顺序等未稳定的实现细节。
- **主要方案**：提供显式的 `UnstableOrd` 包装类型，或增加类似 `f32::total_cmp` 的 `Discriminant::unstable_cmp` 方法；包装类型便于放入结构体并派生排序。有人建议可通过 `unstable_ord()` 获取，但不应设为 `unsafe`，因为这不涉及内存安全。
- **语义与限制**：文档应明确说明，第三方 crate 若调整变体顺序导致使用方代码行为变化，责任在使用方。`Discriminant<T>` 对任意 `T` 都可用；当前 rustc LLVM 后端中，非枚举类型的 discriminant 实际为 `0`。讨论倾向于将 `struct` 视为只有一个 variant 的类型，而不是读取其内部字节；后者还可能遇到未初始化字节。
- **进展与未决事项**：与会者认为显式方法或包装类型较为合理，并可能推进相关 FCP。Zac Harrold 已提交实现 PR `#164231`，并按要求创建 ACP `libs-team/issues/925`；聊天记录中尚未给出最终批准或稳定化结论。

messages.en: Was reading through some old `proposed-final-comment-period` PRs and came across https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/106418. I couldn't find it suggested, but how do people feel about providing an `UnstableOrd` wrapper which can be used to add ordering to `Discriminant<T>` for all `T`? Similar to how `std::path::Display` adds a `Display` implementation to `Path` and `bevy::math::FloatOrd` adds `Ord` to `f32` and `f64`. Could even make its construction `unsafe` if we're *really* concerned about exposing private implementation details?
messages.zh: 我在翻看一些较早的带有 `proposed-final-comment-period` 标签的 PR 时，看到了 https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/106418 。我没有找到有人提出这个建议：大家觉得提供一个 `UnstableOrd` 包装类型如何？它可以为所有 `T` 的 `Discriminant<T>` 增加排序能力，类似于 `std::path::Display` 为 `Path` 提供 `Display` 实现，以及 `bevy::math::FloatOrd` 为 `f32` 和 `f64` 提供 `Ord`。如果我们*真的*担心暴露私有实现细节，甚至可以把它的构造设为 `unsafe`？

messages.en:
having an unstable Ord wrapper could be useful.
imo it shouldn't be `unsafe` (that's only for memory safety and similar).
we should probably make very clear in the docs that if you use `unstable_ord` on some third party crate that if they reorder their variants and that breaks your code that's your fault not theirs (unless they document otherwise).
messages.zh:
提供一个不稳定排序的 Ord 包装类型可能有用。
我认为它不应该是 `unsafe`（unsafe 只用于内存安全等类似问题）。
我们或许应在文档中明确说明：如果你对第三方 crate 使用 `unstable_ord`，而对方重新排列枚举变体导致你的代码出问题，那是你的责任，不是他们的，除非对方另有文档保证。

messages.en: I think having it explicitly named `UnstableOrd` will help with that as well. It'd also be possible for crates to ban that type to prevent its usage internally, which is nice.
messages.zh: 我想，明确把它命名为 `UnstableOrd` 也有助于说明这一点。crate 还可以禁止使用这个类型，阻止内部代码使用它，这也不错。

messages.en: although I think that's possible even just for the (non-existent) `Discriminant::<T>::cmp`
messages.zh: 不过我想，即使只是那个（尚不存在的）`Discriminant::<T>::cmp`，也可以禁止使用。

messages.en: oh, i was thinking you'd get it via `some_discriminant.unstable_ord()` so wouldn't usually need to name the type, just like `path.display()` (I've never seen code using that type by name)
messages.zh: 哦，我设想的是通过 `some_discriminant.unstable_ord()` 获取它，所以通常不需要写出类型名称，就像 `path.display()` 一样（我从没见过代码显式使用那个类型名）。

messages.en: Either would work, and both the inheret method and the type could be equally banned.
messages.zh: 两种方式都可以，而且固有方法和类型都同样可以禁用。

messages.en:
Note that float types also have a method that returns a total ordering in the standard library
https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.f64.html#method.total_cmp
messages.zh:
注意，标准库里的浮点类型也有返回全序比较结果的方法：
https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.f64.html#method.total_cmp

messages.en: A wrapper type is more useful if you want to put it in a struct and derive an ordering. Which seems more important for floats than discriminants.
messages.zh: 如果想把它放进结构体中并派生排序实现，包装类型会更有用。对浮点数而言，这似乎比对判别值更重要。

messages.en: Yeah so we could do `Discriminant::unstable_cmp` to mirror the float API
messages.zh: 是的，所以我们可以提供 `Discriminant::unstable_cmp`，与浮点数的 API 对应。

messages.en: Interestingly, `Discriminant` works for any type, it's just not specified what gets returned for structs, so I guess this would be a way to get a partial ordering for arbitrary types
messages.zh: 有趣的是，`Discriminant` 适用于任何类型，只是没有规定对结构体会返回什么。所以我想，这或许能为任意类型提供一种偏序。

messages.en: Not a useful one in most contexts, but I guess better than nothing (?)
messages.zh: 虽然在多数场景中没什么用，不过总比没有好吧（？）

messages.en:
Currently the non-enum discriminant value is just zero in the rustc LLVM backend
https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/b5427502dab50cb27d9327d2893ddf2337dd4388/compiler/rustc_codegen_ssa/src/mir/operand.rs#L488
messages.zh:
目前，在 rustc 的 LLVM 后端中，非枚举类型的判别值就是零：
https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/b5427502dab50cb27d9327d2893ddf2337dd4388/compiler/rustc_codegen_ssa/src/mir/operand.rs#L488

messages.en: Which makes sense, no different than if the type was an enum with exactly one variant
messages.zh: 这很合理，就像该类型是一个恰好只有一个变体的枚举一样。

messages.en: :clar_fon: honestly it would be useful to document that structs are treated as 1-variant enums in practice. I don't think it would be a large ask to guarantee that
messages.zh: :clar_fon: 说实话，把结构体实际上按单变体枚举处理这一点写入文档会有帮助。我认为保证这一点并不是很高的要求。

messages.en: The other possible impl would be reading the first byte(s) of the struct, aka, falling through to the "separate enum discriminant" arm
messages.zh: 另一种可能的实现是读取结构体开头的一个或几个字节，也就是落入“独立枚举判别值”的那个分支。

messages.en:
@_**teor|325209** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Impl.20Partial.2FOrd.20for.20Discriminant/near/630970731):
```quote
The other possible impl would be reading the first byte(s) of the struct, aka, falling through to the "separate enum discriminant" arm
```

I would be very surprised to see that as the implementation TBH. It feels intuitive to me that a struct is essentially a single variant enum, so I would expect `enum Foo { Inner(...) }` to behave the same way as `struct Foo(...)` as far as discrimination is concerned.
messages.zh:
@_**teor|325209** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Impl.20Partial.2FOrd.20for.20Discriminant/near/630970731):
```quote
另一种可能的实现是读取结构体开头的一个或几个字节，也就是落入“独立枚举判别值”的那个分支。
```

坦白说，如果真采用那种实现，我会很惊讶。对我来说，结构体本质上是单变体枚举，这很直观。因此就判别而言，我预期 `enum Foo { Inner(...) }` 的行为应该与 `struct Foo(...)` 相同。

messages.en: I can appreciate that reading some data within the struct would allow the discriminant value to be more useful, but I believe it's a utility at too high a conceptual cost.
messages.zh: 我理解，读取结构体内部的一些数据会让判别值更有用，但我认为为此付出的概念复杂度代价太高。

messages.en: Especially since the intention is for everyone to actually use `PartialOrd`
messages.zh: 尤其是既然我们的意图是让大家真正去使用 `PartialOrd`。

messages.en: effectively it represents the "trivially correct" implementation of `Ord` which just treats all values as equal
messages.zh: 实际上，它代表的是一种“显然正确”的 `Ord` 实现：直接把所有值都视为相等。

messages.en: reading data within a struct may not always be possible, because it might contain bytes that are uninit
messages.zh: 读取结构体内部的数据不一定总是可行，因为其中可能包含未初始化的字节。

messages.en: yeah, it would need to be special cased for that anyway
messages.zh: 对，无论如何也得为这种情况做特殊处理。

messages.en: Note that if someone really wants to order `std::mem::Discriminant`s they can hack it using `Hash`, which exposes the underlying discriminant value anyway. I agree that implementing `Ord`/`PartialOrd` would be too implicit, but having a separate type or method (e.g. `Discriminant::unstable_cmp`, similar to `f32::total_cmp`) should be explicit enough.
messages.zh: 注意，如果有人真的想对 `std::mem::Discriminant` 排序，可以利用 `Hash` 绕着实现，因为它反正会暴露底层判别值。我同意直接实现 `Ord`/`PartialOrd` 太隐式，但单独提供一个类型或方法（例如类似 `f32::total_cmp` 的 `Discriminant::unstable_cmp`）应该足够显式。

messages.en: note that this would unblock the FCP also IMHO to offer a method, since even if we had direct access to discriminants as values that weren't represent this type, we would just deprecate this type anyway
messages.zh: 注意，我个人认为，提供一个方法也能解除 FCP 的阻碍，因为即使以后可以直接访问不由这个类型表示的判别值，我们也只需弃用这个类型。

messages.en: so it seems reasonable to add
messages.zh: 所以加上它似乎合理。

topics.name: ✔ Weird (unreachable) alignment check in `subslice_range`
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：`subslice_range` 文档称，当 `subslice` 未与 `self` 中的元素对齐时会返回 `None`。asquared31415 起初认为这条件不可能发生，因为两者都是 `&[T]`，都满足 `T` 的对齐要求。
- **重要澄清**：元素对齐不等同于类型对齐。即使指针满足 `T` 的对齐要求，子切片的起始位置仍可能落在元素中间，例如相对于元素边界偏移 `0.25`。实现检查的是字节偏移是否为 `size_of::<T>()` 的倍数，而不是 `align_of::<T>()`。
- **文档方案**：讨论认为现有措辞容易引起误解；`element_offset` 的文档表述“未指向切片中某个元素的起始位置”更清楚，且已有相关示例。asquared31415 同意据此改写并补充示例。
- **结论与状态**：asquared31415 提交了 PR #164937，并将话题标记为已解决；聊天记录未说明该 PR 是否已合并。

messages.en:
[subslice_range](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.subslice_range) says:
> Returns `None` if `subslice` does not point within the slice **or if it is not aligned with the elements in the slice**.

(emphasis mine)

I think that that second condition is unreachable and potentially confusing to include in documentation, and should be removed. `self` and `subslice` are both `&[T]` for the same `T`, and there's a **validity** invariant on references that they must be well aligned. Given that both `self` and `subslice` must be aligned to at least the align of `T`, then `subslice` will always be well aligned compared to `self`.

Is there something that I'm missing, or some other reason to keep this around? LLVM appears to optimize out the check anyway, so it seems unlikely to me that anyone could be accidentally relying on this returning `None` with arguments that were already UB to construct.
messages.zh:
[subslice_range](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.subslice_range) 的文档说：
> 如果 `subslice` 没有指向该切片内部，**或者没有与切片中的元素边界对齐**，则返回 `None`。

（强调是我加的。）

我认为第二个条件不可能出现，写在文档里反而容易造成困惑，应该删除。`self` 和 `subslice` 都是同一个 `T` 的 `&[T]`，而引用有一项**有效性**不变量：必须满足对齐要求。既然 `self` 和 `subslice` 都至少按 `T` 的对齐要求对齐，那么相对于 `self`，`subslice` 应该始终正确对齐。

我是不是漏掉了什么，或者还有其他理由保留这个条件？LLVM 似乎无论如何都会优化掉这项检查，所以我觉得不太可能有人无意中依赖这样的行为：传入在构造时就已经产生 UB 的参数，然后得到 `None`。

messages.en: what if `T` is `[u8; 4]` where you could have your slice start 1 byte before the element you're querying?
messages.zh: 如果 `T` 是 `[u8; 4]` 呢？切片可能从你所查询元素的前一个字节开始。

messages.en: that's still well aligned, isn't it?
messages.zh: 那不仍然满足对齐要求吗？

messages.en: `T` being aligned does not mean the alignment is the same as `T`'s size
messages.zh: `T` 满足对齐要求，不代表它的对齐值等于 `T` 的大小。

messages.en:
@_**asquared31415|384759** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Weird.20.28unreachable.29.20alignment.20check.20in.20.60subslice_range.60/near/634802720):
```quote
that's still well aligned, isn't it?
```

not to the slice's elements, it would be at index `0.25`
messages.zh:
@_**asquared31415|384759** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Weird.20.28unreachable.29.20alignment.20check.20in.20.60subslice_range.60/near/634802720):
```quote
那不仍然满足对齐要求吗？
```

没有与切片中的元素边界对齐，它相当于位于索引 `0.25`。

messages.en: oh right
messages.zh: 哦，对。

messages.en: The wording in the docs is a little confusing, we should add an example for this. If you look at the implementation, it doesn't check anything related to `align_of::<T>()`, only whether the byte offset within the slice  is a multiple of `size_of::<T>()`
messages.zh: 文档措辞有点容易误解，我们应该加一个例子。如果看实现，它没有检查任何与 `align_of::<T>()` 有关的东西，只检查切片内的字节偏移是否为 `size_of::<T>()` 的整数倍。

messages.en: A docs example definitely would have helped! I can work on that.
messages.zh: 文档示例肯定会有帮助！我可以来补。

messages.en:
There is an existing example in the method above
https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.element_offset
messages.zh:
上面那个方法已经有一个例子：
https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.element_offset

messages.en:
It also has clearer wording:
> does not point to the start of an element within the slice.
messages.zh:
它的措辞也更清楚：
> 没有指向切片内某个元素的起始位置。

topics.name: skipping ACP in obvious cases?
topics.summary:
- 核心问题：对于像 #164848 这样明显属于疏漏、实现直接且团队大概率会接受的改动，是否可以跳过 ACP（API Change Proposal）流程。
- Jacob Pratt 倾向于在补充测试后直接接受该 PR，认为无需 ACP；他指出该改动是 unstable implementation，因此不涉及相应担忧。
- Max 以 #161531 为例指出，ACP 的适用规则似乎较为主观：该 PR 虽被告知可以跳过 ACP，但仍在 `proposed-fcp` 阶段停留了两个月。
- Fon 澄清：ACP 严格来说是可选流程，reviewer 可以自行判断是否有必要，因此不同 reviewer 可能作出不同决定。
- 结论：是否需要 ACP 由 reviewer 按具体情况决定，并不存在所有人都必须遵循的统一硬性标准；但这种规则的主观性和一致性问题仍未解决。

messages.en: Without digging up the document introducing ACPs, are we allowed to skip it in cases that are obvious? I ask because of #164848. It's unquestionably an oversight, has a straightforward implementation, and I cannot imagine the team *not* wanting this. Personally I'm inclined to accept to PR once tests are added, bypassing the ACP.

topics.name: Pushing `breakpoint` over the finish line?
topics.name_zh: 正在推送`breakpoint`冲过终点线了？
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：`breakpoint` intrinsic 的语义长期未能统一，主要分歧是继续执行后出现 UB 时由谁负责。讨论中的 `yeet1` 认为默认应将其视为不会继续执行，继续操作由 debugger 用户承担风险；`yeet2` 则要求程序本身必须在 `breakpoint()` 返回后保持无 UB，等价于程序应能承受 `breakpoint()` 被替换为 NOP。
- **编译器与优化行为**：目前普遍认为 `yeet1` 与 `yeet2` 在普通编译器优化和代码生成上没有区别（除 `const-eval`/Miri 行为外）；两者都应是至少和“可能退出程序”的操作一样强的 barrier，不能让后续 UB 向 `breakpoint()` 之前“时间旅行”。真正差异主要是 soundness 责任归属，以及 Miri/CTFE 如何处理。
- **主要倾向与方案**：多数参与者倾向 `yeet2`，认为名为 `breakpoint` 的操作应类似 debugger 中设置的断点，继续执行不应天然被视为 UB；若需要绝对终止，应使用 `abort_immediate()` 或循环。支持 `yeet1` 的观点则强调需要一个与底层 `int3`/debug-break 指令一一对应、默认中止但允许 debugger 用户强行继续的原语，尤其用于紧凑的 assert-like 调试代码。
- **可移植性与实现问题**：不同架构和环境对 breakpoint 指令的行为不同；某些目标（如旧 ARM、AVR、Wasm 以及部分 bare-metal 环境）可能在无 debugger 时继续、成为 NOP、只能循环或无法可靠触发调试器。因此 `yeet1` 可能无法在所有目标上实现，`yeet2` 更容易提供可移植语义，但“仅在 debugger 存在时暂停、否则 NOP”的行为需要 OS 支持，不能由 `core` 普遍保证。
- **当前结论与未解决事项**：尚未达成最终稳定化结论。讨论中形成的共识是应尽快选择并发布某种方案，且 `t-lang` 需要参与确定 intrinsic 的 opsem；可能的方向包括先稳定 `yeet2`（名称可为 `resumable_breakpoint` 或 `breakpoint`），以后再增加 `yeet1`，或同时提供两个明确命名的函数。仍未解决的问题包括最终的 soundness 规则、Miri/CTFE 默认应 abort 还是继续、不同目标的 fallback，以及两个相近 API 带来的命名和使用困惑。

messages.en: I feel like at this point, the only thing worse than picking the "wrong" one of these two is not picking either, and leaving Rust without an official way to trigger a breakpoint for another year. I have a clearly expressed preference that I will keep arguing for, but I would prefer the outcome of "t-libs picks the option I dont like" over "we dont pick anything".
messages.zh: 我觉得到了现在这个阶段，唯一比在这两个选项中选错更糟糕的事，就是一个都不选，让 Rust 再过一年仍然没有官方触发断点的方式。我确实有明确表达过自己的偏好，也会继续为此争论，但相比“什么都不选”，我更愿意接受“t-libs 选择了我不喜欢的那个选项”。

messages.en: (t-lang may also have opinions on this and they will be involved because this is an intrinsic. I didn't know which of the teams to bring this to first.)
messages.zh: （t-lang 可能也会对此有自己的看法，而且由于这是一个 intrinsic，他们也会参与进来。我只是拿不准应该先找哪个团队。）

messages.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622575547):
````quote
`yeet1` or `yeet2` -- since `trap` is clearly different, it has a different type signature
````
sorry i am new to this conversation, but the way i see it, `yeet1` and `yeet2` should probably have different type signatures. 
after all few things make behavior more clear than good typing.

`yeet1` should return a `FakeInhabited` type, with a safe `ex_nihilo::<T>(self) -> T` method that calls  `unreacheable_unchecked`, but would not otherwise register as uninhabited to the compiler, meaning producing it would not immediately mark the following code as unreacheable.
that would properly enshrine the fact that the following code is unreacheable (it is not possible to have `FakeInhabited` in safe reacheable code) but the compiler isn't aware of it unless we tell it.

`FakeInhabited` is actually a quite convenient type to have when one whishes to check ghost branches of code without having the borrow checker go "oh, an uninhabited type was produced, let's just ignore everything that follows"
messages.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说过](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622575547)：
````quote
`yeet1` 或 `yeet2`——因为 `trap` 显然有所不同，它的类型签名也不同
````
抱歉，我刚加入这个讨论，不过在我看来，`yeet1` 和 `yeet2` 可能本来就应该有不同的类型签名。

毕竟，很少有什么东西能比良好的类型设计更能让行为变得清晰。

`yeet1` 应该返回一个 `FakeInhabited` 类型，并提供一个安全的 `ex_nihilo::<T>(self) -> T` 方法，该方法会调用 `unreacheable_unchecked`；但它本身不应被编译器视为无 inhabitant 的类型，这意味着生成它不会立即让后续代码被标记为不可达。

这样就能恰当地确立这样一个事实：后续代码是不可达的（在安全且可达的代码中不可能存在 `FakeInhabited`），但除非我们明确告知编译器，否则编译器并不知道这一点。

当你想检查代码中的幽灵分支，又不希望借用检查器看到“哦，生成了一个无 inhabitant 的类型，那我们直接忽略后面的所有内容吧”时，`FakeInhabited` 实际上是一个相当方便的类型。

messages.en:
I think it would be very weird for us to have something called `breakpoint` which doesn't match what other languages do. And I think even if we want a breakpoint with special ub semantics, we'd still want the underlying thing that others use (aka yeet2 in the summary).

I don't love the longer name (`breakpoint_assume_noop`) for it but I'd live with it if it means we can stabilise something.
messages.zh:
我觉得，如果我们有一个叫 `breakpoint` 的东西，却不符合其他语言中的惯例，那会非常奇怪。而且，即使我们想要一个具有特殊 UB 语义的断点，我们仍然会需要其他语言所使用的底层行为（也就是总结中的 `yeet2`）。

我不太喜欢更长的名称（`breakpoint_assume_noop`），但如果这意味着我们可以先稳定化某个东西，我也能接受。

messages.en: I’m confused about `yeet2`. The description of its assumptions sounds like it should be (in pragmatic terms) “if a debugger is not attached, continue”, and yet the “in practice” paragraph says that it would be compiled the same as `yeet1()`. Do I correctly understand, then, that of all 3 possibilities, there are none that are “continue if no debugger”?
messages.zh: 我对 `yeet2` 有些困惑。对其假设条件的描述，听起来从务实角度说应该是“如果没有附加调试器，就继续执行”，但“实际情况”那一段却说它的编译结果会和 `yeet1()` 一样。那么我是否可以正确理解为，在这 3 种可能性中，没有一种是“没有调试器时继续执行”？

messages.en: Oh, never mind, [that was already discussed](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/133724#issuecomment-2544368780) — it's not portable to do so.
messages.zh: 哦，等等，这一点[之前已经讨论过了](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/133724#issuecomment-2544368780)——这样做不具备可移植性。

messages.en: Maybe we should have `yeet2` and call it `continuable_breakpoint()`, which I think is clearer, plainer language than “breakpoint_assume_noop”.
messages.zh: 也许我们应该保留 `yeet2`，并把它叫作 `continuable_breakpoint()`；我觉得这比“breakpoint_assume_noop”更清楚，也更直白。

messages.en: (As I have said a time or two before: when you can't agree on the perfect single word that means what you want, try using more than one word. There is a lack of agreement, suggesting that `breakpoint` is not a good name.)
messages.zh: （正如我之前已经说过一两次的那样：当你们无法就一个完美的单词达成一致，而这个单词又要表达你们想表达的含义时，试试用多个单词。现在存在分歧，这说明 `breakpoint` 不是个好名字。）

messages.en: I'll throw in `breakpoint_pause` and `breakpoint_stop`
messages.zh: 我再提议两个名字：`breakpoint_pause` 和 `breakpoint_stop`。

messages.en:
It is in `core::arch` so I would kind of expect it to just follow platform semantics (although I guess it should really be in `core::os` since it's OS dependent). My problem with the longer names is they should ideally encapsulate that what it does can vary by platform, even if, the most common behaviour is consistent. We could also guard it with `is_debugger_attached()` but I don't think that's a good idea for the more primitive thing (and some platforms may not have a way to test for debugger presence).

But again, I'd be happy with any proposal that can gain consensus even if I think it less than ideal. We can stabilise whatever we call `yeet2` today but `yeet1` hasn't been implemented yet so we don't have to finalise its name (although having some idea would be good).
messages.zh:
它位于 `core::arch` 中，所以我多少会期待它直接遵循平台语义（不过我猜它实际上应该位于 `core::os`，因为它依赖操作系统）。我对较长名称的担忧是，它们理想情况下应该体现出该功能的行为可能因平台而异，即使最常见的行为是一致的。我们也可以用 `is_debugger_attached()` 对它进行保护，但我不认为这对于更底层的功能来说是个好主意（而且有些平台可能根本没有办法检测调试器是否存在）。

不过话说回来，只要某个提案能获得共识，即使我觉得它不够理想，我也会接受。我们今天就可以稳定化我们给 `yeet2` 取的任何名称，但 `yeet1` 还没有实现，因此我们不必现在就敲定它的名称（不过如果能有个大致想法就更好了）。

messages.en: like, it should optimize as-if it could return

messages.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622652907)：

```

我想到一种情况：你并不是字面意义上在使用 `unreachable_unchecked`，而是在追查某处更隐蔽的不健全性。如果你正试图修复一个已知不健全的问题，并在潜在不健全的代码之前设置了断点，那么如果允许这种 poison 传播到断点之前，就会很烦人。

messages.en:
yeet2: whenever you write `breakpoint()` you have to make sure that it's okay for that to be a NOP, and the code that runs after `breakpoint()` returns (if it returns) has to run without UB.
or, equivalently: if your code becomes unsound when I replace `breakpoint()` by a NOP, then your code was already unsound before I did that.
messages.zh:
yeet2：每当你写下 `breakpoint()` 时，都必须确保即使它实际上是个 NOP 也没问题；并且 `breakpoint()` 返回之后运行的代码（如果它返回的话）必须能够在不触发 UB 的情况下运行。  
或者等价地说：如果把 `breakpoint()` 替换成 NOP 后你的代码就会变得不健全，那么在我这么做之前，你的代码就已经是不健全的。

messages.en: yeet1: whenever you write `breakpoint()`, you can if you want treat whatever comes after that function as dead code (but the code can make the choice that its okay to continue if it wants -- which means that the compiler will not treat it as dead code, it'll pretend that the code may actually run, so the asm you get is the same as for yeet2)
messages.zh: yeet1 ：每当你写`breakpoint()`，如果您想将该函数后面的任何内容视为死代码（但代码可以做出选择，如果需要，可以继续--这意味着编译器不会将其视为死代码，它会假装代码实际上可能运行，因此您获得的asm与yeet2相同）

messages.en: I think that in my head I had a similar summary. But what is the compiler allowed to do with this distinction, if it must be a fence in either case?
messages.zh: 我觉得我脑海中也有一个类似的总结。但如果无论哪种情况它都必须是一个屏障，那么编译器究竟可以利用这个区别做什么呢？

messages.en: I'm also in favor of yeet2. yeet1 would not be sound for systems where breakpoint instructions are automatically resumed if no debugger is attached (I don't know if such native systems exist, but it is more logical to me than aborting when no debugger is attached and matches how javascript handles `debugger;`)
messages.zh: 我也支持 yeet2。对于那些在没有连接调试器时会自动继续执行断点指令的系统，yeet1 并不健全（我不知道是否真的存在这样的原生系统，但在我看来，这比没有连接调试器时直接中止更合乎逻辑，而且也符合 javascript 处理 `debugger;` 的方式）。

messages.en:
For reference, C++ merely says the semantics of `std::breakpoint` is "implementation-defined". There is a note though:

> *Note 1*: When invoked the execution of the program temporarily halts and execution is handed to the debugger until such a time as: the program is terminated by the debugger or, the debugger resumes execution of the program as if the function was not invoked.  — *end note*
messages.zh:
供参考，C++ 只说 `std::breakpoint` 的语义是“由实现定义的”。不过有一条注释：

> *注 1*：调用时，程序的执行会暂时暂停，并将执行权交给调试器，直到发生以下情况之一：程序被调试器终止，或调试器恢复程序的执行，就好像从未调用过该函数一样。——*注释结束*

messages.en: I think it should be only `yeet2`. It doesn't make sense to me to tell people it's okay to pretend debuggers don't have a continue button. If you want things to be guaranteed to stop after the breakpoint, put an abort call there.
messages.zh: 我认为应该只有 `yeet2`。在我看来，告诉人们可以假装调试器没有继续执行按钮，是没有道理的。如果你希望断点之后一定停止，那就在那儿放一个 abort 调用。

messages.en: This means that `yeet2(); unreachable_unchecked()` isn't "sound", e.g. it won't save you from the effects of `unreachable_unchecked()` if it's all that's between your code and it,  but that doesn't mean it isn't useful. I could imagine writing a macro that expanded to `#[cfg(something)] yeet2(); unreachable_unchecked();` or something, so that you could get a breakpoint in a case when you thought was impossible.
messages.zh: 这意味着 `yeet2(); unreachable_unchecked()` 并不“安全”，例如，如果你的代码与它之间只有这一段代码，它也无法保护你免受 `unreachable_unchecked()` 影响；但这并不意味着它没有用。我可以想象写一个宏，展开成 `#[cfg(something)] yeet2(); unreachable_unchecked();` 之类的形式，这样在某个你认为不可能发生的情况下，也能触发断点。

messages.zh:
@_**Thom Chiovoloni|209168** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622667935)：

我认为应该只有 `yeet2`。在我看来，告诉人们可以假装调试器没有继续执行按钮，是没有道理的。如果你希望断点之后一定停止，那就在那儿放一个 abort 调用。

人们提出这个观点，是因为希望 yeet1 断点之后的代码仍能按照“它是可达的”来进行优化，而在那里放一个 abort 并不能达到这一点。至于为什么这会如此有用，我并不清楚。

messages.en: I mean, fine, put `black_box(abort as fn())()` if that's something they care about.
messages.zh: 我的意思是，如果他们确实在意这个，那就用 `black_box(abort as fn())()`。

messages.en: The case where you care about this seems very niche to me.
messages.zh: 在我看来，会在意这种情况的人实在太少了。

messages.en: Like, realistically the ability to click 'continue' exists in the debugger. And if a program I'm running in a debugger hits a breakpoint, like, I'm probably going to try hitting continue (after looking around a bit)?

messages.en: I don't think you can put this onto a user and say 'they should know it's UB to hit continue'. That's very strange. But if that's *really* what you want, it's not like you can't "outside the model" this for cases where you control the program, and put in your documentation "if you run my program in a debugger, pressing the continue button on any breakpoints is unsafe and unsupported". It would be very strange to do this, for sure, but that's why I think it's strange for Rust to have this as an invariant in a stdlib function.
messages.zh: 我不认为你可以把这件事推给用户，然后说“他们应该知道点击继续会导致 UB”。这非常奇怪。不过，如果这确实是你想要的，也不是不能在你控制程序的情况下把它置于“模型之外”，并在文档中写明：“如果你在调试器中运行我的程序，按下任何断点上的继续按钮都是不安全且不受支持的。”这么做当然会非常奇怪，但这正是我认为 Rust 不应该把它作为标准库函数不变量的原因。

messages.en: So I haven't finished reading that huge thread and perhaps haven't gotten to the followup, but based on https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/133724#issuecomment-2961578385 it seems like the argument for yeet1 is that aborting when a debugger is not attached is desirable, so you don't forget these exist then trap some downstream user's code when they're running `strace`
messages.zh: 所以我还没读完那个很长的讨论，也许还没看到后续内容；但根据 https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/133724#issuecomment-2961578385，yeet1 的理由似乎是：当没有连接调试器时直接中止是更理想的行为，这样你就不会忘记这些断点的存在，之后又在某个下游用户运行 `strace` 时让其代码触发陷阱。

messages.en: I do kind of get that. But couldn't we theoretically have abort-by-default behavior with yeet2 soundness semantics?

messages.en: totally, yeet2 is compatible both with abort-by-default and continue-by-default

messages.en:
Are these the rules we'd want for yeet2 semantics?

1. The only guarantee is that `breakpoint` will act as either a nop or an abort
2. If a debugger is attached, it should pause on `breakpoint()` but allow resuming (net nop)
3. If a debugger is not attached or if we have no way to do (2), `breakpoint()` *should* abort, but it is also defined behavior to be a nop
4. In Miri and CTFE (if we add that), `breakpoint` is a nop
messages.zh:
以下这些是我们希望采用的 yeet2 语义规则吗？

1. 唯一的保证是，`breakpoint` 将表现为 NOP 或 abort 二者之一
2. 如果连接了调试器，那么它应该在 `breakpoint()` 处暂停，但允许继续执行（实际效果等同于 NOP）
3. 如果没有连接调试器，或者我们没有办法做到第 2 点，那么 `breakpoint()` *应该* abort，但表现为 NOP 也属于有定义的行为
4. 在 Miri 和 CTFE 中（如果我们加入这一支持），`breakpoint` 是 NOP

messages.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622662594):
```quote
yeet2: whenever you write `breakpoint()` you have to make sure that it's okay for that to be a NOP, and the code that runs after `breakpoint()` returns (if it returns) has to run without UB.
or, equivalently: if your code becomes unsound when I replace `breakpoint()` by a NOP, then your code was already unsound before I did that.
```

I'm wondering if the recent discussions about "time-traveling UB" might be able to help here. Writing something like `breakpoint(); possible_ub();`, in the course of debugging `possible_ub()` is a lot like writing `eprintln!("about to maybe crash"); possible_ub();`, but stronger. In both cases, the UB of `possible_ub()` can't time-travel to before the previous statement, it can only happen after the breakpoint/eprintln. If you continue after the breakpoint, the program executes UB, and whatever that UB causes to happen will happen. If you *don't* continue after the breakpoint, the program didn't execute UB. (Just as, for instance, if you write "if the pointer is not null, dereference it", you aren't dereferencing a null pointer.)
messages.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20%60breakpoint%60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622662594)：
```quote
yeet2：每当你写下 `breakpoint()` 时，都必须确保它表现为 NOP 是没问题的；而且 `breakpoint()` 返回后（如果它返回），后续运行的代码必须能够在没有 UB 的情况下执行。
或者，等价地说：如果把 `breakpoint()` 替换成 NOP 会让你的代码变得不健全，那么在我进行替换之前，你的代码就已经是不健全的。
```

我在想，最近关于“会穿越时间的 UB”的讨论也许能在这里帮上忙。在调试 `possible_ub()` 的过程中，写下类似 `breakpoint(); possible_ub();` 的代码，很像写下 `eprintln!("about to maybe crash"); possible_ub();`，但前者的保证更强。在这两种情况下，`possible_ub()` 的 UB 都不可能穿越时间回到前一条语句之前；它只能在 breakpoint/eprintln 之后发生。如果你在 breakpoint 之后继续执行，程序就会执行 UB，而这个 UB 导致发生的一切都会发生。如果你*不*在 breakpoint 之后继续执行，那么程序就没有执行 UB。（例如，如果你写下“如果指针不为空，就解引用它”，那么你并没有解引用空指针。）

messages.en: Nobody is claiming that the program *doesn't* have UB in it. But the no-time-traveling requirement makes the breakpoint still meaningful in that case: the program doesn't *execute* UB if you abort at the breakpoint and don't continue. Which is not the same thing as *not having* UB, but I'm hoping we broadly agree that it's still important in for breakpoints to be able to help you debug things.
messages.zh: 没人声称程序中*不存在* UB。但“不能穿越时间”的要求在这种情况下仍然让断点有意义：如果你在断点处 abort 而不继续执行，那么程序就不会*执行* UB。这和*不存在* UB 不是一回事，但我希望我们大体上都同意，对于断点来说，能够帮助你调试仍然很重要。

messages.en: I feel like the notion of somehow knowing, when you write the breakpoint, what you *want* to have happen (e.g. the user being able to continue or not) is implying a known-to-not-be-buggy program, which is somewhat incongruous with the idea of trying to debug it.
messages.zh: 我觉得，认为你在写下断点时就能以某种方式知道自己*希望*发生什么（例如用户能否继续执行），这实际上意味着你已经知道程序没有 bug；而这和尝试调试程序的想法多少有些矛盾。

messages.en: If I'm using a breakpoint to debug code that might have UB in it, then if I knew whether the breakpoint was resumable when I put it in, I'd already know the answer to the question my debugging efforts are trying to answer.
messages.zh: 如果我正在使用断点来调试一段可能包含 UB 的代码，那么如果我在加入断点时就知道这个断点是否可以继续执行，我就已经知道了调试工作想要回答的问题的答案。

messages.en: ah, for `loop { breakpoint() }` I was thinking more of something like `assert!` where you know you reached a bad state and need to stop except it specifically invokes the debugger and likely doesn't take much code space.
messages.zh: 啊，对于 `loop { breakpoint() }`，我想的更像是 `assert!`：你知道自己已经进入了错误状态，需要停下来；只不过它会专门调用调试器，而且可能不会占用多少代码空间。

messages.en: I agree `breakpoint()` should prevent later UB from messing up the stuff that comes before the `breakpoint()` call.
messages.zh: 我同意，`breakpoint()` 应该阻止后续的 UB 破坏 `breakpoint()` 调用之前的内容。

@_**Josh Triplett|239881** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622708276):

I'm wondering if the recent discussions about "time-traveling UB" might be able to help here. Writing something like `breakpoint(); possible_ub();`, in the course of debugging `possible_ub()` is a lot like writing `eprintln!("about to maybe crash"); possible_ub();`, but stronger. In both cases, the UB of `possible_ub()` can't time-travel to before the previous statement, it can only happen after the breakpoint/eprintln. If you continue after the breakpoint, the program executes UB, and whatever that UB causes to happen will happen. If you *don't* continue after the breakpoint, the program didn't execute UB. (Just as, for instance, if you write "if the pointer is not null, dereference it", you aren't dereferencing a null pointer.)

help with what?
yeet2 does not allow UB to travel upwards across it, independent of the no-time-travel change. this was already the case a year ago. *The optimizer treats yeet1 and yeet2 entirely equivalently.* The only difference between the two is who will get blamed if someone ships a library with code like [this](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622659899) and there is UB. If the person writing the code and the person operating the debugger are the same (as is typical during debugging), then either way the UB is their fault so I cannot see a meaningful difference between yeet1 and yeet2 for that case.
so which problem are you trying to solve by preferring yeet1 over yeet2 (assuming that's still what you are arguing for)?

这能帮上什么忙？
无论是否有“不能穿越时间”的改动，yeet2 都不允许 UB 穿过它向上蔓延。一年前就已经是这样了。*优化器对待 yeet1 和 yeet2 完全相同。*二者唯一的区别在于：如果有人发布了一个包含[这段代码](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20%60breakpoint%60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622659899)的库，并且其中存在 UB，那么最终该怪谁。若编写代码的人和操作调试器的人是同一个人（调试时通常如此），那么无论哪种情况，UB 都是他们自己的责任，因此在这种情况下，我看不出 yeet1 和 yeet2 有什么实质区别。
所以，假设你现在仍然主张优先采用 yeet1 而不是 yeet2，你究竟想通过这样做解决什么问题？

调试期间，程序显然可能存在 bug。这没问题。yeet2 只会说——是的，你的程序仍然有 bug。仅仅添加断点并不会修复这个 bug。这样有什么问题？

messages.en: it's not correct that what yeet2 proponents want to have happen implies a known not-to-be-buggy program
messages.zh: 认为 yeet2 的支持者希望发生的事情意味着程序已知没有 bug，这种说法并不正确。

messages.en: it is a bit simplisitc to categorize programs into just 2 buckets, "buggy" and "non-buggy". a program can be buggy for some inputs but non-buggy for others. (we'd still call that "buggy" overall but the distinction can matter.) a program can be buggy when the user inputs "1" on the terminal, and non-buggy if they input "0". or for this discussion, a program can be buggy when the breakpoint is continued but non-buggy if the breakpoint is aborted. in either case, it was always part of the Rust compiler correctness contract that even if one of those cases is UB, the other case must behave correctly.
messages.zh: 把程序简单地分成“有 bug”和“没有 bug”这两类，有点过于简单了。程序可能对某些输入有 bug，但对另一些输入没有。（总体上我们仍然会称其为“有 bug”，但这种区分可能很重要。）比如，用户在终端输入“1”时程序可能有 bug，而输入“0”时则没有。或者就这次讨论而言，继续执行断点时程序可能有 bug，而 abort 断点时则没有。无论是哪种情况，Rust 编译器正确性契约一直都要求：即使其中一种情况会导致 UB，另一种情况也必须正确运行。

messages.en: My argument is that it's perfectly valid for someone to define a version of assert that uses a breakpoint instruction rather than a panic. Which is useful if you want something compact and usable in a no_std context, and as a bonus is convenient for getting a backtrace about the "shouldn't happen" condition that just happened. If you continue from that point without thinking about it, you may encounter the code the assert guarded against.
messages.zh: 我的论点是，有人使用断点指令而不是恐慌来定义断言版本是完全有效的。如果您想要在no_std上下文中紧凑且可用的东西，这很有用，并且作为奖励，可以方便地获得有关刚刚发生的“不应该发生”情况的回溯。如果您从这一点继续而不考虑它，您可能会遇到断言防范的代码。

messages.en: It is valid to do that with an `asm!("int3")` if you're not portable. It would be nice to have the portable equivalent when available, so that people are not tempted to write the non-portable version.
messages.zh: 使用以下方式进行此操作是有效的：`asm!("int3")`如果你不是便携式的。如果有可用的便携式版本，那就太好了，这样人们就不会想要编写非便携式版本。

messages.en: Hitting "continue" in a debugger after a breakpoint is like taking a program that accepts filenames and giving it `/proc/self/mem`. Once you're in a debugger, and do something to modify the control flow of the program from what it would have been *without* a debugger, the correct operation of the program is now your responsibility.
messages.zh: 在断点后在调试器中点击“继续”就像拿一个接受文件名的程序并给它`/proc/self/mem`。一旦你进入调试器，并做一些事情来修改程序的控制流，从*没有*调试器，程序的正确操作现在是你的责任。

messages.en: It may be *useful* for a library to make breakpoints continuable, or non-continuable, or not ship them at all. (That last one will by far be the most common case.) It may be *useful* to have any number of different tracing or logging or error-message conventions, too. None of those should be mandated.
messages.zh: 对于库来说，使断点具有连续性、不可持续性或根本不运送断点可能是*有用的*。（到目前为止，最后一种将是最常见的情况。）拥有任意数量的不同跟踪或日志记录或错误消息约定也可能是*有用的*。所有这些都不应得到授权。

messages.en: I would ask what we *gain* by such a mandate, compared to what we *lose*.
messages.zh: 我会问，与我们*失去*的东西相比，我们通过这样的授权*获得*了什么。

@_**Josh Triplett|239881** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622821051):
```quote
My argument is that it's perfectly valid for someone to define a version of assert that uses a breakpoint instruction rather than a panic. Which is useful if you want something compact and usable in a no_std context, and as a bonus is convenient for getting a backtrace about the "shouldn't happen" condition that just happened. If you continue from that point without thinking about it, you may encounter the code the assert guarded against.
```

I'm not sure I agree that it's perfectly valid. It can be fine in some cases I suppose, but the reality is that this *is* a feature that exists and it's so intrinsic to the functionality of the debugger that I think it falls on the program that wants to do it to contend with (and document) the fact that they're doing something odd.

To be clear: People can do this if they want, but as I suggested above, they're taking it upon themselves to apply and document this extra safety requirement for running their program: you must not use a debugger to continue past a breakpoint. There's nothing wrong with a given program having additional safety requirements beyond what Rust provides (we often call this "outside the model"); this is how programs like ripgrep can support mmaping files without it being a violation of Rust's rules. If you do something like this, you are just supposed to communicate to the user what your additional requirements are, such as not truncating certain files, or not stepping in a debugger.

@_**Thom Chiovoloni|209168** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622834312):
```quote
I do still sorta think `yeet2(); black_box(abort as fn())()` kinda still works for that. But I don't think it's the case either of these functions is more portable than the other. I think both permit lowering to `abort_immediate()` or `loop {}` (in practice `yeet2` probably permits lowering to a noop if that's *truly* all that can be done).
```

The fact that `yeet2` permits lowering to a no-op is precisely why I'm arguing against it. I'm not saying I've *never* seen an architecture that has no way to crash, but I've never seen one we're likely to port Rust to. And if you have a way to crash, you have a way to implement `breakpoint()`, as a fallback if there's no explicit breakpoint instruction.

messages.en: You *can* write a handler that explicitly ignores it, though. But it's a bad idea unless you know it's valid for all breakpoints in your program. Anti-debugger methods, to the extent they're legitimate, are essentially saying "we assert that there should never be a breakpoint instruction in this program (because if one is there it means someone's trying to debug us, which we don't want to allow)".

messages.en: Leaving aside race conditions on signal dispositions, `signal(SIGTRAP, SIG_IGN); raise(SIGTRAP);` is a valid way to spell "let this breakpoint be explicitly ignorable".
