messages.en:
TL;DR of the last times this argument was had:
* Rust code can not read a `u8` (or whatever other type) from uninitialized memory. You can read a `MaybeUninit` but there is no way to get "out of" that MaybeUninit. If you try to with unsafe code, you get UB. It is just *not* a "thing Rust can do" :tm: 
* Rust code can generate non-deterministic values. For example via concurrency (two threads atomically increment some counter, who will be first?). So non-determinism is already a "thing Rust can do" :tm: 
* There is a proposal for adding a `freeze` primitive to `MaybeUninit` which will probably copy the `MaybeUninit` and return a new one where all bytes that were uninitialized now hold a non-deterministic. This would then make such an operation a "thing Rust can do" :tm: So far that's not accepted.
* When you write `asm!` blocks, the ASM block is only allowed to do "things Rust can do" :tm: as far as the visible behavior for the rest of the program is concerned. The ASM block can produce output as a side-effect (which is not something the Rust abstract machine really cares about) or it can modify memory the same way Rust does. But in the latter case, the modifications must be explainable as being some "thing Rust can do" :tm: 
* You can state that your `asm!` block that reads an uninitialized value just returns something non-deterministic, and then you get a non-deterministic choice (a "thing Rust can do" :tm: already, but the ASM block might implement it more efficiently or whatever). But it cannot "return non-det only when the byte was uninit" because that is not a "thing Rust can do" :tm: 
* Your ASM block can read memory and then ignore the result as well because this is also a "thing Rust can do" :tm: (Rust could have read it as a `MaybeUninit`). But the key point is that whatever function your `asm!` blocks implement must be composed from "things Rust can do" :tm: 

Since `freeze` is currently not a "thing Rust can do" :tm: you can also not approximate it with assembly instructions. The compiler could be relying on the `asm!` not being able to freeze the memory and therefore optimize the surrounding code with that knowledge. In practice, it will not, but this is `t-opsem` not `t-in-practice` because we try to do better than such kind of reasoning (like which compiler optimizations do and do not happen).
messages.zh:
前几次争论的简要总结：
* Rust 代码不能从未初始化内存读取 `u8`（或其他任何类型）。你可以读取 `MaybeUninit`，但无法从这个 MaybeUninit 中“取出”值。如果用 unsafe 代码尝试，就会发生 UB。它就是不属于“Rust 能做的事情” :tm:。
* Rust 代码可以生成非确定性值。例如通过并发（两个线程以原子方式递增同一个计数器，谁会先执行？）。所以非确定性已经属于“Rust 能做的事情” :tm:。
* 有人提议为 `MaybeUninit` 增加 `freeze` 原语。它大概会复制该 `MaybeUninit`，返回一个新的值，其中所有原先未初始化的字节如今都包含一个非确定性值。这样，这种操作就会成为“Rust 能做的事情” :tm:。但目前尚未接受该提议。
* 编写 `asm!` 块时，就程序其余部分可见的行为而言，ASM 块只能做“Rust 能做的事情” :tm:。ASM 块可以通过副作用产生输出（Rust 抽象机器实际上并不太关心这一点），也可以像 Rust 一样修改内存。但在后一种情况下，这些修改必须能解释为某种“Rust 能做的事情” :tm:。
* 你可以声明：读取未初始化值的 `asm!` 块只是返回一个非确定性值，这样你便获得一次非确定性选择（它已经是“Rust 能做的事情” :tm:，只是 ASM 块可能实现得更高效之类）。但它不能“仅在字节未初始化时才返回非确定性值”，因为这不是“Rust 能做的事情” :tm:。
* ASM 块也可以读取内存然后忽略结果，因为这也是“Rust 能做的事情” :tm:（Rust 可以将其作为 `MaybeUninit` 读取）。但关键在于，`asm!` 块实现的任何函数都必须由“Rust 能做的事情” :tm: 组合而成。

由于 `freeze` 目前不是“Rust 能做的事情” :tm:，因此也不能用汇编指令来近似实现它。编译器可能依赖 `asm!` 无法冻结内存这一点，并据此优化周围代码。实际上它不会这样做，但这里是 `t-opsem`，不是 `t-in-practice`，因为我们试图超越这种推理方式（例如讨论哪些编译器优化实际会发生、哪些不会）。

messages.en:
moreso, even, that T-opsem is the one arguing for doing or not doing optimizations because of its soundness, as it were, so it cannot shrug and delegate the authority of "what optimizations *should be able to happen*".
( `t-compiler` of course is `t-in-practice` lol. )
messages.zh:
更进一步，T-opsem 正是依据可靠性来主张应当或不应当做某种优化的一方，所以它不能耸耸肩，把“*应当允许进行哪些优化*”的决定权交给别人。
（当然，`t-compiler` 就是 `t-in-practice`，哈哈。）

messages.zh: C 可以通过位域写入单独的位（即便是未初始化值中的位），而不触碰其他位，但这不是 Rust 能做的事情。

messages.en: does that mean if i call a c function that does this through ffi, my program may (theoretically) compile to nonsense, through the compiler assuming that uninit is something that applies to full bytes only?

messages.en: the rest of the byte is still uninit as far as c is concerned

messages.en: C's bitfields are specced to operate on "storage units" in such a way that gives the compiler liberty to update the entire storage unit in place when a bitfield is written because that is how it must be for many ISAs.
messages.zh: C 的位域规范规定它们作用于“存储单元”，并允许编译器在写入位域时就地更新整个存储单元，因为许多 ISA 必须这样实现。

messages.en: ( and bitfields are not allowed to overlap with other fields. )
messages.zh: （而且位域不允许与其他字段重叠。）

messages.en: so there is no reason to add the implementation complexity of bit-level uninit just because of bitfields (assuming freeze exists)
messages.zh: 所以没必要仅仅因为位域，就增加位级未初始化状态的实现复杂度（假定 freeze 存在）。

yes. Rust has byte-level granularity for uninit. When you call C code you need to tell a story, and a story you can tell is that wherever C code returns a byte that has uninit'ed bits, then the byte is wholly uninit in Rust. Copying it around might not preserve the individual bits (except in practice, they do, I guess, because LLVM does the optimizations and uninit bits are a "thing LLVM can do" (I think). Don't ask me about other backends :stuck_out_tongue: ).

@_**Max|960514** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/the.20freeze.20discussion.20vMax/near/636722489):
```quote
so when I interact with some funny posix implementation that does this to an opaque struct that we model as `MaybeUninit<[u8; ...]>`, i may silently lose data on the rust side? (theoretically, from an opsem perspective)
```

I still think the problem with the bit field topic that you're trying to tell a Rust story in terms of the bitwise-uninit model of the C AM. Yes, you cannot define an operation like "set the i-th bit of this byte to a value and leave the other bits uninit if they were uninit before" because the concept of "uninit bits" does not compute. What you should do instead is tell a story where every byte is either fully initialized (possibly with some non-det choices for bits that from the C/LLVM POV would be uninit) or fully uninitialized. When it matters that the C side initialized some bit fields, the story says that the FFI call initialized all bytes that contain that bitfield. For the other bytes that don't matter, you can pick any story you like (as long as it's consistent with the actual behavior of the machine code).

That's not a full fidelity representation of what the C side thinks it's doing. If you tried to give a combined account of Rust AM + C AM, you'd arrive at the conclusion that "pass a bitfield type from C to Rust and pass it back to C unmodified" would be either UB or a "lossy" (freezing-ish) operation, depending on how you try to make the respective memory models get along. But trying to mash two AMs together like that leads to madness, and is unnecessary. They never meet directly. If both are compiled to concrete machine code, both can look at the same concrete machine state and see their respective AM state reflected in it (just with different stories).

You do get into trouble with this approach when doing cross-language LTO because LLVM IR is also an abstract machine and it doesn't see the language boundary as an AM-CM boundary. But as Ralf said in the earlier thread, for cross-language LTO you don't need FFI/asm storytelling, you need to deal with the LLVM AM and how your Rust and C programs got translated into it, which is also far outside t-opsem (and outside of language specs more generally).

@_**Max|960514** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/the.20freeze.20discussion.20vMax/near/636722489):
```quote
所以，如果我与某个古怪的 POSIX 实现交互，它对我们建模为 `MaybeUninit<[u8; ...]>` 的不透明结构体做了这种操作，我可能在 Rust 这边悄悄丢失数据？（理论上，从操作语义角度看。）
```

我仍然认为，位域讨论的问题在于，你试图根据 C AM 的逐位未初始化模型，来讲述 Rust 的叙述。没错，你无法定义“把此字节的第 i 位设为某个值，而其他原先未初始化的位仍保持未初始化”这样的操作，因为“未初始化位”这个概念在这里说不通。你应该换一种叙述：每个字节要么完全初始化（对于 C/LLVM 看来未初始化的位，可能有一些非确定性选择），要么完全未初始化。如果 C 一侧初始化某些位域这件事很重要，叙述就说该 FFI 调用初始化了包含该位域的所有字节。对于其他无关字节，你可以选择任何叙述（只要与机器代码的实际行为一致）。

这并不是对 C 一侧自认为正在做什么的完全忠实表示。如果试图联合描述 Rust AM 和 C AM，你就会得出：“把位域类型从 C 传给 Rust，再原样传回 C”要么是 UB，要么是“有损”（类似冻结）的操作，具体取决于你如何尝试协调两者的内存模型。但试图如此硬凑两个 AM 会让人发疯，也没有必要。它们从不直接碰面。如果两者都编译为具体机器代码，它们都可以观察同一具体机器状态，并在其中看到各自 AM 状态的反映（只是叙述不同）。

进行跨语言 LTO 时，这种方法确实会遇到问题，因为 LLVM IR 也是抽象机器，它不把语言边界视为 AM-CM 边界。但正如 Ralf 在之前讨论中说的，跨语言 LTO 不需要 FFI/asm 叙述，而是需要处理 LLVM AM，以及 Rust 和 C 程序如何被转换到其中；这也远远超出了 t-opsem（以及一般语言规范）的范围。

It only needs to choose after the environment chose/committed to `f`. Either `f` must hit UB if I pass in uninit, in which case I choose `b` false, and the optimised program refines because after UB I can do anything (including panicking), or the output of `f` is independent of the input, in which case I choose `b` true, and can optimise away the dead write (dead because it will never be read; the branch *is* taken).

它只需要在环境选定／确定 `f` 之后作出选择。要么传入未初始化值时 `f` 必然遇到 UB，此时我选择 `b` 为 false，优化后的程序满足精化关系，因为 UB 后我可以做任何事（包括 panic）；要么 `f` 的输出独立于输入，此时我选择 `b` 为 true，就能优化掉死写入（它是死写入，因为永远不会被读取；分支*确实会*执行）。

I don't think that optimization is valid. If `b` happens to be picked as `true`, then the write to `x` has to be preserved as `f` may be reading it. If `b` happens to be picked as `false`, then for that particular story of `f` where `x` is read from, you did just get UB. The compiler doesn't get to pick which story an asm block has. It has to optimize under the assumption that it may be any story for which there would not be UB for some input.

@_**Max|960514** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/the.20freeze.20discussion.20vMax/near/636898796):
```quote
`f` doesn't see `b`. The compiler may assume that the behavior of `f` does not depend on `b`, and therefore it does not inspect `x`
```

I don't think you can argue that way. I would think the compiler has to optimize under the assumption that each possible story may have been the correct one. So it has to do optimizations that are correct for the case where `f` returns the argument and has UB on uninit and for the case where `f` doesn't look at the argument at all. The suggested transformation is not valid for the former possible story and thus the compiler is not allowed to do that transformation.
messages.zh:
@_**Max|960514** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/the.20freeze.20discussion.20vMax/near/636898796):
```quote
`f` 看不到 `b`。编译器可以假定 `f` 的行为不依赖 `b`，因此它不会检查 `x`。
```

我认为不能这样论证。我觉得编译器必须假定每个可能的叙述都可能是正确的，并据此优化。因此，它的优化既必须适用于 `f` 返回参数、参数未初始化就触发 UB 的情况，也必须适用于 `f` 完全不查看参数的情况。所提议的变换对前一种可能的叙述无效，因此编译器不能执行该变换。

messages.en: There's no story for `f`. It's a Rust function. The story is for its ASM block which may only access its parameter, after which it must be initialized. The function cannot assume its parameter to be initialized since it may be called with uninit (at the demon discretion). So the ASM story (which must be unique, but the compiler doesn't know which one of the possible stories it is) cannot read the function parameter since it cannot tell if it's initialized. If `b` was a global, then that optimization would be wrong (as long as the ASM options permit reading globals).
messages.zh: `f` 没有叙述。它是 Rust 函数。叙述属于其中的 ASM 块，而该块只能访问参数，并且在块结束后参数必须已初始化。函数不能假定参数已初始化，因为调用时可能传入未初始化值（由恶魔决定）。因此，ASM 的叙述（必须唯一，但编译器不知道它是哪种可能的叙述）不能读取函数参数，因为无法判断参数是否已初始化。如果 `b` 是全局变量，那么这个优化就是错误的（只要 ASM 选项允许读取全局变量）。

topics.name: Opsem of non-contiguous references
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：View types 允许多个 `&mut` 指向同一范围，但各自只能访问不相交的子范围；讨论重点是这类非连续引用是否应被视为普通“类型”，以及如何在 aliasing model 中处理 `retag`、`protector` 和后端属性。
- **主要方案**：由于 view types 只涉及 borrowck 已能区分的子对象（目前主要设想是 struct/enum fields，而非任意数组索引），可以让 `retag` 只作用于允许访问的 offset，无需让 pointer tree 本身支持非连续 provenance。若无法这样处理，则可能需要在 aliasing model 中将其按 raw pointers 对待。
- **LLVM 属性**：讨论认为仍可发出 `noalias`：不同 view 只要不访问同一 field，就符合 LLVM 对基于不同参数指针的访问限制。对于 `dereferenceable`，一方认为非连续区域可能需要截断到第一个 hole，或因 view types 是 `!Sized` 而不发出该属性；但另一方认为不应因此性能退化。随后又指出 `dereferenceable` 与 spurious loads、aliasing writes 的关系存在语义争议，Rust 侧可能意味着不能有别名写入。
- **padding**：普通 reference 通常允许访问 fields 之间的 padding，而 view reference 只允许访问指定 fields。有人提出为优化允许访问连续 viewed fields 之间的 padding，或规定每个 field 负责其后的 padding；目前只认为应采用一致的规则，未确定具体方案。
- **已达成与未解决**：基本共识是按可访问 offset 修改 retag 比引入非连续 provenance 简单，且 `noalias` 看来可以保留；但 `dereferenceable` 的准确处理、padding 的归属及是否允许跨 viewed fields 访问仍未完全解决。

messages.en:
View types are starting to get experimented with ([project goal](https://goals.rust-lang.org/2026/view-types-experiment.html), cc @**Sasha Pourcelot (scrabsha)**). This allows having e.g. two `&mut` that point to the same range, but with access to only disjoint subranges.

I understand they'll be made `?Sized` (or some other marker) to prevent most operations on them, but we'll still want (non-contiguous) retags/protectors for them. How bad is that, opsemwise? Should they even count as "types", given that they're never read/written as a whole?
messages.zh:
视图类型开始进入实验阶段了（[项目目标](https://goals.rust-lang.org/2026/view-types-experiment.html)，抄送 @**Sasha Pourcelot (scrabsha)**）。它允许例如两个 `&mut` 指向同一范围，但各自只能访问互不重叠的子范围。

我理解，它们会被设为 `?Sized`（或使用其他标记），以阻止对其执行大多数操作，但我们仍然希望为它们提供（不连续的）重新打标／保护器。从操作语义看，这会有多麻烦？考虑到它们从不作为整体读写，甚至还应该算作“类型”吗？

messages.en: hi! i don't know much about opsem, and there's no entry in the unsafe code guidelines reference glossary about retags - what are they?
messages.zh: 你好！我不太了解操作语义，而不安全代码指南参考手册的术语表中也没有 retag（重新打标）的条目——它是什么？

messages.en: tried my best here: https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/652453-t-lang.2Fview-types/topic/Intro.20to.20the.20aliasing.20model/with/638110768
messages.zh: 我在这里尽力解释了一下：https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/652453-t-lang.2Fview-types/topic/Intro.20to.20the.20aliasing.20model/with/638110768

messages.en:
I mean, if you know which bytes you are (not) allowed to access, then the aliasing model can simply only retag on these offsets. Saying that a retag behaves like a different kind of retag on some bytes is one of the easiest things you can tweak about the aliasing model. The example in the project goal suggests that this will be the case (since it's just struct fields which have known offsets), but I have only skimmed the intro so I do not know what else is planned.

If this can not be done, one would need to treat such references as raw pointers in the aliasing model.
messages.zh:
我是说，如果知道允许（或不允许）访问哪些字节，别名模型就只对那些偏移进行重新打标即可。规定某些字节上的 retag 像另一种 retag 一样运作，是别名模型中最容易调整的事情之一。项目目标中的示例表明情况会是如此（因为那只是偏移已知的结构体字段），不过我只粗略看了介绍，不知道还有什么计划。

如果无法做到这一点，就需要在别名模型中把这样的引用视为裸指针。

messages.en:
@_**Johannes Hostert|495238** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Opsem.20of.20non-contiguous.20references/near/638114774):
```quote
since it's just struct fields which have known offsets
```

struct field offsets may not be known statically because `dyn` tails, but I guess this doesn't change much
messages.zh:
@_**Johannes Hostert|495238** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Opsem.20of.20non-contiguous.20references/near/638114774):
```quote
因为那只是偏移已知的结构体字段
```

由于 `dyn` 尾部，结构体字段偏移未必能静态获知，但我猜这不会改变太多。

messages.en: I think that's basically it, view types will only be about subplaces that borrowck already knows how to distinguish, so struct/enum fields at most I imagine. I would not want array view types that borrow only chosen indices ^^
messages.zh: 我认为基本就是这样。视图类型只涉及 borrowck 已经知道如何区分的子位置，所以我想最多就是结构体／枚举字段。我不希望有只借用选定索引的数组视图类型 ^^

messages.en: the other question is whether the added complexity in the aliasing model is worth it: Are we still able to emit `noalias`? The answer is **yes**, I think, because we can make the holes behave like we already make out-of-bounds accesses do, and for these `noalias` is also sound. But for something like `dereferenceable` we might need to cap it at "the first hole" because `dereferenceable` is "continuous" and does not like holes.
messages.zh: 另一个问题是，给别名模型增加这份复杂度是否值得：我们还能生成 `noalias` 吗？我认为答案是**能**，因为可以让空洞的行为类似于我们已经规定的越界访问行为，而对于后者，`noalias` 也是可靠的。不过，对于 `dereferenceable` 之类的属性，可能需要把范围限制在“第一个空洞”之前，因为 `dereferenceable` 要求“连续”，不喜欢空洞。

messages.en: So whoever implements this can have fun thinking about this when going into the backend :smiling_imp:
messages.zh: 所以，实现它的人深入后端时，就可以享受思考这些问题的乐趣了 :smiling_imp:

messages.en: we plan to make views `!Sized`, so AIUI we could quite simply never emit `dereferenceable`. would that work?
messages.zh: 我们计划让视图是 `!Sized`，因此据我理解，可以很简单地始终不生成 `dereferenceable`。这样可行吗？

messages.en: I think we do want dereferencable, there's no reason to pessimize view types there.
messages.zh: 我认为确实需要 dereferenceable，没有理由在这里让视图类型的优化变差。

messages.en: Note that dereferencable only requires that memory accesses not fault. It still permits concurrents/aliasing writes.
messages.zh: 注意，dereferenceable 只要求内存访问不会触发故障。它仍允许并发／别名写入。

messages.en:
LLVM Langref definition of `noalias`:

> This indicates that memory locations accessed via pointer values [based](https://llvm.org/docs/LangRef.html#pointeraliasing) on the argument or return value are not also accessed, during the execution of the function, via pointer values not *based* on the argument or return value.
messages.zh:
LLVM Langref 对 `noalias` 的定义：

> 这表示：在函数执行期间，通过[基于](https://llvm.org/docs/LangRef.html#pointeraliasing)该参数或返回值的指针值所访问的内存位置，不会同时通过*不基于*该参数或返回值的指针值访问。

messages.en: So as long as you don't access the same field from both pointers you're fine.
messages.zh: 所以，只要不通过两个指针访问同一个字段，就没问题。

messages.en: :o very cool
messages.zh: :o 太酷了

messages.en:
@_**Amanieu d'Antras|143274** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Opsem.20of.20non-contiguous.20references/near/638152771):
```quote
LLVM Langref definition of `noalias`:

> This indicates that memory locations accessed via pointer values [based](https://llvm.org/docs/LangRef.html#pointeraliasing) on the argument or return value are not also accessed, during the execution of the function, via pointer values not *based* on the argument or return value.
```

with the restriction that no restrictions apply until somebody writes (which is why shared references are also `noalias` in the usual circumstances: nobody writes). So you can imagine having references that are mutable for some fields and shared for some others and it's still `noalias`. But I digress
messages.zh:
@_**Amanieu d'Antras|143274** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Opsem.20of.20non-contiguous.20references/near/638152771):
```quote
LLVM Langref 对 `noalias` 的定义：

> 这表示：在函数执行期间，通过[基于](https://llvm.org/docs/LangRef.html#pointeraliasing)该参数或返回值的指针值所访问的内存位置，不会同时通过*不基于*该参数或返回值的指针值访问。
```

还要加一个限制：在有人写入之前，不施加任何限制（因此，共享引用在通常情况下也是 `noalias`：没有人写入）。所以可以设想一种引用，对某些字段是可变的，对其他字段是共享的，它仍然是 `noalias`。不过我扯远了。

messages.en:
> Note that dereferencable only requires that memory accesses not fault. It still permits concurrents/aliasing writes.

This is not true. Interaction of noalias with spurious loads on the LLVM side is an unsolved semantics problem, but I believe on the Rust side it's basically "dereferenceable implies spurious read", so you can't have an aliasing write.
messages.zh:
> 注意，dereferenceable 只要求内存访问不会触发故障。它仍允许并发／别名写入。

这不正确。LLVM 一侧 noalias 与额外引入的加载如何交互，仍是尚未解决的语义问题。但我认为在 Rust 一侧，基本上是“dereferenceable 意味着可能额外读取”，所以不能有别名写入。

messages.en:
@_**Johannes Hostert|495238** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Opsem.20of.20non-contiguous.20references/near/638114774):
```quote
the aliasing model can simply only retag on these offsets
```

yeah ok I was worried we might need the pointer tree itself to have a notion of non-contiguous provenance. changing retags sounds a billion times simpler
messages.zh:
@_**Johannes Hostert|495238** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Opsem.20of.20non-contiguous.20references/near/638114774):
```quote
别名模型就只对那些偏移进行重新打标即可
```

好吧，我原本担心可能需要让指针树本身具有不连续指针来源的概念。修改 retag 听起来简单太多了。

messages.en: :vi_fon: astonishingly this opsem thread is small enough still to skim but am I missing something or does this apply to all structs with padding and isn't actually anything new?
messages.zh: :vi_fon: 真令人惊讶，这个操作语义讨论还短得可以快速浏览。不过是我漏了什么，还是这适用于所有带填充的结构体，实际上并不是什么新东西？

messages.en: A normal reference gives you permission to access padding between fields. A view reference only allows access to a specific set of fields.
messages.zh: 普通引用赋予你访问字段之间填充区域的权限。视图引用只允许访问一组特定字段。

messages.en: right, I guess that you technically still have permission to access the padding, it's just uninit
messages.zh: 对，我想严格来说，你确实仍然有权限访问填充，只是它未初始化。

messages.en:
it might be good, for optimization purposes, to allow access to padding between consecutively viewed fields

cc @**waffle** (sitting next to me, who theorized this)
messages.zh:
从优化角度看，允许访问连续可见字段之间的填充，可能会很好。

抄送 @**waffle**（坐在我旁边，是他提出这个设想的）。

messages.en: or perhaps easier: each field owns the padding that comes right after it (or something similar)
messages.zh: 或者也许更简单：每个字段拥有紧随其后的填充（或类似规则）。

messages.en: as long as a consistent choice is made, I don't see a problem with that
messages.zh: 只要选择保持一致，我看不出有什么问题。

messages.en:
@_**Clar Fon|330161** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Opsem.20of.20non-contiguous.20references/near/638251194):
```quote
right, I guess that you technically still have permission to access the padding, it's just uninit
```

you could very well read/write to it, e.g. if you cast a `&mut u64` to `&mut (u8, u16)` the padding is fine
messages.zh:
@_**Clar Fon|330161** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Opsem.20of.20non-contiguous.20references/near/638251194):
```quote
对，我想严格来说，你确实仍然有权限访问填充，只是它未初始化。
```

你完全可以读写它，例如，把 `&mut u64` 转换为 `&mut (u8, u16)` 时，填充就没有问题。

topics.name: linker section slice iteration
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：通过 `START`/`END` 两个外部 ZST static 标记 linker section 的边界，并从 Rust 中遍历其中的 `usize`；但若同一程序用 `#[link_section]` 和 `#[used]` 放入 `MY_PART`，就会出现通过 `START` 访问与 `MY_PART` 重叠内存的情况。问题在于 Rust/LLVM 是否允许这种“手动合并”不同 static 的做法。
- **主要观点**：讨论者倾向于将这些对象视为**逻辑上不同的 allocations，只是物理字节范围重叠**；只要是只读数据，通常不会产生可变内存的 aliasing 问题，provenance 仍然保持区分。RalfJ 认为这类似 `unnamed_addr` allocation 的重叠，但不希望因此普遍改变 Rust 对 statics 不重叠的保证。
- **LLVM 方面的风险**：LLVM 当前通常假设非 `unnamed_addr` globals 不重叠，并且对 global definition 越界访问视为 UB；如果 LLVM 根据“来自不同 static”推断指针地址必不相等，可能错误优化 `icmp`。Nikita Popov 表示 immutable globals 的 aliasing 可能没问题，但 provenance、越界访问和地址假设仍需明确；相关 LLVM PR 尚未确定是否合入。
- **可能的约束方案**：可将该模式限制在专用 linker sections 中，避免与编译器正常使用的 section 混用；也有人提出要求重叠 static 内容完全相等，或通过专门的语法/attribute 显式标记。不过直接使用 `unnamed_addr` 被认为可能导致 LLVM 复制或去重，从而破坏 linker-section 语义；`#[used]` 的作用也更接近阻止合并，而不是允许合并。另有观点认为 `#[link_section]` 不应自动赋予“可通过一个 static 访问邻接 static”的语义。
- **仍未解决的问题**：尚未形成 Rust 语言层面的正式规范，也未确认 LLVM 是否会正式支持 immutable statics 的这种重叠及相应地址语义；`START`/`END` 声明、重叠范围和 provenance 的精确定义，以及是否需要专门的 Rust 表达形式，仍待进一步讨论和 LLVM 文档/变更支持。

messages.en: I wonder if we could say that in general, read-only allocations can arbitrarily overlap?
messages.zh: 我在想，能否一般性地规定，只读分配可以任意重叠？

messages.en: that might also help with the allocation deduplication issues we had
messages.zh: 这也可能有助于解决我们之前遇到的分配去重问题。

messages.en: they can overlap as long as there's some suitable refinement relation between the bytes stored at the same address
messages.zh: 只要同一地址存储的字节之间存在某种合适的精化关系，它们就可以重叠。

messages.en: I feel like that matches most people's intuition
messages.zh: 我感觉这符合大多数人的直觉。

messages.en: Note that one common case of this will be putting function pointers into the section, and then iterating over them and calling them.
messages.zh: 注意，这里的一个常见用例是把函数指针放进这个节，然后迭代并调用它们。

messages.en: Yeah... hopefully `#[used]` actually works everywhere now...
messages.zh: 是啊……希望现在 `#[used]` 真的能在所有地方工作了……

messages.en: Being able to merge read-only statics would be nice for the deduplication, but I'm a bit worried that it could break real unsafe code that relies on the "non-ZST statics don't overlap" property for shenanigans. I don't have any specific code in mind, but I also can't convince myself it's likely to be a non-issue.
messages.zh: 能够合并只读 static 会有利于去重，但我有点担心，它可能破坏真实的不安全代码：那些代码依赖“非 ZST 的 static 不重叠”这个性质来玩一些技巧。我想不出具体代码，但也无法说服自己这大概率不是问题。

messages.en: I think we should still guarantee that we dont merge statics
messages.zh: 我认为仍应保证不会合并 static。

messages.en: this is about the user "manually" merging statics
messages.zh: 这里讨论的是用户“手动”合并 static。

messages.en: by doing linker shenanigans
messages.zh: 通过一些链接器技巧。

messages.en: doesn't LLVM already sometimes merge statics? i remember a case of [0; N] and [uninit; N] having the same address?
messages.zh: LLVM 不是已经有时会合并 static 了吗？我记得有个 `[0; N]` 和 `[uninit; N]` 地址相同的例子？

messages.en: that was for consts, not statics
messages.zh: 那是 const，不是 static。

messages.en: we mark those as `unnamed_addr`
messages.zh: 我们把它们标记为 `unnamed_addr`。

messages.en: which permits merging
messages.zh: 这就允许合并。

messages.en: ah okay, whoops, makes sense
messages.zh: 啊，好吧，搞错了，这就说得通了。

messages.en: we dont do that for statics
messages.zh: 对 static，我们不这样做。

messages.en: the immediate concern here is whether LLVM is okay with people manually merging their immutable statics
messages.zh: 眼下关心的是，LLVM 是否接受用户手动合并不可变 static。

messages.en: from the Rust side I dont see a fundamental problem. provenance still remains in force, these allocations are logically distinct even if they share the byte representation.
messages.zh: 从 Rust 一侧看，我看不出根本性问题。指针来源仍然有效，即便共享字节表示，这些分配在逻辑上仍彼此独立。

messages.en: but if LLVM does reasoning like "well those two statics both have size 4 so their addresses must be at least 4 apart" we might be in trouble
messages.zh: 但如果 LLVM 推理说“这两个 static 的大小都是 4，所以地址至少相差 4”，我们可能就有麻烦了。

messages.en: (though in this specific case one has size 0 so that wouldnt even apply)
messages.zh: （不过这个具体例子里有一个大小为 0，所以甚至不适用。）

messages.en: Oh, hm, I guess that's possible because both statics that can be merged need to opt in somehow. Unless the "linker section slice" happens to point at the section that we normally put statics in. Which is probably UB anyway, and we can probably also outlaw it explicitly (under the "don't throw a wrench in normal compiler operation" rule).
messages.zh: 哦，嗯，我想这应该可行，因为两个可合并的 static 都必须以某种方式选择加入。除非这个“链接器节切片”恰好指向我们通常存放 static 的节。但那大概本来就是 UB，我们大概也可以明确禁止（依据“不要破坏编译器正常运作”的规则）。

messages.en: but, like, "you did a 4-byte load from static A  and that is different from static B so their addresses must be at least 4 apart" is something one could imagine LLVM doing
messages.zh: 不过，完全可以想象 LLVM 会做这样的推理：“你从 static A 加载了 4 个字节，而 A 不同于 static B，所以它们的地址至少相差 4。”

messages.en: and we want it to not do that as it would break this (apparently common) pattern
messages.zh: 而我们希望它别这样做，否则会破坏这种（看来很常见的）模式。

messages.en: Like, it would be bad if I defined a private `static SENTINEL: u8 = 0;` and did shenanigans with that, and anyone else can create a static that overlaps `SENTINEL` and give me a pointer to that other static with different provenance. But the easy answer to that is "don't do that".
messages.zh: 比如，如果我定义一个私有的 `static SENTINEL: u8 = 0;`，并用它玩一些技巧，而其他任何人都能创建一个与 `SENTINEL` 重叠的 static，再给我一个指向那个 static、具有不同指针来源的指针，那就很糟糕。不过，简单答案就是“别这样做”。

messages.en: yeah I think we can assume that these must be dedicated linker sections that the compiler wouldn't usually use
messages.zh: 对，我认为可以假定这些必须是专用链接器节，编译器通常不会使用它们。

messages.en:
Would this discussion also cover the defmt case, where iirc only the address is used as an ID, the actual data is never included in the binary? Or is that a separate case?

(Defmt being an embedded logging framework that puts logging strings into a section that never ends up on the target, but a host program can read the full file to figure which log message each ID corresponds to)
messages.zh:
这个讨论也涵盖 defmt 的情况吗？如果没记错，那里只把地址用作 ID，实际数据根本不会放进二进制文件？还是说那属于另一种情况？

（Defmt 是嵌入式日志框架，会把日志字符串放进一个最终不会出现在目标设备上的节，但主机程序可以读取完整文件，确定每个 ID 对应哪条日志消息。）

messages.en: I hope it's unaffected by this discussion (my understanding is that here we look at whether the language authorizes the user to merge allocations, while for defmt we want the language to guarantee it doesn't merge statics). For reference, https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/554 describes this defmt case
messages.zh: 我希望它不受这次讨论影响（我的理解是，这里讨论语言是否允许用户合并分配，而对于 defmt，我们希望语言保证不会合并 static）。供参考，https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/554 描述了 defmt 的情况。

messages.en: For defmt the respective section is never iterated on at runtime. It is only read by external programs. Defmt is completely fine with non-overlapping statics. If anything it would break on overlap.
messages.zh: 对于 defmt，运行时从不迭代对应的节，只有外部程序会读取。Defmt 完全接受不重叠的 static。真要说的话，重叠反而会破坏它。

messages.en: Could we require that statics put inside the linker section are actually unnamed_addr (roughly)? That would sort of "bless" the merging operation and presumably make it less likely to go wrong in LLVM...?
messages.zh: 我们能否要求放进该链接器节的 static 实际上具有 unnamed_addr（大致如此）？这样可以算是“认可”合并操作，而且大概也能减少 LLVM 中出错的可能……？

messages.en: At least the overlapping ones. The start/end probably can't be, though if they are ZST overlap is a little ill-defined anyway.
messages.zh: 至少让重叠的那些如此。不过起点／终点大概不能这样，尽管如果它们是 ZST，重叠本来就有些定义不清。

messages.en: I wonder if `#[used]` should imply that non-mergeability and non-unnamed-addr, since it clearly means you're doing something "clever" with it.
messages.zh: 我在想，`#[used]` 是否应该意味着不可合并、没有 unnamed_addr，因为它显然意味着你正在对它做某种“巧妙”的操作。

messages.en:
@_**simulacrum|116122** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/linker.20section.20slice.20iteration/near/633809337):
```quote
Could we require that statics put inside the linker section are actually unnamed_addr (roughly)? That would sort of "bless" the merging operation and presumably make it less likely to go wrong in LLVM...?
```

I think using unnamed_addr for this would probably have bad consequences
messages.zh:
@_**simulacrum|116122** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/linker.20section.20slice.20iteration/near/633809337):
```quote
我们能否要求放进该链接器节的 static 实际上具有 unnamed_addr（大致如此）？这样可以算是“认可”合并操作，而且大概也能减少 LLVM 中出错的可能……？
```

我认为在这里使用 unnamed_addr 很可能产生糟糕的后果。

messages.en: unnamed_addr allows duplicating and deduplicating by LLVM, which is exactly what you don't want when mucking around with linker sections.
messages.zh: unnamed_addr 允许 LLVM 复制和去重，而折腾链接器节时，你恰恰不希望这样。

messages.en: It could cause a global constructor to run twice or two runs of the same global constructor to get deduplicated, which has observable effects.
messages.zh: 它可能导致某个全局构造函数运行两次，或者把同一全局构造函数的两次运行去重，这些都会产生可观察的影响。

messages.en: Ah, sorry, I got the polarity wrong there.
messages.zh: 啊，抱歉，我把方向弄反了。

messages.en: I was suggesting that marking something `#[used]` should give it the "you must *not* merge me" marking, which I guess is the *absence* of `unnamed_addr`.
messages.zh: 我的建议是，给某个对象标记 `#[used]`，就应该赋予它“你*不得*合并我”的标记；我想这其实对应于*没有* `unnamed_addr`。

messages.en: but anyway the main question here is whether LLVM is fine with immutable statics that overlap
messages.zh: 不过总之，这里的主要问题是 LLVM 是否接受重叠的不可变 static。

messages.en: So, as START needs to be able to access all parts and there is no multi-allocation provenance, I assume the underlying model here is that the actual allocation is at START, covering all parts, and the parts have provenance of START+offset?
messages.zh: 那么，既然 START 需要能访问所有部分，而且不存在多分配指针来源，我猜底层模型是：实际分配位于 START，覆盖所有部分，而各部分具有 START+offset 的指针来源？

messages.en: From an aliasing perspective, this would certainly be a no-go if these were mutable allocations. As you mention, immutable allocations do not alias in the first place, so that would probably be fine.
messages.zh: 从别名角度看，如果这些是可变分配，显然不可行。正如你提到的，不可变分配本来就不涉及别名问题，因此大概没问题。

messages.en: Though other provenance assumptions still play a role. For example, if you access *(MY_PART+sizeof(MY_PART)), is that supposed to work, because it's actually part of the larger START allocation? Or does MY_PART actually have your most favorite thing in the world (subobject provenance!) And if so, which kind (inbounds interaction?)
messages.zh: 但其他指针来源假设仍然起作用。例如，访问 `*(MY_PART+sizeof(MY_PART))` 时，是否应当可行，因为它实际上属于更大的 START 分配？还是 MY_PART 实际上具有你最喜欢的东西（子对象指针来源！）？如果有，又是哪种（与 inbounds 如何交互）？

messages.en: LLVM currently does assume that accessing a global definition out of bounds is UB.
messages.zh: LLVM 目前确实假定：对全局定义的越界访问是 UB。

messages.en: Now, the other part of the question would be about the addresses involved, rather than provenance. LLVM does currently assume that (non-unnamed_addr) globals do not overlap. This includes the case where one is a definition and the other a declaration. Of course, the declaration here is zero-size, so it would work out fine in practice. But generally the assumption is there.
messages.zh: 现在，问题的另一部分涉及相关地址，而非指针来源。LLVM 目前确实假定（非 unnamed_addr）全局对象不重叠。其中也包括一个是定义、另一个是声明的情况。当然，这里的声明大小为零，所以实践中没问题。但一般而言，这个假设确实存在。

messages.en: There's this PR (https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/229243) that proposes to change the handling of declarations, which may or may not land (it's certainly missing some LangRef changes...)
messages.zh: 有一个 PR（https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/229243）提议修改声明的处理方式，可能会合入，也可能不会（它显然还缺少一些 LangRef 修改……）。

messages.en: Though if you wanted to spec this, I think it would be curious to what extent you want to allow overlap. Would you say that arbitrary (subject to the refinement constraint) immutable allocations can overlap, so LLVM can't assume no-overlap even if it sees two *definitions*?
messages.zh: 不过，如果你想为此制定规范，我觉得值得问问，你究竟希望允许多大程度的重叠。是否要规定任意不可变分配都可以重叠（满足精化约束即可），因此即便 LLVM 看到了两个*定义*，也不能假定它们不重叠？

messages.en: One implication that I don't particularly like here is that this means we expand the scope of recently discussed issues around unnamed_addr (that you cannot conclude equal contents from an address comparison due to differences in poison-ness and provenance) from just the unnamed_addr case to all cases. (Ignoring the current possibility of merging unnamed_addr into non-unnamed_addr, which we likely want to forbid anyway.)
messages.zh: 这里有一个我不太喜欢的后果：这意味着，最近讨论的 unnamed_addr 问题（由于 poison 状态和指针来源不同，无法通过地址比较推断内容相等），会从仅限 unnamed_addr 的情况扩展到所有情况。（暂且忽略目前可以把 unnamed_addr 合并到非 unnamed_addr 中的可能性——反正我们大概也想禁止它。）

messages.en: My mental model is that if you use `#[link_section]` then the static isn't its own allocation, but is instead an offset within a larger allocation (which consists of the entire section). Statics without that attribute don't have this behavior.
messages.zh: 我的理解是：使用 `#[link_section]` 时，static 不再拥有独立分配，而是更大分配中的一个偏移（这个更大分配由整个节组成）。没有该属性的 static 不会具有这种行为。

messages.en: The start and end symbols are normally not declared with `#[link_section]`, so I don't think that is enough on it's own to make linker section iteration work.
messages.zh: 起点和终点符号通常不会用 `#[link_section]` 声明，因此我认为仅靠它还不足以让链接器节迭代成立。

messages.en: Why? Would it break something if they were declared that way?
messages.zh: 为什么？如果那样声明，会破坏什么吗？

messages.en:
`#[link_section]` is ignored on declarations.

```
warning: the `link_section` attribute cannot be used on foreign statics
 --> src/lib.rs:2:14
  |
2 |     #[unsafe(link_section = ".a")]
  |              ^^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = help: the `link_section` attribute can be applied to functions and statics
  = warning: this was previously accepted by the compiler but is being phased out; it will become a hard error in a future release!
  = note: `#[warn(unused_attributes)]` (part of `#[warn(unused)]`) on by default
```

messages.en: Huh, this is interesting. People already noticed the PR https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/229243 but it derives from the issue https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/222410 where C has apparently declared functions can compare equal in at least some cases, and it's no longer "some weird linker/ELF thing".
messages.zh: 咦，这很有意思。大家已经注意到 PR https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/229243，但它源自 issue https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/222410；看来 C 已经规定，至少在某些情况下，函数比较可以相等，所以这不再只是“某种古怪的链接器／ELF 行为”。

messages.en:
@_**Amanieu d'Antras|143274** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/linker.20section.20slice.20iteration/near/637783894):
```quote
My mental model is that if you use `#[link_section]` then the static isn't its own allocation, but is instead an offset within a larger allocation (which consists of the entire section). Statics without that attribute don't have this behavior.
```

I dont think we should allow such statics to be used to access neighboring statics in the same section. that'd be a much bigger change.
messages.zh:
@_**Amanieu d'Antras|143274** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/linker.20section.20slice.20iteration/near/637783894):
```quote
我的理解是：使用 `#[link_section]` 时，static 不再拥有独立分配，而是更大分配中的一个偏移（这个更大分配由整个节组成）。没有该属性的 static 不会具有这种行为。
```

我不认为应该允许通过这样的 static 访问同一节中相邻的 static。那会是大得多的变化。

messages.en:
@_**Nikita Popov|133224** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/linker.20section.20slice.20iteration/near/637777851):
```quote
One implication that I don't particularly like here is that this means we expand the scope of recently discussed issues around unnamed_addr (that you cannot conclude equal contents from an address comparison due to differences in poison-ness and provenance) from just the unnamed_addr case to all cases.
```

we could require that such overlapping statics must have fully equal contents, not just some sort of refinement
messages.zh:
@_**Nikita Popov|133224** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/linker.20section.20slice.20iteration/near/637777851):
```quote
这里有一个我不太喜欢的后果：这意味着，最近讨论的 unnamed_addr 问题（由于 poison 状态和指针来源不同，无法通过地址比较推断内容相等），会从仅限 unnamed_addr 的情况扩展到所有情况。
```

我们可以要求这些重叠 static 的内容必须完全相等，而不只是存在某种精化关系。

topics.name: Vibes on subobject provenance
topics.name_zh: 关于子对象来源追踪的一些看法
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：讨论 `&blah.foo` 创建的 reference 是否只能访问该 field 对应的字节，还是可以通过 raw pointer 等方式访问同一 allocation 中的其他字节；这直接影响 `&Header`、数组/切片、FFI 和 aliasing/优化语义。

- **支持 subobject provenance 的观点**：它可帮助 opaque/indirect call 后进行字段级优化，例如 `g(&mut b.buf); b.i` 可优化为已知值，也可能支持 enum discriminant 优化、MIR 中的 SRoA，以及让 reference 的访问范围更符合“只访问目标字节”的直觉。Mario Carneiro 等人认为这有助于形成更简单、可教学的模型，并希望未来仍保留这条演进路线。

- **反对或谨慎观点**：`&Header`、bindgen 生成的 flexible array member/FAM 模式、`repr(C)` 结构体公共前缀，以及大量数组/切片代码已经依赖从 field 或 element 派生的 pointer 访问更大范围；强制 subobject provenance 会给现有代码引入大量 UB。raw pointer/`&raw` 的 ergonomics 较差，且容易被隐式 autoref 或中间 reference 绕过。Thom Chiovoloni、Hanna Kruppe 等还认为新增 UB 带来的安全和可维护性成本未必能由实际优化收益抵偿。

- **阶段性共识/倾向**：根据会议和讨论，至少多数 opsem 成员倾向于：对当前语言已有的数组、slice 和 `repr(C)` struct 不启用 subobject provenance；RalfJ 进一步提出明确承诺不对 arrays/slices 采用该规则。allocations 的独立 provenance 不受影响。对 enum，尤其 enum discriminant 或 downcast，仍可能单独采用更严格规则，但尚未决定。

- **仍未解决的问题与候选方案**：如何在不破坏既有代码的情况下为优化提供更窄的访问范围仍无定论。讨论过 `restrict_provenance` intrinsic、类型/字段属性、`repr` 或 edition-based 规则、marker type、extern type/newtype，以及通过更强的 alias analysis、MIR 优化或 LLVM 信息传播来替代全局 UB；这些方案在安全性、FFI/`&Header` 兼容性、API ergonomics、edition 迁移和实际优化收益方面仍存在争议。

messages.en:
During the meeting today I learned that @**Ben Kimock (Saethlin)** is generally doubtful about having any form of subobject provenance.
Context: this is about https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/256; the question is whether a reference created via `&blah.foo` is allowed to (unsafely) access any bytes outside that field.

What are the general vibes about that? My assumption was that yes we do want subobject provenance sometimes, for some things (e.g. for fields of repr(Rust) types). If that's not the case then we don't even need to discuss the enum discriminant shenanigans @**Mario Carneiro** has been proposing.

The one argument for subobject provenance is optimizations, though I'd have to re-scan that issue to get a more concrete idea for which optimizations we considered.
messages.zh:
我在今天的会议上了解到，@**Ben Kimock (Saethlin)** 总体上对引入任何形式的子对象溯源都持怀疑态度。
背景是这样的：讨论的是 https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/256；问题在于，通过 `&blah.foo` 创建的引用，是否允许（以不安全的方式）访问该字段之外的其他字节。

大家对此总体是什么看法？我原本以为，我们确实有时希望具备子对象溯源，用于某些场景（例如 `repr(Rust)` 类型的字段）。如果不是这样，那我们甚至不需要讨论 @**Mario Carneiro** 一直在提议的枚举判别值相关问题。

支持子对象溯源的一个理由是优化，不过我得重新浏览一下那个 issue，才能更具体地想起我们当时考虑的是哪些优化。

messages.en: the [first example](https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/256#issuecomment-725638217) I mention here... sounds like nonsense? we can do that optimization in Tree Borrows even without subobject provenance...
messages.zh: 我在这里提到的[第一个例子](https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/256#issuecomment-725638217)……听起来像是无稽之谈？即使没有子对象溯源，我们也可以在 Tree Borrows 中进行那项优化……

messages.en: reading through the issue I only see people posting usecases for the &Header pattern, not motivations for subobject provenance...
messages.zh: 通读这个 issue 后，我只看到大家在发关于 `&Header` 模式的使用场景，而不是关于子对象溯源的动机……

messages.en: one motivation is the enum discriminant optimization we talked about (for non-niched enums)
messages.zh: 其中一个动机是我们讨论过的枚举判别值优化（针对没有 niche 的枚举）。

messages.en: It's surprising to me that whether or not the type is `#[repr(Rust)]` would matter for this. My mental model has always been that `#[repr(Rust)]` and `#[repr(C)]` were essentially just inputs to the layout algorithm, and not properties that matter after that algorithm produces its result.
messages.zh: 在我看来，类型是否为 `#[repr(Rust)]` 会影响这一点，这很令人意外。我的理解一直是，`#[repr(Rust)]` 和 `#[repr(C)]` 本质上只是布局算法的输入，而不是布局算法得出结果之后仍然会产生影响的属性。

messages.en: Admittedly I don't feel that strongly about this.
messages.zh: 不过说实话，我对此也没有特别强烈的看法。

messages.en: Typical example for useful subobject provenance in C is arrays in a struct with other members, or multi-dimensional arrays. Though this seems a lot less relevant in Rust because of bounds checks.
messages.zh: 在 C 中，一个有用的子对象溯源的典型例子是：结构体中包含数组以及其他成员，或者多维数组。不过由于 Rust 有边界检查，这似乎在 Rust 中没那么重要。

messages.en: How do bounds checks relate to this?
messages.zh: 边界检查和这个有什么关系？

messages.en: Are you saying that the check itself provides the same optimization? Or that the check blocks the desirable optimization?
messages.zh: 你的意思是，检查本身提供了同样的优化？还是说，检查会阻碍我们想要的优化？

messages.en: If LLVM had a way of expressing subobject provenance, we could use that for bounds-checked array accesses, without requiring subobject provenance in the aliasing model itself.
messages.zh: 如果 LLVM 有办法表达子对象溯源，我们就可以把它用于经过边界检查的数组访问，而不需要在别名模型本身中引入子对象溯源。

messages.en: So like, a Rust-specific intrinsic?
messages.zh: 所以，类似于 Rust 专用的 intrinsic？

messages.en: So, I was thinking about this. I wonder how much read access needs to be limited, compared to the potential usefulness of write access.
messages.zh: 我刚才在想这个问题。我在琢磨，相比于写访问潜在的实用性，读访问究竟需要受到多大限制。

messages.en:
My unsubstantiated gut feeling is that subobject provenance is probably not worth it for the long tail of capricious gotchas when writing unsafe code that it would likely cause. On the other hand, more than once I've stared at some code that passes a pointer to one field of an ADT into a function, and looking at some access to *other* fields around the call, and thinking that subobject provenance would be really nice for letting LLVM optimize those other accesses better.

For example, [this code](https://github.com/hanna-kruppe/chacha8rand/blob/fbd14b30f7030e7d0a227db177a7630687c6e177/chacha8rand/src/lib.rs#L823-L824) does an indirect call to refill a buffer that's a field of `self`, then resets another field of `self` (index into that buffer) to zero. Semantically, the order of these two steps doesn't matter. But at least for rustc+LLVM as it stands now, it's not clear that the indirect call can't change the counter, so the current order is better because it makes obvious that the counter will be zero after a refill. I'm not sure if protectors or other parts of a Rust aliasing model would help with this.
messages.zh:
我未经证实的直觉是，考虑到它很可能在编写不安全代码时带来一长串变幻莫测的坑，子对象溯源大概不值得引入。另一方面，我不止一次盯着这样的代码看过：它把一个 ADT 中某个字段的指针传给一个函数，然后观察调用附近对其他字段的访问，并想着，如果有子对象溯源，就能让 LLVM 更好地优化对那些其他字段的访问，那该多好。

例如，[这段代码](https://github.com/hanna-kruppe/chacha8rand/blob/fbd14b30f7030e7d0a227db177a7630687c6e177/chacha8rand/src/lib.rs#L823-L824) 间接调用了一个函数来填充 `self` 的一个字段（缓冲区），然后把 `self` 的另一个字段（该缓冲区的索引）重置为零。从语义上说，这两个步骤的顺序并不重要。但至少就目前的 rustc+LLVM 而言，间接调用不能修改计数器这一点并不明确，因此当前的顺序更好，因为这样显然可以看出，填充完成后计数器会是零。我不确定 protectors 或 Rust 别名模型的其他部分能否解决这个问题。

messages.en: I think arrays/slices are a bigger issue in practice for sub-object provenance than structs. There's a lot of code out there that takes the address of one element of an array, turns it into a raw pointer and then expects to be able to access any element of the array with it. Ideally such code should be using `&raw`, but that syntax is relatively new and a lot of existing code just creates a normal reference and casts that to a pointer.
messages.zh: 我觉得，在实践中，相比结构体，数组/切片涉及的子对象溯源问题更大。有大量现存代码会获取数组某个元素的地址，将其转换为裸指针，然后期望通过这个指针访问数组中的任意元素。理想情况下，这类代码应该使用 `&raw`，但这种语法相对较新，许多现有代码只是创建一个普通引用，再把它转换成指针。

messages.en: An interesting data point is Swift which is [even stricter](https://www.cocoawithlove.com/blog/2016/02/16/use_it_or_lose_it_why_safe_c_is_sometimes_unsafe_swift.html) than what is being proposed here. In Swift taking the address of a field "materializes" that field only for the scope of the borrow. Not only does this mean that you can't access other fields through that pointer, it also means that if you take the address of 2 fields adjacent of a local then there is no guarantee that they have consecutive addresses.
messages.zh: 有一个有趣的参考点是 Swift：它甚至比这里提议的方案[更加严格](https://www.cocoawithlove.com/blog/2016/02/16/use_it_or_lose_it_why_safe_c_is_sometimes_unsafe_swift.html)。在 Swift 中，获取字段的地址只会在借用的作用域内将该字段“实体化”。这不仅意味着你不能通过那个指针访问其他字段，还意味着，如果你获取了一个局部变量中两个相邻字段的地址，就不能保证它们的地址是连续的。

messages.en:
I think for structs there's still code that does this. For example, when I started with Rust I did stuff like
```rs
#[repr(C)]
pub struct Vec3 {
    pub x: f32,
    pub y: f32,
    pub z: f32,
}
```
And then use `&v.x as *const f32` (or mut) to access all 3 elements of `v` like an array. This is not strictly allowed in C/C++ either, but doing it is common. That said, I haven't written code like this in a long time (I'm well aware that `v as *const _ as *const f32` is the way to do that), but it wouldn't surprise me at all if there's code out there that does this. In fact, it would surprise me quite a bit if there is not.
messages.zh:
我觉得结构体也存在这么做的代码。例如，我刚开始接触 Rust 时，会写类似这样的代码：
```rs
#[repr(C)]
pub struct Vec3 {
    pub x: f32,
    pub y: f32,
    pub z: f32,
}
```
然后使用 `&v.x as *const f32`（或 mut）像访问数组一样访问 `v` 的全部 3 个元素。这在 C/C++ 中严格来说也不允许，但这样做很常见。话虽如此，我已经很久没写过这样的代码了（我很清楚 `v as *const _ as *const f32` 才是正确的做法），但如果外面确实存在这么做的代码，我一点也不会觉得意外。事实上，如果不存在这样的代码，我反而会相当惊讶。

messages.en: like, a bunch of `repr(C)` structs with a common prefix
messages.zh: 比如说，一堆具有相同公共前缀的 `repr(C)` 结构体。

messages.en: so I don't think we can realistically enforce subobject provenance on repr(C) types
messages.zh: 所以我认为，现实中我们无法对 `repr(C)` 类型强制执行子对象来源。

messages.zh: 仅使用裸指针的便利性仍然很差，这会把人们推向使用引用。

messages.en: there's work on improving these ergonomics
messages.zh: 目前有人在努力改善这方面的便利性。

messages.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/598567443):
```quote
so I don't think we can realistically enforce subobject provenance on repr(C) types
```

I think the proper fix for `&Header` is extern types, so we indeed better not enforce subobject provenance for `repr(C)` structs until those have been stabilized and been stable for a while.

*Technically*, it is something that we could change on an edition boundary, right? So that `repr(C)` only disables subobject provenance for a struct if that struct is defined in an edition < 20xy crate. And even before extern types stabelize, disabling subobject provenance could be made into its own attribute.
messages.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/598567443):
```quote
so I don't think we can realistically enforce subobject provenance on repr(C) types
```

我认为，解决 `&Header` 的正确方式是使用 extern 类型，因此在 extern 类型稳定并稳定运行一段时间之前，我们确实最好不要对 `repr(C)` 结构体强制执行子对象来源。

*严格来说*，我们可以在 edition 边界进行这种改变，对吧？也就是说，只有当某个结构体定义于 edition < 20xy 的 crate 中时，`repr(C)` 才会让该结构体禁用子对象来源。而且，即使 extern 类型尚未稳定，也可以将禁用子对象来源设计成一个单独的属性。

messages.en: technically, yes

messages.en: I would very much like to be able to tell LLVM about subobject provenance for the move elimination optimization. The optimization has a tendency to replace locals with projections into a larger local. When this happens, I would like to be able to tell LLVM alias analysis that references into the larger local (that were originally references to an unmerged local) are guaranteed to only access a subset of that larger local.
messages.zh: 我非常希望能把子对象来源信息告知 LLVM，以便进行消除移动优化。该优化倾向于用对一个更大局部变量的投影来替代局部变量。发生这种情况时，我希望能够告诉 LLVM 的别名分析：对这个更大局部变量的引用（原本是对某个未合并局部变量的引用）保证只会访问该更大局部变量的一个子集。

messages.en: Essentially, I can see this being useful in MIR even if we never expose it in the surface language.
messages.zh: 本质上，即使我们永远不在表层语言中暴露它，我也能看出它在 MIR 中会很有用。

messages.en: General subobject provenance in LLVM is kind of Hard, because it adds a lot of intrinsics on the pointer path, and everything needs to learn to look past them (correctly), otherwise you lose optimizations. I think your case might be handled more easily if we add allocator provenance intrinsics (I guess this also more directly represents what you are doing, where multiple sub-allocations are serviced from one larger one). In that case looking through the intrinsics shouldn't be important. (The subobject provenance issue may become simpler if we add ptr_provenance path as part of full restrict.)
messages.zh: LLVM 中通用的子对象来源信息有点难处理，因为它会在指针路径上加入大量 intrinsic，而所有东西都需要学会（正确地）越过它们进行分析，否则就会损失优化机会。我认为，如果我们添加分配器来源信息 intrinsic，或许能更容易地处理你的场景（我猜这也更直接地表达了你正在做的事情：从一个更大的分配中提供多个子分配）。这样一来，分析时是否越过这些 intrinsic 就不那么重要了。（如果我们把 `ptr_provenance` 路径作为完整 restrict 的一部分加入，子对象来源信息的问题或许会变得更简单。）

messages.en:
Stumbled across this and these are my thoughts from the CHERI world:

CHERI can support this in the architecture, and so in CHERI LLVM it is a compile-time option to enable (for C/C++), with various type and member annotations, and builtins, to opt out in specific cases when otherwise enabled. This does brush up against language semantics issues (e.g. &a[x] is defined to be equivalent to a + x in C so shouldn't be restricted, and yet there are clearly reasons why that might be useful to do), as well as just de-facto use (e.g. embedding linked list nodes into larger structures), so our default is to turn it off, and if you want to turn it on you can, with varying degrees of aggressiveness that increasingly violate ISO C yet have clear benefits for certain use cases (like the array example, which you have to dial things up quite a bit to get). For our CheriBSD kernel we turn it on, as there is a non-zero number of past CVEs for overflowing within a struct, but only at the lowest level. Even then it is a decent source of friction (the cause of most of our panics these days when exercising previously-untested device drivers etc), but we currently view it as a worthwhile thing to do. I would hope that Rust would be better poised to be able to have a subobject provenance story in its semantics, but I know well the pain that can come from imposing such constraints on systems code...
messages.zh:
偶然看到了这个话题，以下是我从 CHERI 领域得到的一些想法：

CHERI 可以在架构层面支持这一点，因此在 CHERI LLVM 中，对于 C/C++，这是一个可以在编译时启用的选项；同时还提供各种类型和成员注解，以及 builtins，以便在默认启用时针对特定情况选择退出。这确实会触及语言语义问题（例如，在 C 中，`&a[x]` 被定义为等价于 `a + x`，所以不应受到限制，但显然，限制它又有充分的理由），也会涉及实际上的使用方式（例如，将链表节点嵌入更大的结构体中）。因此我们的默认设置是关闭它；如果你想开启，可以自行开启，并根据需要选择不同程度的激进设置。这些设置越激进，就越偏离 ISO C，但对某些使用场景有明显好处（比如数组示例——要实现这一点，你得把设置调得相当激进）。对于 CheriBSD 内核，我们会开启它，因为过去确实有不少 CVE 是由于在结构体内部发生溢出导致的，不过我们只在最低层级启用。即便如此，这仍然会带来相当大的摩擦（如今，在测试之前未测试过的设备驱动等代码时，我们大多数 panic 都是由此引起的），但目前我们认为这样做是值得的。我希望 Rust 在其语义中建立一套子对象来源信息机制时能更有优势，但我也很清楚，给系统代码施加这类约束可能会带来多大的痛苦……

@_**Ben Kimock (Saethlin)|120827** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/598408051):

I don't know if this is the same thing, but one problem we had (still have? dunno) with the `array::IntoIter` was that it was really hard to SRoA because offsetting into the *array* field -- which basically always happens for any interesting consumer -- looks extremely similar to offsetting to read the start/end fields of the iterator itself so it needed *some* way to know that `array_intoiter.as_slice()[i]` isn't allowed to read the start/end fields.

IIRC we ended up moving the array after the start/end so that as long as one only uses known-positive GEP offsets it worked well enough?  But `array::IntoIter<usize, 10>` is a place where the `Range<usize>` and `[usize; 10]` being UB to intermingle would be handy.

(Said without thinking about practicality of it as an overall rule.)
messages.zh:
@_**Ben Kimock (Saethlin)|120827** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/598408051)：
```quote
你是说检查本身提供了同样的优化吗？还是说这个检查阻止了我们所希望的优化？
```

我不知道这是不是同一回事，但我们之前（现在还存在吗？不知道）在处理 `array::IntoIter` 时遇到的一个问题是：它很难进行 SRoA，因为对 *array* 字段进行偏移——任何有趣的使用者基本都会这样做——看起来和对迭代器自身的 start/end 字段进行读取时的偏移极其相似，所以它需要某种方式来知道 `array_intoiter.as_slice()[i]` 不允许读取 start/end 字段。

如果我没记错，我们最后把 array 放到了 start/end 之后，这样只要只使用已知为正的 GEP 偏移量，效果就还算不错？不过，`array::IntoIter<usize, 10>` 确实是一个这样的场景：如果规定 `Range<usize>` 和 `[usize; 10]` 之间不能混用且这会触发 UB，那将会很有帮助。

（这里没有考虑把它作为一条总体规则的实际可行性。）

messages.en: @**Jessica Clarke** is the point that enforcing subobject provenance is useful to find real bugs (that would be bugs even if the language had no subobject provenance)?
messages.zh: @**Jessica Clarke** 的意思是，强制执行子对象来源信息，是为了找出实际的 bug（即使语言没有子对象来源信息，这些问题本来也会是 bug）吗？

messages.en: one could consider turning some forms of subobject provenance violations into EB not UB, so we couldnt use it for optimizations (and there is no risk of miscompilations) but a strict enforcement mode could still error on such code
messages.zh: 可以考虑把某些形式的子对象来源信息违规行为改成 EB，而不是 UB。这样我们就不能利用它进行优化（也不会有错误编译的风险），但严格执行模式仍然可以对这类代码报错。

messages.en: that said, I am fairly convinced that we dont want any such EB or UB for array indexing
messages.zh: 话虽如此，我相当确信，我们不希望数组索引存在任何这类 EB 或 UB。

messages.en: (i.e., we want to match the C semantics there)
messages.zh: （也就是说，我们希望在这里匹配 C 的语义。）

messages.en: that would also mean no official rust tool should ever complain about code that "violates" array subobject provenance
messages.zh: 这也意味着，任何官方 Rust 工具都不应因为代码“违反”了数组子对象来源信息规则而报错。

messages.en:
I am outside of opsem and only a little chic of a Rust developer so I don't think my vibes count for much but... I must say I actually do find myself thinking that I'd prefer having subobject provenance.

I find myself thinking that lacking subobject provenance sounds harder to reason about in unsafe code, or harder to teach maybe...? Like, you have an unsafe operation that takes some `&T` and its safety condition is that this must have been created in a particular way / from a particular struct, and also must not have had its provenance restricted, but none of that is visible in the type system. Effectively, the safest of safe types can now have fairly gnarly variance to when they're actually safe, and Rust just says: "yes, this is fine and if you want to write your unsafe code to work with references to a field of type T that just looks like a normal reference to a T, then knock yourself out."

Compared to having subobject provenance, where a reference is a reference is a reference, and if you want to do fancy and unsafe things with eg. field pointers then you have to write specific wrappers over field pointers and carefully carry the provenance over. A `&u32` is always just a `&u32` in this world, never a `&u32<MyStruct::field>`.
messages.zh:
我不属于 opsem 领域，也只是个对 Rust 略懂皮毛的开发者，所以我不觉得自己的直觉有多大参考价值，不过……我得说，我确实发现自己更倾向于拥有子对象来源信息。

我总觉得，缺少子对象来源信息会让 unsafe 代码更难推理，也可能更难教学……比如，有一个 unsafe 操作接受某个 `&T`，它的安全条件是：这个引用必须以特定方式创建，或者必须来自某个特定结构体；同时，它的来源信息还不能被限制，但这些要求在类型系统中完全不可见。实际上，就连最安全的安全类型，现在也可能在什么情况下才真正安全这件事上存在相当棘手的差异，而 Rust 只会说：“没问题；如果你想让自己的 unsafe 代码处理指向某个字段的引用，而这个引用看起来就只是普通的 `T` 类型引用，那你尽管去做吧。”

相比之下，如果存在子对象来源信息，那么引用就是引用；如果你想对字段指针之类的东西做一些复杂而不安全的操作，就必须为字段指针编写专门的封装，并谨慎地传递其来源信息。在这个世界里，`&u32` 永远只是 `&u32`，而不会是 `&u32<MyStruct::field>`。

messages.en: The main way that people run up against subobject provenance is with the `&Header` pattern. That's quite different from `&u32`. The user-defined `Header` types have safety invariants directly tied to the extra data (beyond what `size_of_val` says) existing. Sometimes you can't even statically write down the type that the header is part of. I don't think it's obvious that that kind of unsafe code would become much simpler to reason about by enforcing subobject provenance.
messages.zh: 人们遇到子对象来源信息问题的主要方式，是使用 `&Header` 模式。这和 `&u32` 很不一样。用户定义的 `Header` 类型，其安全不变量直接依赖于额外数据的存在，而这些数据并不在 `size_of_val` 所反映的范围内。有时，你甚至无法静态地写出这个 header 所属对象的类型。我不认为，强制执行子对象来源信息，显然就能让这类 unsafe 代码变得更容易推理。

messages.en: You are making the mistake of pinning library requirements to language requirements. Stricter preconditions do not make unsafe code easier to write.
messages.zh: 你把库的要求和语言的要求混为一谈了。更严格的前置条件并不会让 unsafe 代码更容易编写。

messages.en: The kind of reasoning you are try to engage in is hazardous because if it was valid, would forbid removing UB from the language. Adding UB to the language is already a breaking change, so if we were to also forbid removing UB, the opsem would be fixed and immutable.
messages.zh: 你试图进行的这种推理很危险，因为如果它成立，就会禁止从语言中移除 UB。向语言中添加 UB 本身就已经是一项破坏性变更；所以，如果我们还要禁止移除 UB，那么 opsem 就会被固定下来，永远不可改变。

messages.en:
I'm not smart enough and probably too tired to really understand but... In a sense I feel like this makes _safe_ code harder to write.

```rust
fn do_with_type_erased_t(t: &Header) { ... }
```

Is this function safe? Or did we make a mistake and it should actually be `unsafe`? That depends:
1. If it does not read anything beyond the Header then it is safe.
2. If it does read beyond the Header and we do not have subobject provenance it is also safe.
3. Exception: If we have a safe `fn restrict_provenance` in which case it must be unsafe.
4. Exception to 3: If we have a marker trait `Restrictable` that a type can opt out of which is required to call `fn restrict_provenance` then it is safe.
5. Alternative exception to 3: If `fn restrict_provenance` is unsafe then the function is again safe. The safety precondition on `restrict_provenance` is going to be pretty rough though; "reference must not be used to access data out of its bounds". That just feels like it's on the wrong end of the stick - proving a negative instead of giving a positive guarantee.

It just seems complicated to me that `&(mut )T` of all types would have a potentially viral safety condition like this.
messages.zh:
我不够聪明，而且可能也太累了，实在没法完全理解，但……从某种意义上说，我觉得这会让编写 _safe_ 代码变得更困难。

```rust
fn do_with_type_erased_t(t: &Header) { ... }
```

这个函数安全吗？还是说我们犯了错，它实际上应该是 `unsafe`？这取决于具体情况：
1. 如果它不会读取 Header 之外的任何内容，那么它是安全的。
2. 如果它确实会读取 Header 之外的内容，而我们又没有子对象 provenance，那么它也仍然是安全的。
3. 例外：如果我们有一个安全的 `fn restrict_provenance`，那么它就必须是 `unsafe`。
4. 对第 3 点的例外：如果我们有一个标记 trait `Restrictable`，类型可以选择不实现它，而调用 `fn restrict_provenance` 又要求实现该 trait，那么它就是安全的。
5. 对第 3 点的另一种例外：如果 `fn restrict_provenance` 是 `unsafe` 的，那么该函数又重新变得安全了。不过，`restrict_provenance` 的安全前置条件会相当棘手——“不得使用该引用访问其边界之外的数据”。这给人的感觉就是方向完全反了：不是提供一个正向保证，而是要求证明某件事不会发生。

在我看来，所有类型的 `&(mut )T` 都可能带有这样一种会传染开的安全条件，实在太复杂了。

messages.zh:
@_**Aapo Alasuutari|699208** [写道](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/602863390)：
```quote
2. If it does read beyond the Header and we do not have subobject provenance it is also safe.
```

messages.en:
I had generally been having similar thoughts to @_**Aapo Alasuutari** but this conversation is making it clearer how `&Header` can be a sensible thing even in safe code.

* Unambiguously true: When we attribute a type `T` to a piece of memory, such as by passing an `&T`, we make a claim about the contents of that memory.
* Potential extension: When we attribute a type `T` to a piece of memory, we make a claim about the contents of *adjacent* memory.
messages.zh:
我之前总体上也有和 @_**Aapo Alasuutari** 类似的想法，但这次讨论让我更清楚地认识到，即使在安全代码中，`&Header` 也可以是合理的。

* 毫无疑问：当我们把类型 `T` 归属于一块内存时，比如传入一个 `&T`，我们是在对这块内存的内容做出某种断言。
* 可能的扩展：当我们把类型 `T` 归属于一块内存时，我们是在对*相邻*内存的内容也做出某种断言。

messages.en: …hm, wait, what about [`std::slice::from_ref()`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/slice/fn.from_ref.html)? This implies that, if it is valid to unsafely access the adjacent memory from an arbitrary provided `&Header`, then it must also be valid to unsafely access the adjacent memory from the last element of `&[Header]` (because safe code may transform `&Header` to `&[Header]` and back). This seems like it might have bad consequences for the optimizability of slice accesses.
messages.zh: ……嗯，等等，那 [`std::slice::from_ref()`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/slice/fn.from_ref.html) 怎么办？这意味着，如果从任意给定的 `&Header` 访问相邻内存在 unsafe 情况下是有效的，那么从 `&[Header]` 的最后一个元素访问相邻内存在 unsafe 情况下也必须是有效的（因为安全代码可以将 `&Header` 转换成 `&[Header]`，再转换回来）。这似乎可能会对 slice 访问的优化能力造成不良影响。

messages.en:
@_**Aapo Alasuutari|699208** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/602869588):
```quote
they'll just be unsound in a more subtle manner (cannot have `restrict_provenance` called on `&(mut )Header`)
```

Yes, `restrict_provenance` is essentially incompatible with the `&Header` pattern. That is a good point. Though it's not so surprising to me: we know the `&Header` pattern is incompatible with subobject provenance, and having `restrict_provenance` essentially means "we have subobject provenance, but it's applied only sometimes instead of automatically for every `&T` that is created" which of course makes no difference for soundness.
messages.zh:
@_**Aapo Alasuutari|699208** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/602869588)：
```quote
它们只会以一种更隐蔽的方式变得不健全（不能对 `&(mut )Header` 调用 `restrict_provenance`）
```

是的，`restrict_provenance` 本质上与 `&Header` 模式不兼容。这一点说得很好。不过，这对我来说并不意外：我们知道 `&Header` 模式与子对象 provenance 不兼容，而 `restrict_provenance` 的本质就是“我们有子对象 provenance，但只在某些时候应用它，而不是自动应用于每个创建出来的 `&T`”，这当然不会对健全性产生任何不同。

messages.en: In a similarly reductive manner, the `&T <-> &[T]` case seems to boil down to: if we don't have subobject provenance, we don't have subobject provenance for slice elements in particular. Or, with a bit more nuance, it may be difficult to define and explain a coherent model that has e.g. subobject provenance for `&slice[i]` projections but not for `&x.field`. But since the `&Header` pattern often involves slices at some level as well, it's never been clear to me how to draw a meaningful distinction between these.
messages.zh: 同样以一种简化的方式来看，`&T <-> &[T]` 这个问题似乎可以归结为：如果我们没有子对象 provenance，那么特别是对于 slice 元素，我们也没有子对象 provenance。或者更细致地说，要定义并解释一个自洽的模型可能会很困难，例如在这个模型中，`&slice[i]` 投影具有子对象 provenance，而 `&x.field` 却没有。不过，由于 `&Header` 模式通常也会在某个层面涉及 slices，我一直不清楚该如何在这两者之间划出有意义的区别。

@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/602795996):
```quote
@**Jessica Clarke** is the point that enforcing subobject provenance is useful to find real bugs (that would be bugs even if the language had no subobject provenance)?
```

It's about closing security vulnerabilities that are due to intra-object overflows, like https://projectzero.google/2021/12/this-shouldnt-have-happened.html. In theory if you turn on subobject bounds with CHERI LLVM when compiling that code then (ignoring that the next step in the chain was to inject a function pointer which we'd also break, but surely there are other interesting data-oriented things you could do) CHERI could have prevented it. Sometimes there are good reasons why you don't want subobject provenance, but I generally take the view that it's the exception not the rule and it's not too onerous to require opting into the less-secure form, but at least in the case of C there is a lot of existing code that would break so the story is more awkward. With Rust though I imagine (or at least naively hope...) people are generally better about not doing things that go against subobject provenance than your average overly-cunning C programmer.

```quote
@**Jessica Clarke** 的意思是，强制执行子对象 provenance，是因为这有助于发现真正的 bug（即使语言没有子对象 provenance，这些问题也仍然会是 bug）吗？
```

这关系到修复由对象内部溢出导致的安全漏洞，例如 https://projectzero.google/2021/12/this-shouldnt-have-happened.html。理论上，如果你在用 CHERI LLVM 编译那段代码时启用子对象边界，那么（先不考虑攻击链的下一步是注入一个函数指针，而这同样会被我们阻止；不过肯定还可以进行其他有趣的面向数据的攻击）CHERI 本来是可以阻止它的。有时你确实有充分理由不希望使用子对象 provenance，但总的来说，我认为这属于例外而不是常态；要求用户显式选择安全性较低的形式，负担并不算太大。不过至少对于 C 来说，已经存在大量会因此无法工作的代码，所以情况要棘手得多。至于 Rust，我想（或者至少天真地希望……）人们通常比那些平均水平上过于狡猾的 C 程序员更不容易写出违背子对象 provenance 的代码。

messages.en:
by that I mean that just like the compiler can't put `T` in read-only memory if it contains an `UnsafeCell` ignoring stuff behind pointers, I think the compiler shouldn't enable subobject provenance if `T` contains any type with subobject provenance disabled, ignoring stuff behind pointers. I'm not saying that some other unrelated field of `T` gets disabled subobject provenance too, which is the undecided part of `UnsafeCell`. e.g.:
```rust
pub struct T {
    pub unrelated: Unrelated,
    pub field: TypeWithoutSubobjectProvenance,
}
```
so with `t: T` -- `&t` doesn't use subobject provenance, neither does `&t.field`, but `&t.unrelated` can use subobject provenance since `Unrelated` doesn't disable it.
messages.zh:
我的意思是，就像编译器不能把包含 `UnsafeCell` 的 `T`（忽略指针背后的内容）放入只读内存一样，我认为如果 `T` 包含任何禁用了子对象来源的类型（同样忽略指针背后的内容），编译器也不应该启用子对象来源。我并不是说 `T` 的其他无关字段也应该禁用子对象来源；这正是 `UnsafeCell` 尚未决定的部分。例如：
```rust
pub struct T {
    pub unrelated: Unrelated,
    pub field: TypeWithoutSubobjectProvenance,
}
```
因此，对于 `t: T`——`&t` 不使用子对象来源，`&t.field` 也不使用，但 `&t.unrelated` 可以使用子对象来源，因为 `Unrelated` 并不会禁用它。

messages.en:
For CHERI C/C++ we currently have all of the following opt-out mechanisms:
* type-level annotations
* member-level annotations
* declaration-level annotations

@_**Amanieu d'Antras|143274** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/598438266):
```quote
An interesting data point is Swift which is [even stricter](https://www.cocoawithlove.com/blog/2016/02/16/use_it_or_lose_it_why_safe_c_is_sometimes_unsafe_swift.html) than what is being proposed here. In Swift taking the address of a field "materializes" that field only for the scope of the borrow. Not only does this mean that you can't access other fields through that pointer, it also means that if you take the address of 2 fields adjacent of a local then there is no guarantee that they have consecutive addresses.
```

In an old thread (https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Varargs.20SROA.20sadness/), I really wanted this for variadic generics. Not just for performance, but when bringing `unsized_fn_params` into the mix, it's necessary for certain varargs designs to work at all
messages.zh:
@_**Amanieu d'Antras|143274** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/598438266)：
```quote
一个有趣的参考点是 Swift，它甚至比这里提议的方案更加严格。[在 Swift 中](https://www.cocoawithlove.com/blog/2016/02/16/use_it_or_lose_it_why_safe_c_is_sometimes_unsafe_swift.html)，获取字段地址只会在借用的作用域内“实体化”该字段。这不仅意味着你不能通过那个指针访问其他字段，还意味着如果你获取了局部变量中两个相邻字段的地址，就无法保证它们的地址是连续的。
```

在一个较早的讨论串（https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Varargs.20SROA.20sadness/）中，我非常希望变参泛型能具备这一点。不仅仅是为了性能；当把 `unsized_fn_params` 也考虑进来后，某些变参设计要想正常工作，这甚至是必需的。

messages.en:
@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/603950737):
```quote
C's flexible array member pattern is commonly used from Rust in a way that would violate subobject provenance: https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-bindgen/using-fam.html
```

They don't inherently violate subobject provenance, and you can still restrict references in the abstract machine to be only to the array, but you do need a way to talk about the size of that subobject in the semantics (and, for enforcement, obtain it somehow). For us, C flexible array members (and I think zero-sized ones as well, since zero-sized arrays are a GNU extension that often get used for flexible arrays in pre-C99 code) with subobject bounds enabled notionally get bounds of the entire flexible array member, which we realise by leaving the upper bound from the surrounding object as-is, only increasing the lower bond, which is a conservative over-approximation (since depending on where that capability came from there may be other objects beyond the end of that flexible array member which will end up within bounds, but it's the best we can do without further annotations like the `__counted_by` used by Apple's -fbounds-safety software bounds enforcement).
messages.zh:
@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/603950737)：
```quote
C 的柔性数组成员模式在 Rust 中很常见，但其用法会违反子对象来源：https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-bindgen/using-fam.html
```

它们并非从根本上违反子对象来源；在抽象机中，你仍然可以将引用限制为只能指向数组。但你确实需要一种方式，在语义中描述该子对象的大小（而在实施检查时，也需要以某种方式获取这个大小）。对我们来说，启用了子对象边界的 C 柔性数组成员（我认为零大小数组也一样，因为零大小数组是 GNU 扩展，在 C99 之前的代码中经常被用作柔性数组）在概念上会获得整个柔性数组成员的边界。我们的实现方式是保留外围对象的上界，只增大下界；这是一种保守的过度近似（因为根据该能力的来源，柔性数组成员末尾之后可能还有其他对象，而这些对象最终也会落在边界内），但如果没有进一步的注解——例如 Apple 的 `-fbounds-safety` 软件边界检查所使用的 `__counted_by`——这已经是我们能做到的最好结果。

messages.en: also it's easy to accidentally screw it up - if you write `takes_raw_ptr(&x.foo)` instead of `takes_raw_ptr(&raw x.foo)` it'll compile just fine without warning (even clippy doesn't warn for it). Adding a warning for that is probably doable just fine, but it's not there yet.

messages.zh: 某种程度上是这样，但我认为至少在 https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-bindgen/using-fam.html 这类场景中，子对象 provenance 违规行为与所传入的结构体有非常紧密的联系。只有针对特意为这种用法设计的特定结构体，访问超出子对象的部分才有意义，而不是对所有结构体都适用。

messages.en: IMO the edition change should take effect at the point where the reference is created, not based on the type. So `&x.y` in 2024 returns a reference with whole-allocation provenance, but in 2027 edition returns a reference restricted to the `y` field.
messages.zh: 我认为，edition 变更应该在创建引用的地方生效，而不是取决于类型。因此，2024 中的 `&x.y` 会返回具有整个分配 provenance 的引用，而在 2027 edition 中则会返回一个 provenance 受限于 `y` 字段的引用。

messages.en: so then if you use a struct from a 3rd-party crate that is edition 2024 in edition 2027 code, there is no way to return a `&Header` with provenance for the data after the header since creating a reference causes sub-object provenance, but you can do that in edition 2024? that seems like the wrong way to me
messages.zh: 那么，如果你在 edition 2027 的代码中使用一个来自第三方 crate、且该 crate 使用 edition 2024 的结构体，就无法返回一个具有 header 之后数据 provenance 的 `&Header`，因为创建引用会导致子对象 provenance；但在 edition 2024 中却可以做到？这在我看来似乎不是正确的做法。

messages.en: it works much better if it's based on which edition the struct is defined in so `Header` from an edition 2024 crate still works when used in an edition 2027 crate, and when the struct definition is changed to edition 2027 it can have the opt-out of subobject provenance attribute, so keeps working
messages.zh: 如果根据结构体定义所在的 edition 来决定，效果会好得多：这样，来自 edition 2024 crate 的 `Header` 在 edition 2027 crate 中使用时仍然可以正常工作；而当结构体定义改为 edition 2027 时，可以通过属性选择退出子对象 provenance，从而继续保持正常工作。

messages.en: Making it based on the edition where the struct is defined means it's a breaking change for the defining crate to update its edition without opting every single one of its types out of subobject provenance
messages.zh: 如果根据结构体定义所在的 edition 来决定，那么定义该结构体的 crate 在更新 edition 时，如果不为它的每一个类型都选择退出子对象 provenance，就会构成破坏性变更。

messages.en: That only applies to types with public fields as you can't create a reference to private fields outside of the defining crate, right?
messages.zh: 不过，这只适用于字段为 public 的类型，对吧？因为在定义它的 crate 外部无法创建指向私有字段的引用。

messages.en:
based on the discussion above and at the recent t-opsem meeting, it seems like at least 3 out of 5 opsem members would be fine with saying "there is no subobject provenance on types that currently exist in the language, except maybe for enums". The main arguments are
- a bunch of existing code assumes this already for arrays and slices
- a lot of code generated by bindgen assumes this at least for repr(C) structs
- `#[repr]` shouldn't affect the opsem in such subtle ways
- the benefits of this UB are unclear. there are optimizations one can sketch where this is useful, but the fact that LLVM has no way of even representing this makes it look like there's no that much to be had here in terms of practically useful optimizations.

@**Crystal Durham** @**Mario Carneiro** you weren't at that meeting -- I wonder what your thoughts on this are?
messages.zh:
根据上面的讨论以及最近的 t-opsem 会议，至少 5 位 opsem 成员中的 3 位似乎都可以接受这样的说法：“对于语言目前已有的类型，不存在 subobject provenance；枚举或许例外。”主要论据如下：

- 大量现有代码已经假定数组和切片不存在这种 provenance
- bindgen 生成的大量代码至少对 `repr(C)` 结构体做了这样的假定
- `#[repr]` 不应该以如此微妙的方式影响 opsem
- 这种 UB 的收益并不明确。我们可以设想一些它有用的优化，但 LLVM 甚至没有办法表示这种信息，这让人觉得它在实际有用的优化方面并没有多少可发挥的空间。

@**Crystal Durham** @**Mario Carneiro** 你们当时没参加那次会议——想知道你们对此有什么看法？

messages.zh:
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607113158)：


无论我们如何处理 subobject provenance，Rust 中（对一个指向字段的指针会逃逸的结构体）执行 SRoA 基本上都没戏，因为即使是在完全安全的 Rust 中，也仍然可以观察到各种指针的地址彼此之间是什么关系。

这里唯一的解决办法是更好的内联，以及跨函数的逃逸分析。

messages.en: I don't think LLVM's SRoA currently does this, but it's possible to promote some fields of an aggregate to SSA values while still keeping the original local, if subobject provenance proves that the escaping pointers can only access a subset of fields. For example, for a local `pair: (u32, f32)` where only `&pair.0` escapes, all mentions of `pair.1` could be redirected to a separate local `pair_1: f32`. This effectively takes subobject provenance reasoning and recasts it into separate objects to help LLVM's object-based provenance reasoning.
messages.zh:
我不认为 LLVM 当前的 SRoA 会这样做，不过，如果 subobject provenance 能证明那些逃逸的指针只能访问字段的一个子集，那么就有可能在保留原始局部变量的同时，将聚合类型中的某些字段提升为 SSA 值。

例如，对于一个局部变量 `pair: (u32, f32)`，如果只有 `&pair.0` 会逃逸，那么所有涉及 `pair.1` 的地方都可以重定向到一个单独的局部变量 `pair_1: f32`。这样实际上就把 subobject provenance 的推理重新表述成了独立对象，从而帮助 LLVM 进行基于对象的 provenance 推理。

````quote
```

sorry I dont want to spend 10-20 minutes figuring out what you want to demonstrate with this entirely uncommented example. can you explain / add comments please?
````

In the Rust version LLVM can't prove that accesses through `elements` don't also access `start`, which means that on every loop iteration it must write `start` back to memory so that the access via `elements` sees the correct value. The C++ version with TBAA doesn't have this problem because the individual elements of `elements` and `start` have different types. If you change the C++ code to have an array of `size_t` instead of `double` then it also loses the optimization and has to write back `start` on every loop iteration.
messages.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607198537)：
````quote
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607125347)：
```quote
这是一个 C++ 使用 TBAA 后能比 Rust 优化得更多的例子（移除了循环中的存储），但我预计 Rust 可以通过对带有子对象来源的代码使用 SRoA，轻松恢复这一点：https://rust.godbolt.org/z/M836Ke61
```

抱歉，我不想花 10 到 20 分钟去弄清楚这个完全没有注释的例子想展示什么。你能解释一下，或者加些注释吗？
````

在 Rust 版本中，LLVM 无法证明通过 `elements` 的访问不会同时访问 `start`，这意味着在每次循环迭代中，它都必须把 `start` 写回内存，以便通过 `elements` 的访问能看到正确的值。使用 TBAA 的 C++ 版本没有这个问题，因为 `elements` 和 `start` 的各个元素类型不同。如果把 C++ 代码改成使用 `size_t` 数组而不是 `double` 数组，它同样会失去这项优化，并且必须在每次循环迭代中写回 `start`。

C++ definitely has it also. There's a specific concept called pointer-interconvertible for union fields and the first field of a standard-layout struct (or the base classes of a fieldless standard-layout struct), that allows freely casting narrow-to-wide, then disallows leaving the bounds of an object otherwise, except to index other elements of the immediately enclosing array (std::lauder calls this "reachability")


C++ 肯定也有这个。对于联合体字段和标准布局结构体的第一个字段（或者无字段标准布局结构体的基类），有一个专门的概念叫作 pointer-interconvertible，它允许自由地进行从窄指针到宽指针的转换；除此之外，指针不能越出对象边界，唯一的例外是可以索引直接包含它的数组中的其他元素（std::lauder 将此称为“可达性”）

messages.en:
We could say that if a local of an SRoA-eligible struct type does not have its address taken at any point, then its individual fields are treated as separate locals and can have offsets that differ from what the struct layout would prescribe. ("Does not have its address taken at any point" would be defined syntactically; e.g. an `&local` anywhere in the source, even in dead code, amounts to "taking the address".)

There are plenty of reasons why this particular approach might not be a good idea—making `&local` have spooky-action-at-a-distance among them—but hopefully it demonstrates that this is *possible* to support, and maybe there's a cleaner way.
messages.zh:
我们可以规定：如果某个符合 SRoA 条件的结构体类型局部变量在任何时候都没有获取其地址，那么它的各个字段就被视为独立的局部变量，并且其偏移量可以不同于结构体布局所规定的偏移量。（“在任何时候都没有获取其地址”将通过语法来定义；例如，源代码中的任何位置出现 `&local`，即使位于死代码中，也算作“获取地址”。）

这种具体做法有很多理由可能并不是好主意——让 `&local` 产生令人难以预料的远距离影响就是其中之一——但希望这能说明，支持这一点是*可能的*，也许还存在更简洁的方式。

messages.zh: @_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607108666)：```quote 基于上面的讨论以及最近一次 t-opsem 会议上的讨论，看起来至少有 5 位 opsem 成员中的 3 位愿意接受这样的说法：“对于目前语言中已有的类型，不存在子对象来源信息，枚举类型或许除外。”主要理由如下：- 现有的一些代码已经假定数组和切片是这样的 - bindgen 生成的大量代码至少对 repr(C) 结构体作了这样的假定 - `#[repr]` 不应以如此微妙的方式影响 opsem - 这种未定义行为的好处并不明确。我们可以设想出一些在这种情况下有用的优化，但 LLVM 甚至没有办法表示这一点，这似乎说明从实际有用的优化角度来看，这里并没有太多可得之处。 @**Crystal Durham** @**Mario Carneiro** 你们当时没参加那次会议——我想知道你们对此有什么看法？``` 考虑到我的枚举提案依赖于子对象来源信息，你们应该能预料到，我赞成至少在这些情况下保留它（无论是否进行 niche 优化，也就是说，`Option<u8>` 也应具有子对象来源信息）。我已经详细阐述过，我认为这种未定义行为有哪些好处。
