````quote
@_**Thom Chiovoloni|209168** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/621906074):
```quote
* And then it forces you to use `ptr::expose_provenance()` over `ptr::addr()` more of the time (since `addr()` can't be used for comparisons reliably),
```

it encourages you to compare the pointers directly rather than converting them into addresses first.
having to use expose_provenance seems pretty rare?
````

Sure, I meant for the cases where you could previously use just addr. The fact that usually you can just compare pointers is why I think it's not so bad.

> We already say that the program can abort with a stack overflow basically any time (but as a QoI concern it generally won't), so this could be similar. OTOH it is a bit silly since unlike a stack overflow, we know this will actually *never* happen

Ah, I had interpreted that as being a legit OOM case where because of the expose, we could no longer remove an allocation (and now something else will OOM, so I guess the fact that the OOM isn't in the right place for that should have tipped me off...).

> I would think that many "violations" actually have `a.addr() == b.addr()` as syntactic shape

I don't think so. I can't imagine when you would ever compare `a.addr()` to `b.addr()` directly. Maybe some arithmetic to avoid going through `ptr::wrapping_{add,sub,offset}` (because those are sometimes seen as less 'correct' for somewhat dubious reasons) or something?

One case I can imagine is `(a.addr() & SOME_MASK) == (b.addr() & SOME_MASK)`. And whether or not that's okay depends on which bits `SOME_MASK` is removing...

...

In the interest of being a bit less abstract, I looked around std a bit for things that either violate this rule or seem dubious under it. Here are some cases where addresses are compared (to things other than constants)

- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f207aa3913114c3326bc0b88acbd12b10244edf8/library/std/src/sys/pal/unix/stack_overflow/thread_info.rs (`errno_location().addr()` used as a thread id in a lock)

- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f207aa3913114c3326bc0b88acbd12b10244edf8/library/std/src/backtrace.rs#L325 (instruction pointer compared to a symbol addr. perhaps these are fine because they're code addresses, not addresses of allocations?)

- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f207aa3913114c3326bc0b88acbd12b10244edf8/library/std/src/sys/pal/windows/mod.rs#L72. This is subtraction and not comparison, although the result of the subtraction does get compared, so it seems similar. My assumption is that this is fine because they're from the same allocation? Or is that only the case for the other model.

- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f207aa3913114c3326bc0b88acbd12b10244edf8/library/std/src/sys/pal/unix/stack_overflow.rs#L110 This actually compares the faulting address to another address range. It feels like this perhaps could be a case that needs to be expose_addr? Certainly the provenances of the guardpage and the fault address are going to be wildly different... Hmmm... Or perhaps we can just declare that this is a case that is Sufficiently Magic to not be a problem?

- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f207aa3913114c3326bc0b88acbd12b10244edf8/library/std/src/path.rs#L1666-L1669 (more addr() on pointers from same alloc -> arith -> do stuff with result. there's a lot of this, so I'll omit the rest).

- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f207aa3913114c3326bc0b88acbd12b10244edf8/library/std/src/sync/mpmc/waker.rs#L71-L92 These thread ids are `addr()`s of thread locals, and are absolutely being compared. I guess they need to expose instead? Or stay as pointers (harder sell maybe)

- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f207aa3913114c3326bc0b88acbd12b10244edf8/library/std/src/thread/tests.rs#L149-L165 A test where the addr of a local is compared. Obviously if the code under test is correct then this is fine (same address), but otherwise ???

- There's... also a few places in std::sync that *seem* fine, but I would probably want to do a real look if this model were accepted. And also the xous sync primitives look like they probably violate it, but I don't care enough to dig into a tier3 platform I've only heard of once. (No offense meant to anybody who cares about it, I suppose.)

Anyway, perhaps figuring out if the usage is "okay" or not will get easier over time, but as it stands just from that cursory review, I would say that this makes reviewing code with `addr()` harder (and the "easiest" fix for that in a lot of cases is just to expose instead, since it doesn't require rewriting the code or carefully maintaining provenance of a pointer).


对，我指的是那些以前只用 addr 就可以处理的情况。通常可以直接比较指针，正因为如此，我才觉得这不算太糟。

> 我们已经说过，程序基本上随时都可能因栈溢出而中止（但作为 QoI 问题，通常不会这样），所以这件事也可以类似处理。不过话说回来，这有点荒谬，因为和栈溢出不同，我们知道这实际上永远不会发生。

> 我认为，很多“违规”实际上在语法形式上都是 `a.addr() == b.addr()`。

我不这么认为。我想不出你什么时候会直接把 `a.addr()` 和 `b.addr()` 进行比较。也许会做一些算术运算，以避免经过 `ptr::wrapping_{add,sub,offset}`（因为出于一些相当可疑的理由，人们有时觉得这些函数“不太正确”），或者类似的事情？

……

为了不那么抽象，我稍微看了一下 std，找了些违反这条规则、或者在这条规则下看起来比较可疑的代码。下面是一些会将地址与常量以外的对象进行比较的情况：

- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f207aa3913114c3326bc0b88acbd12b10244edf8/library/std/src/sys/pal/unix/stack_overflow/thread_info.rs （在锁中将 `errno_location().addr()` 用作线程 ID）

- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f207aa3913114c3326bc0b88acbd12b10244edf8/library/std/src/sys/pal/windows/mod.rs#L72。这是减法而不是比较，不过减法的结果确实会被比较，所以看起来类似。我的假设是这没问题，因为它们来自同一个分配？还是说这只在另一个模型下成立？

- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f207aa3913114c3326bc0b88acbd12b10244edf8/library/std/src/sys/pal/unix/stack_overflow.rs#L110 这里实际上将触发故障的地址与另一个地址范围进行了比较。感觉这或许是一个需要使用 expose_addr 的情况？保护页和故障地址的 provenance 肯定会相差十万八千里……嗯……又或者，我们可以直接宣布这种情况已经“足够特殊”，所以不构成问题？

- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f207aa3913114c3326bc0b88acbd12b10244edf8/library/std/src/path.rs#L1666-L1669 （又是对来自同一分配的指针调用 addr() → 做算术运算 → 用结果做某些事情。这类代码很多，剩下的我就不列了。）

messages.en:
So as far as I can tell, it's *almost* the case that LLVM only removes an allocation if it can prove that the program's behavior is the same no matter which (legal) address it chooses. So the program can convert the pointer to an address and check its lower bits, which are zero in any program due to alignment. It can do math where the base address cancels out (i.e. `x - x` simplifies to `0`). Also, LLVM will optimize `ptr1.addr() == ptr2.addr()` to just `ptr1 == ptr2`.

Now the only case where this doesn't apply is that LLVM is happy to constant fold `ptr1 == ptr2` to `false` even if both pointers are removed. This is a bit unfortunate for that model because it means that it removed the allocation even though not *all* choices for `ptr1.addr()` and `ptr2.addr()` lead to the same program behavior, because the choice where both are equal has different behavior.

So because of that, we cannot just inspect all possible choices for the address and require that the program behavior must be the same no matter what the chosen address is.
messages.zh:
所以据我所知，情况几乎是这样的：只有当 LLVM 能证明无论它选择哪个（合法）地址，程序的行为都相同时，它才会移除分配。因此，程序可以把指针转换成地址并检查其低位，而由于对齐要求，在任何程序中这些低位都是零。它也可以进行基地址会抵消的运算（也就是 `x - x` 会简化为 `0`）。此外，LLVM 会把 `ptr1.addr() == ptr2.addr()` 优化成 `ptr1 == ptr2`。

现在唯一不适用的情况是：即使两个指针都被移除了，LLVM 也很乐意把 `ptr1 == ptr2` 常量折叠为 `false`。这对那个模型来说有点遗憾，因为这意味着它移除了分配，尽管并非 `ptr1.addr()` 和 `ptr2.addr()` 的所有取值选择都会导致相同的程序行为：当两者相等时，程序行为就不同。

因此，我们不能简单地检查地址的所有可能取值，并要求无论选择哪个地址，程序行为都必须相同。

messages.en:
Actually, I think it would be good to change our documentation today to indicate that pointer equality and address equality could be different. It doesn't seem like we really have a choice here; the planes approach and its variations are the only solutions we came up with so far where the trade-off is somewhat reasonable (after quite a lot of proposals and discussion, both on the UCG issue and in this zulip thread). And we don't have to commit to a particular model yet; it is just very likely that an eventual solution will have to distinguish pointer and address equality.

I'd rather document this now, rather than wait for 5 years until someone proves an impossibility theorem. There is still a ton of code that didn't update to strict-provenance yet, and it would see the documentation on `addr()` once they decide to upgrade.

The impossibility theorem would probably be something like this:

> You can have at most 4 of the following:
> 1. `let _ = ptr.addr();` can be optimized away
> 2. `let ptr = alloc(); dealloc(ptr);` can be optimized away
> 3. integers do not carry provenance
> 4. `ptr1 == ptr2` is equivalent to `ptr1.addr() == ptr2.addr()` (assuming thin pointers)
> 5. `if ptr1 == ptr2 { assert_eq!(*ptr1, *ptr2); }` never panicks
messages.zh:
不可能性定理大概会是这样：

> 以下性质最多只能同时满足四项：
> 1. `let _ = ptr.addr();` 可以被优化掉。
> 2. `let ptr = alloc(); dealloc(ptr);` 可以被优化掉。
> 3. 整数不携带指针来源。
> 4. `ptr1 == ptr2` 等价于 `ptr1.addr() == ptr2.addr()`（假定是细指针）。
> 5. `if ptr1 == ptr2 { assert_eq!(*ptr1, *ptr2); }` 永远不会 panic。

messages.en:
(5) needs some caveat / reformulation to deal with the potential UB of the loads... like,
- ``if ptr1 == ptr2 { assert_eq!(*ptr1, *ptr2); }`` is refined by ``if ptr1 == ptr2 {  }``

or
- ``if ptr1 == ptr2 { assert_eq!(*ptr1, *ptr2); }`` is equivalent to ``if ptr1 == ptr2 {  let _val = *ptr1; let _val = *ptr2; }``
messages.zh:

或者：

messages.zh:
@_**niluxv|401145** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/625535186):


对，当然，这看起来很难，也很奇怪。但你们似乎都在选择的代价是……不匹配 LLVM 优化实际在做的事情。这难道不一样糟糕吗？

整个讨论的目的，就是 LLVM 在做一些我们希望保留的奇怪优化。因此，我们当然应该选择一种与之匹配的操作语义吧？

messages.en: That requires LLVM to first pick an opsem where what it's doing isn't unsound
messages.zh: 这要求 LLVM 先选定一种操作语义，使它所做的事情不再是不可靠的。

messages.en: LLVM is just assuming it can do *all* the optimisations, in particular it can use properties 1 to 5. The only option that is more in line with LLVM than picking poison 4 is picking 6: exhausting the address space is UB. But we kind of made a promise that safe code does not cause UB...
messages.zh: LLVM 只是直接假定它可以做*所有*优化，尤其可以使用性质 1 到 5。比选择代价 4 更贴近 LLVM 的唯一选项，是选择 6：耗尽地址空间属于 UB。但我们多少已经承诺过，安全代码不会导致 UB……

messages.en: LLVM has integer provenance
messages.zh: LLVM 有整数指针来源。

messages.en: No, they don't. Ralf convinced them...
messages.zh: 不，没有。Ralf 说服了他们……

messages.en: Oh, and even with "exhausting the address space is UB", LLVM is probably inconsistent, because it will probably move allocator calls up or down across non-`willreturn` operations.
messages.zh: 哦，而且即便规定“耗尽地址空间属于 UB”，LLVM 大概仍不一致，因为它很可能跨越非 `willreturn` 的操作，把分配器调用向上或向下移动。

```quote
Yeah, sure, it seems hard and weird. But the poison you all seem to be picking is ... to not match what LLVM's optimizations are actually doing. Which seems just as bad?
```

the only degree of freedom we have is to decide *which* of LLVM's optimizations we are breaking.

but also note that all this proposal does is remove a guarantee from `addr`.  it doesnt by itself break any optimizations. LLVM IR semantics and Rust semantics are not the same, we just have to be able to map the latter into the former, and fewer guarantees can only make that easier.

@_**Alice Ryhl|218683** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/625535907):

```quote
对，当然，这看起来很难，也很奇怪。但你们似乎都在选择的代价是……不匹配 LLVM 优化实际在做的事情。这难道不一样糟糕吗？
```

我们唯一的自由，就是决定要破坏 LLVM 的*哪些*优化。

不过也请注意，这个提议只是移除了 `addr` 的一个保证，本身不会破坏任何优化。LLVM IR 语义与 Rust 语义并不相同；我们只需要能把后者映射到前者，而减少保证只会让这件事更容易。

messages.en: the point of this issue is to make it so that *Rust can have a semantics at all* that is compatible with dead allocation removal
messages.zh: 这个 issue 的目的，是让 *Rust 至少能够拥有一种*与死分配消除兼容的语义。

messages.en: the new semantics are *still* compatible with "ptr cmp is just addr cmp" *if* we give up on dead allocation removal. but the new semantics also leave us the  breathing room to prefer dead allocation removal over "ptr cmp is just addr cmp". it doesn't commit to either choice, it just enables us to actually make a choice.
messages.zh: *如果*放弃死分配消除，新语义*仍然*兼容“指针比较就是地址比较”。但新语义也给我们留下了余地，可以优先保留死分配消除，而不是“指针比较就是地址比较”。它不承诺任何一个选择，只是让我们真正能够作出选择。

messages.en:
I thought about the fractions thing a bit more. My conclusion is that I think planes should be ~~integer~~`nat`-indexed. Basically we should abstractly think of the address as being some arbitrary unbounded natural number `n ∈ N`, and then `n % 2^64` is stored in the physical part of the pointer and `floor(n / 2^64)` is stored in the provenance as the "plane index".

IOW, I think your example that checks whether there's at most finitely many addresses between any two pointers should indeed demonstrate that yes there can be at most finitely many of them.
messages.zh:
我又想了想分数的问题。结论是，我认为平面应该用 ~~整数~~`nat`（自然数）索引。基本上，我们应该在抽象层面把地址看作任意无界自然数 `n ∈ N`，然后将 `n % 2^64` 存在指针的物理部分，将 `floor(n / 2^64)` 作为“平面索引”存在指针来源中。

换句话说，我认为你那个检查任意两个指针之间是否至多有有限多个地址的例子，确实应该表明：对，它们至多只能有有限多个。

messages.zh: 自然数。

@_**joboet|541962** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/627131539):
```quote
I want to point out that the proposed semantics create problems when testing `std` under miri
```

Yes, testing is a major problem.

> [And yes, testing is a real problem. You probably need static analysis or (runtime) taint analysis.](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/163013#issuecomment-5793593505)

The OOM case for `expose_provenance` should basically be treated as NB by miri. The best way to do that that I can think of (but very non-trivial to implement) would be to have a static analysis pass which determines which allocations get exposed (you can either choose to over-approximate, which means that some possible executions never get tested, or under-approximate, in which case you might actually hit the OOM), and then use this analysis as an input to miri, which will then always allocate these allocations in plane 0. If you go with the under-approximation, you could even combine this with some runtime administration of which facts about the allocation were already observed by the execution like @**Jules Bertholet** suggested and move the allocation to plane 0 if still possible, to further reduce the OOM rate.

@_**joboet|541962** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/627131539):
```quote
我想指出，提议的语义会给在 Miri 下测试 `std` 带来问题。
```

是的，测试是个大问题。

> [而且没错，测试确实是个问题。大概需要静态分析或（运行时）污点分析。](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/163013#issuecomment-5793593505)

Miri 基本上应该把 `expose_provenance` 的 OOM 情况当作 NB 处理。我能想到的最佳方法（但实现起来非常困难）是：先通过一个静态分析遍，确定哪些分配会被暴露（可以选择过近似，意味着某些可能执行永远测不到；也可以选择欠近似，此时可能真的遇到 OOM），然后把分析结果作为 Miri 的输入，让 Miri 始终在平面 0 分配这些对象。如果采用欠近似，甚至可以像 @**Jules Bertholet** 建议的那样，在运行时记录执行已经观察到该分配的哪些事实；只要仍然可行，就把分配移动到平面 0，以进一步降低 OOM 发生率。

messages.en: A kind of runtime taint analysis would be an easier option, not for testing code under newly allowed executions, but just for "linting" potentially problematic integer comparisons (so that a human can have a look). You tag every integer that is obtained using `addr` with the AllocId for the pointer. Subtracting two integers with the same AllocId gives a "pure" integer (this is to reduce the false positive rate, but can introduce some false negatives as well). Comparison of integers with different AllocIds (or one having an AllocId and the other being "pure") raises the warning. To support `expose_provenance` forcing plane 0, you could also treat every AllocId that has been exposed as "pure" integers instead. (This still has false positives if the expose comes after the comparison.)
messages.zh: 一种运行时污点分析会更容易实现。它不是为了在新允许的执行方式下测试代码，而只是为可能有问题的整数比较发出“lint”（供人检查）。给通过 `addr` 得到的每个整数标上对应指针的 AllocId。两个具有相同 AllocId 的整数相减，得到“纯”整数（这是为了降低误报率，但也会引入一些漏报）。比较具有不同 AllocId 的整数（或一个有 AllocId、另一个是“纯”整数），就发出警告。为支持 `expose_provenance` 强制进入平面 0，也可以把所有已暴露 AllocId 对应的整数视为“纯”整数。（如果暴露发生在比较之后，仍然会误报。）

messages.en: that still leaves the question of how you'd tell llvm not to optimize it away though, no?
messages.zh: 不过，这仍然留下一个问题：怎么告诉 LLVM 别把它优化掉，对吧？

messages.en:
(Pedantic: Since you can always move "forcing plane 0" up, calling such function early would be worst for opts/perf, not the best. But I don't think where you put it matters at all really.)

Even if we do not expose such forcing function, I think the compiler should definitely codegen `expose_provenance` as two intrinsics, one for the expose and one for the force. Indeed because you can hoist force up (except the alloc that produces the pointer) and sink expose down (except down a `with_exposed_provenance`).
messages.zh:
（较真一下：既然始终可以把“强制进入平面 0”上移，尽早调用这种函数对优化／性能其实最差，而非最好。但我认为实际上放在哪里根本无所谓。）

即使不公开这种强制函数，我也认为编译器绝对应该把 `expose_provenance` 生成为两个 intrinsic：一个负责暴露，一个负责强制平面。正是因为强制操作可以上提（但不能跨越产生指针的分配），而暴露操作可以下沉（但不能跨越 `with_exposed_provenance`）。

"Provenance monotonicity" is the property that adding more provenance to your program strictly refines its observable behavior at runtime. E.g. if you have a pointer with no provenance, and then an optimization gives it provenance, that optimization is valid

```quote
那是什么？
```

“来源信息单调性”指这样一个性质：给程序添加更多来源信息，只会精化它运行时可观察的行为。例如，一个指针原本没有来源信息，某项优化为它赋予来源信息，那么这项优化就是有效的。

messages.en: a usize read strips provenance. the write stores the provenance-less value back to memory.

messages.en: removing this roundtrip removes the provenance stripping and therefore *adds* provenance compared to the original execution

messages.en:
Neither model that I proposed above satisfies that property. My first approach was saying that pointer *values* always have (plane) provenance. The moment you interpret bytes to a pointer value, if the bytes don't carry provenance, the provenance for the pointer value is chosen non-deterministically. The second approach is to say that pointer values can have "no provenance" (like bytes can), but then I spec comparison when one pointer lacks provenance as non-deterministic.

Of course `ptr::without_provenance` doesn't produce a pointer without plane provenance. That would be unworkable. It is a magic function that creates a pointer with the specified address in the 0 plane. This doesn't contradict provenance monotonicity, because it is always the 0-plane, regardless of what is passed in.
messages.zh:
我上面提出的两种模型都不满足这个性质。第一种方案规定，指针值始终具有平面来源信息。将字节解释为指针值时，如果字节不带来源信息，就非确定性地为该指针值选择来源信息。第二种方案规定，指针值可以像字节一样“没有来源信息”，但只要比较的一方缺少来源信息，就将比较结果规定为非确定的。

当然，`ptr::without_provenance` 并不会生成没有平面来源信息的指针，那样无法工作。它是个神奇的函数，会在第 0 平面创建具有指定地址的指针。这不违反来源信息单调性，因为无论传入什么，它都始终是第 0 平面。

messages.en: The key point is "no provenance" doesn't mean 0-plane, it means "I have no idea which plane", so comparing it like a 0-plane pointer doesn't really make sense.
messages.zh: 关键是，“没有来源信息”不是第 0 平面，而是“完全不知道是哪个平面”，所以把它当作第 0 平面指针比较并不合理。

messages.en: the status quo is that pointer values can have no provenance.
messages.zh: 目前的模型允许指针值没有来源信息。

messages.en:
Hm, yeah, okay, this is tricky. If we make integers always encode plane 0, then, while the semantics is technically provenance-monotone, we still cannot optimise out
```rust
let x = ptr.read(); ptr.write(x);
```
because this is no longer something that "only" strips provenance, it is *changing* provenance (incomparably). That is unacceptable.
messages.zh:
嗯，好，这很棘手。如果让整数始终编码为第 0 平面，那么虽然严格来说语义满足来源信息单调性，我们仍然不能通过优化消除
```rust
let x = ptr.read(); ptr.write(x);
```
因为它不再“只是”剥离来源信息，而是在以不可比较的方式改变来源信息。这不可接受。

messages.en:
I mentioned it before, but I still think elided allocations should be treated as being "outside" of the range 0 to usize::MAX rather than having them be overlapping with each other. It matches what LLVM actually does with its optimizations better.

Yes, it means that even usize must have values outside of 0 to usize::MAX, which means even integers can have a form of provenance. But you know, I think it matches what LLVM does pretty well, since LLVM literally does escape analysis including on integers to determine whether it can elide an allocation or not. If the address "escapes", the allocation is not elided.

It can be a separate form of provenance from the one we have today. So ptr2int still loses the provenancen we know and love on pointers, but it retains the "symbolic value" of the usize if the allocation was optimized out.
messages.zh:
我之前提过，但我仍认为，被消除的分配应该被视为位于 0 到 usize::MAX 范围之外，而不是互相重叠。这更符合 LLVM 实际执行的优化。

是的，这意味着即使 usize 也必须能表示 0 到 usize::MAX 以外的值，因而整数也有某种形式的来源信息。不过我认为，这非常符合 LLVM 的行为，因为 LLVM 确实会进行逃逸分析，甚至对整数也如此，用来判断能否消除分配。如果地址“逃逸”，就不消除分配。

这可以是一种独立于现有机制的来源信息。因此 ptr2int 仍会丢失我们熟悉的指针来源信息，但如果分配被优化掉，它会保留 usize 的“符号值”。

No, always encoding integers as plane 0 provenance (in the byte) means that there is no "no provenance" byte anymore. The SB/TB provenance can be empty, but the plane would always have a "value". Technically prov. monotone (since adding prov. can only mean leaving the plane in tact, and adding SB/TB prov.), but completely useless.

Of all the awful choices presented so far, I still think losing this is the least awful. Unless someone comes up with a workable version of:

@_**Alice Ryhl|218683** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/627773372):

```quote
I mentioned it before, but I still think elided allocations should be treated as being "outside" of the range 0 to usize::MAX rather than having them be overlapping with each other. It matches what LLVM actually does with its optimizations better.

[…]
```

If we do accept that `let x = ptr.read(); ptr.write(x);` can't be optimized out in the general case, we will need to ensure it can still be elided in as many specific cases as possible. IOW, the compiler should be able to infer that `ptr` doesn't point to anything with provenance in as many cases as possible. So we'll have to be more aggressive about stripping provenance behind references.

```quote
7. `let x = ptr.read(); ptr.write(x);` 可以优化为 `let x = ptr.read();`，
```

@_**Alice Ryhl|218683** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/627773372):

```quote
[…]
```

如果确实接受一般情况下不能通过优化消除 `let x = ptr.read(); ptr.write(x);`，我们就需要确保仍能在尽可能多的具体场景消除它。换句话说，编译器应该尽可能推断出 `ptr` 指向的对象不携带来源信息。因此，我们必须更积极地剥离引用背后数据的来源信息。

messages.en: a no-provenance-monotonicity semantics is possible I think, while still allowing redundant store elimination. we just have to make ptr2int transmutes UB if they would otherwise drop provenance. that was the semantics I originally proposed many years ago but then @**Mario Carneiro** convinced me that we should go with provenance monotonicity instead. maybe we have to revise that choice...

I mean, it would be really a bad look if we told people "hey, do these things to placate miri and make your unsafe code more robust against our future changes" and then have it turn out that they'd be better off if they had done nothing. It's bad optics, and I fear that it makes it more likely that people will ignore our recommendations in the future.

That said, I think if we went this route, some hack to make direct provenance-stripping transmute of a pointer count as an expose would help a lot. I think this wouldn't have to count transmute-equivalent things like reads/writes through casts and so on, and I don't think it would have to count cases where the pointer is inside a struct or array or something like that.

Even just `if is_ptr::<Src>() && same_type::<Dst, usize>() { expose_provenance(p) } else { really_transmute::<Src, Dst>(p) }`. (Of course, a crater run to judge the damage would be necessary to justify such a hack)

我的意思是，如果我们告诉大家“这样做可以让 Miri 满意，也能让 unsafe 代码更能适应我们未来的变化”，结果最后发现他们什么都不做反而更好，那观感确实很糟。我担心这会增加大家将来忽视建议的可能性。

不过，如果走这条路，用一点特殊处理，将直接剥离指针来源信息的 transmute 视为一次暴露来源信息，应该会有很大帮助。我认为不必包括通过强制转换后读写等与 transmute 等效的操作，也不必包括指针位于结构体或数组内部的情况。

甚至可以只是 `if is_ptr::<Src>() && same_type::<Dst, usize>() { expose_provenance(p) } else { really_transmute::<Src, Dst>(p) }`。（当然，需要跑一次 Crater 评估影响，才能证明这种特殊处理值得做。）

messages.en: I think this would make freeze/frozen (https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/4001) much less useful too, unless that makes it 'safe' somehow. One of the main use cases I can think of for freeze is something like using calloc for `vec![value; N]` if `value` happens to be all-bytes-zero (obviously we'd only do this for cases where `size_of_val(&value)` is small enough too), in order to optimize cases like `vec![None; N]` or `vec![SomeEnum::VariantThatHasZeroValue; N]`.

messages.en:
I feel like there is an easy-to-teach semantics here:
- A pointer byte can store a value above 255
- But non-provenance-having types can't, so if you transmute such a byte to such a value, you get UB
- `addr()` OOMs if a pointer is outside the `0..=usize::MAX` range
messages.zh:
我觉得这里有一套容易讲清楚的语义：
- 指针字节可以存储大于 255 的值。
- 不携带来源信息的类型不能，所以将这样的字节 transmute 为这种类型的值会导致 UB。
- 如果指针位于 `0..=usize::MAX` 之外，`addr()` 就触发 OOM。

messages.en: And maybe `freeze` or whatever else can OOM too.
messages.zh: 也许 `freeze` 或其他操作也可以触发 OOM。

messages.en: `with_addr` would also force a pointer back into the plane 0 range.
messages.zh: `with_addr` 也会强制将指针带回第 0 平面的范围。

messages.en:
Before we start discussing all kinds of crazy semantics, I want to point out two things.
* If we can afford a multi-stage optimisation pipeline, some options are less bad than they look (for opts), because different stages can potentially pick different poisons.
* Assumption (8) in the :headstone: Theorem is actually *very strong*; I think we can break it without declaring war on (`unsafe`) code authors.
messages.zh:
在开始讨论各种疯狂语义之前，我想指出两点。
* 如果能承担多阶段优化流水线的代价，有些选项对优化而言没有看起来那么糟，因为不同阶段可以选择承受不同的坏处。
* :headstone: 定理中的假设 8 实际上非常强；我认为可以打破它，而不必向 `unsafe` 代码作者宣战。

messages.en:
Assumption 8?? You saying this already makes me want to take out my pitchfork :eyes:
How would you even define `null` so as to not have assumption 8 hold?
messages.zh:
假设 8？？你这么一说我已经想拿起草叉了 :eyes: 
你到底要怎样定义 `null`，才能让假设 8 不成立？

messages.en:
On the first. Multi-stage optimisation sucks for engineering reasons (e.g. which stage IR is the input for LTO? and some optimisation pass might be beneficial at multiple stages, but running it in all might be costly). But if we can afford it, it can sometimes give us almost a "best of both world".

Say we take a planes semantics that compromises on (7). That is unacceptable for optimisations. But I *think* you can "refine" the semantics to one where `addr` is guaranteed to OOM on non-zero plane. At this point you loose (1) (`addr` purity) but you gain (7) back. So now you can still remove those "trivial" stores. And you can move to a third stage, where `alloc` is only allowed to allocate in plane 0. You loose (2) (dead alloc elimination), but gain (1) back.

(I'm not completely sure whether (7) -> (1) is possible, but (1) -> (2) definitely is.)
messages.zh:
先说第一点。多阶段优化在工程上很麻烦（例如，LTO 输入的是哪个阶段的 IR？有些优化 pass 在多个阶段都有益，但每个阶段都运行可能成本很高）。不过，如果我们承受得起，有时几乎能兼得两全。

假设采用一种在第 7 条上妥协的平面语义，这对优化不可接受。但我认为，可以将其精化为：`addr` 在非第 0 平面上保证 OOM。此时失去第 1 条（`addr` 的纯性），但重新获得第 7 条。因此仍可消除那些“平凡”的存储。之后还可以进入第三阶段，只允许 `alloc` 在第 0 平面分配。这样失去第 2 条（无用分配消除），但重新获得第 1 条。

（我不完全确定第 7 条 -> 第 1 条是否可行，但第 1 条 -> 第 2 条肯定可以。）

messages.en: In assumption 8, you're overwriting the pointer with `0usize`. Are you suggesting this is the same as `with_addr(0)`, or that you don't know which plane the pointer belongs to?
messages.zh: 假设 8 中，你用 `0usize` 覆盖了指针。你是说这等价于 `with_addr(0)`，还是说无法知道这个指针属于哪个平面？

messages.en: And for people doing zero-initialisation, we can be so nice to magically make `MaybeUninit::zeroed` store zero-plane in all the initialized bytes, and similar for `GlobalAlloc::alloc_zeroed`. That makes the `ptr::eq` semantics less of a footgun.
messages.zh: 对于做零初始化的人，我们可以贴心地让 `MaybeUninit::zeroed` 神奇地在所有已初始化字节中存入第 0 平面，`GlobalAlloc::alloc_zeroed` 也类似。这样 `ptr::eq` 语义就不那么容易误用。

messages.en: @**Max|960514** I'm suggesting that storing (i.e. encoding) `0usize` clears the plane. The byte has no plane, and therefore decoding as pointer + pointer comparison cannot give any sensible answer.
messages.zh: @**Max|960514** 我的建议是，存储（也就是编码）`0usize` 会清除平面。字节没有平面，因此将其解码为指针再比较指针，不可能得到有意义的答案。

messages.en: What do you mean by "no plane"? Does it compare equal to itself?
messages.zh: “没有平面”是什么意思？它与自身比较会相等吗？

messages.en: `with_addr(0)` cannot change the plane
messages.zh: `with_addr(0)` 不能改变平面。

messages.en: I mean the result of transmuting `0usize` to a pointer
messages.zh: 我是指把 `0usize` transmute 为指针得到的结果。

messages.en: Does that compare equal to another pointer created that way
messages.zh: 它与另一个以同样方式创建的指针比较，会相等吗？

messages.en: Yes, it compares equal with itself, but comparison with any other value would be non-det.
messages.zh: 是的，它与自身相等，但与任何其他值比较时，结果是非确定的。

messages.en: That would still make `==` for pointers not an equivalence relation, no?
messages.zh: 这样指针的 `==` 仍然不是等价关系，对吧？

messages.en: It is basically, if you compare this pointer with any other pointer, then the pointer chooses non-det for just this single comparison a plane.
messages.zh: 基本上，如果把这个指针与任何其他指针比较，它就会仅针对这一次比较，非确定性地选择一个平面。

messages.en: Hm, that is bad
messages.zh: 嗯，这不太好。

messages.en: Why are pointers `Eq`? :sob:
messages.zh: 指针为什么要实现 `Eq`？:sob:

messages.en: :vi_fon: regret
messages.zh: :vi_fon: 后悔。

messages.en: maybe we can make all pointers with address 0 compare equal? but then `a.wrapping_add(n) == b.wrapping_add(n)` is no longer equivalent to `a == b`. that doesn't sound reasonable either...
messages.zh: 也许可以让所有地址为 0 的指针都比较相等？但这样 `a.wrapping_add(n) == b.wrapping_add(n)` 就不再等价于 `a == b`，听起来也不合理……

messages.en: you can already do that with `NonNull::new(…).is_none()`, I think
messages.zh: 我想，用 `NonNull::new(…).is_none()` 已经能做到这一点。

messages.en: oh `NonNull` is fun. which addr-0 pointer does transmuting `None::<NonNull>` give you? (presumably `null`, but this still feels cursed)
messages.zh: 哦，`NonNull` 真有意思。transmute `None::<NonNull>` 会得到哪个地址为 0 的指针？（大概是 `null`，但还是感觉很邪门。）

messages.en: What was the problem with making pointers with "no plane" be in plane 0 again?
messages.zh: 让“没有平面”的指针属于第 0 平面，到底有什么问题来着？

messages.en: That you loose (7)
messages.zh: 那会失去第 7 条。

messages.en:
@_**Max|960514** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628161399):
```quote
oh `NonNull` is fun. which addr-0 pointer does transmuting `None::<NonNull>` give you? (presumably `null`, but this still feels cursed)
```

assuming transmutes are transitive, it's the same as transmuting `[0_u8; size_of::<usize>()]` (or equivalently `0_usize`), so hopefully it's the same as `ptr::null()` returns
messages.zh:
@_**Max|960514** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628161399):
```quote
哦，`NonNull` 真有意思。transmute `None::<NonNull>` 会得到哪个地址为 0 的指针？（大概是 `null`，但还是感觉很邪门。）
```

假设 transmute 具有传递性，那么这等价于 transmute `[0_u8; size_of::<usize>()]`（或等价的 `0_usize`），所以希望它与 `ptr::null()` 返回的结果相同。

messages.en: the option null popinter docs guarantee that `None::<NonNull<T>>` transmutes to `[0_u8; size_of::<thin ptr>()]` for `T: Sized`
messages.zh: Option 空指针优化的文档保证，对于 `T: Sized`，`None::<NonNull<T>>` 会 transmute 为 `[0_u8; size_of::<thin ptr>()]`。

messages.en: `ptr::null` would presumably be plane 0, but we can't pick the result of reading a usize as pointer as plane 0 without violating (7), like explained above
messages.zh: `ptr::null` 想必属于第 0 平面，但如上所述，我们不能把将 usize 读作指针的结果指定为第 0 平面，否则会违反第 7 条。

messages.en: oh right `ptr::null` is implemented as `without_provenance`, which is Special(tm). though it is currently implemented as a transmute so :ferrisclueless:
messages.zh: 哦对，`ptr::null` 实现为特殊的 `without_provenance`。不过它目前又是通过 transmute 实现的，所以 :ferrisclueless:

messages.en: currently™
messages.zh: 目前™。

messages.en: the core libraries truly are peak ostrich
messages.zh: 核心库真是鸵鸟策略的巅峰。

messages.en: i mean it all makes perfect sense if you ignore that the address space is finite ^^
messages.zh: 我是说，只要忽略地址空间有限这一事实，一切都完全说得通 ^^

messages.en:
This can of worms is getting larger with the day. Let me summarise the most promising directions we still have:
1. Multi-stage (7) -> (1) -> (2). Every stage gives up on an optimisation that would in itself be unacceptable, but the whole chain would probably still optimise rather well.
2. (3): integers have provenance; do something like in the paper, and accept that we emit bounds-checks in real world code.
3. (10): decoding pointers as integers is UB. Massive change from status-quo, but Ralf has ideas.
4. (*Changed*) (8): encode integers with non-deterministic plane. Multi-stage (8) -> (7) -> (1) -> (2) likely possible.
messages.zh:
这堆麻烦与日俱增。总结一下目前最有希望的方向：
1. 多阶段第 7 条 -> 第 1 条 -> 第 2 条。每个阶段都放弃一项单看不可接受的优化，但整条链可能仍能优化得很好。
2. 第 3 条：整数携带来源信息，采用论文中的类似方案，并接受在现实代码中生成边界检查。
3. 第 10 条：将指针解码为整数是 UB。这与现状有很大差异，但 Ralf 有一些想法。
4. （已修改）第 8 条：以非确定性的平面编码整数。多阶段第 8 条 -> 第 7 条 -> 第 1 条 -> 第 2 条 很可能可行。

messages.en: 5. stick our heads in the sand by saying that allocations can be optimized away, even if not justified by the opsem
messages.zh: 5. 把头埋进沙子：即使操作语义无法证明合理，也宣称可以优化消除分配。

messages.en: Note that for option 3, we don't have to say that decoding *all* pointers as integers is UB, just the ones with non-zero plane
messages.zh: 注意，对于选项 3，不必规定将所有指针解码为整数都是 UB，只需针对非第 0 平面的指针。

messages.en: all this is making me think it would be better to declare OOM as UB but as a QoI matter we try to just return allocation errors or do normal stack overflow handling
messages.zh: 这一切让我觉得，也许最好直接把 OOM 定义为 UB，但作为实现质量要求，尽量只返回分配错误，或进行常规栈溢出处理。

messages.en: that way pointer addresses retain sane semantics
messages.zh: 这样指针地址就能保留合理的语义。

messages.en: the friendly ostrich approach
messages.zh: 友好的鸵鸟方案。

messages.en: it occasionally pops its head up to say hi
messages.zh: 它偶尔还会抬起头来打个招呼。

messages.en: Also known as abandoning (6), "a fully safe program cannot hit UB"
messages.zh: 也就是放弃第 6 条：“完全安全的程序不会遇到 UB”。

messages.en: we already have other ways a fully safe program can cause UB, e.g. opening `/proc/self/mem` and writing, having OOM technically be UB seems ok to me because it's unlikely to cause problems in practice since the behavior you'll get is non-deterministically reporting an allocation failure or not rather than most of the more severe consequences typically associated with UB.
messages.zh: 完全安全的程序本来就有其他方式引发 UB，例如打开 `/proc/self/mem` 并写入。我觉得严格来说将 OOM 视为 UB 可以接受，因为实践中不太可能造成问题：表现只是非确定性地报告或不报告分配失败，而不是通常与 UB 相关的那些更严重后果。

messages.en:
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628247865):
```quote
e.g. opening `/proc/self/mem` and writing
```

Eh, that's not really "unsound", it's just outside of the environment model. Like `println!("please smash this computer's cpu with a hammer");` and then the user smashes your computer's CPU with a hammer. Some external party is reacting to your program's observable behavior and then choosing to muck around in the Abstract Machine
messages.zh:
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628247865):
```quote
例如打开 `/proc/self/mem` 并写入
```

呃，这其实并不是“不健全”，而是超出了环境模型。就像 `println!("please smash this computer's cpu with a hammer");`，然后用户真的用锤子砸了电脑的 CPU。某个外部参与者对程序的可观察行为作出响应，然后选择干扰抽象机。

messages.en: Allocation isn't observable behavior, it's not allowed to trigger a response from the environment
messages.zh: 分配不是可观察行为，不允许触发环境的响应。

messages.en: well technically it often does, e.g. on linux if you allocate too much memory your program will get killed and/or sent signals that it needs to reduce memory usage.
messages.zh: 严格来说，它经常会。例如在 Linux 上，分配太多内存会导致程序被杀死，或者收到要求减少内存使用的信号。

messages.en:
@_**Thom Chiovoloni|209168** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628110984):
```quote
This would also make code which uses `transmute` as an `addr` shim [...], which would be unfortunate, as that code is *trying* to do the right thing, and was probably changed to this from `as usize` in order to make miri happier.
```

We can just build in a hack so that ptr2int `transmute!` doesn't do a transmute in the opsem but a `addr` call instead. `transmute!` knows the input and output types at compile time after all. And we can do an automated fix over an edition boundary.
messages.zh:
@_**Thom Chiovoloni|209168** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628110984):
```quote
这也会影响把 `transmute` 用作 `addr` 替代实现的代码……这很遗憾，因为这些代码是在努力做正确的事情，很可能正是为了让 Miri 更满意，才从 `as usize` 改成这样。
```

我们可以直接内置一个特殊处理，让 ptr2int `transmute!` 在操作语义中不执行 transmute，而是调用 `addr`。毕竟 `transmute!` 在编译时知道输入与输出类型。然后可以跨 edition 边界提供自动修复。

messages.en:
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628249377):
```quote
well technically it often does, e.g. on linux if you allocate too much memory your program will get killed and/or sent signals that it needs to reduce memory usage.
```

The environment aborting the program is very different from the program having UB in my opinion. Saying that OOM is UB amounts to say that a program may have UB at any time non-deterministically. I don't think that's a good property to have.
messages.zh:
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628249377):
```quote
严格来说，它经常会。例如在 Linux 上，分配太多内存会导致程序被杀死，或者收到要求减少内存使用的信号。
```

我认为，环境终止程序与程序具有 UB 是非常不同的。说 OOM 是 UB，等于说程序随时可能非确定性地出现 UB。我不认为这是一个好性质。

@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628127074):

```quote
If we treat `addr` as different than a ptrtoint transmute, do we still want it to be pure?
```

Yes, if `addr` need not be pure we don't need to have these discussions. We just pick (1) and are done.
messages.zh:
@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628127074):

```quote
如果把 `addr` 与 ptrtoint transmute 区分开，我们还希望它是纯操作吗？
```

是的，如果 `addr` 不必是纯操作，我们就无需展开这些讨论，直接选择第 1 条就结束了。

messages.en:
@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628132081):
```quote
If `.addr()` is equivalent to transmuting to `usize`, that would not be the case, because that transmute definitely should be pure. But if they aren't equivalent, it's no longer a problem
```

It is `.addr` that is used in e.g. `map_addr`; making it impure would definitely hurt optimisations a lot. ptr2int `transmute!` is probably uncommon. (But `usize` load from memory being `willreturn` is really crucial indeed.)
messages.zh:
@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628132081):
```quote
如果 `.addr()` 等价于 transmute 为 `usize`，情况就不同了，因为这个 transmute 显然应该是纯操作。但如果两者不等价，就不再有问题。
```

例如 `map_addr` 使用的就是 `.addr`，把它变成不纯操作肯定会大幅影响优化。ptr2int `transmute!` 大概并不常见。（但从内存加载 `usize` 具有 `willreturn`，确实至关重要。）

@_**niluxv|401145** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628160731):
```quote
Why are pointers `Eq`? :sob:
```

Oh, there was still my earlier proposal of making pointer decode non-det. if the byte lacks plane information. That breaks (7), but if we move the non-det. to the integer encode, then I think we only break (8). Are there *important* optimisations which need encode to be deterministic?
messages.zh:
@_**niluxv|401145** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628160731):


哦，还有我之前的提议：如果字节缺少平面信息，就让指针解码是非确定的。这会打破第 7 条，但如果把非确定性移到整数编码上，我认为就只打破第 8 条。有哪些重要优化需要编码是确定性的？

messages.en:
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628249377):
```quote
if you allocate too much memory your program will get killed
```

That part we can explain. We specify that your program can OOM *at any point*. It is not *caused by* the allocations in the AM. (For signals we can similarly say that you can receive a signal at any point for no reason whatsoever.)
messages.zh:
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628249377):
```quote
如果分配太多内存，程序就会被杀死
```

这部分可以解释。我们规定程序在任何时刻都可能 OOM；这并不是由抽象机中的分配导致的。（对于信号，同样可以说任何时刻都可能无缘无故收到一个信号。）

messages.en: (Minor detail, but for signals it depends which ones. Those that may result from what the AM implementation does are indeed uncontrolled and must be modeled as fully non-det. Otherwise they can follow an agreed protocol between the program and the environment, so they don't need to be modeled as fully non-det. They are "regular observable behavior".)
messages.zh: （一个小细节：对于信号，这取决于具体种类。由抽象机实现行为引起的信号确实不受控，必须建模为完全非确定的。其他信号则可以遵循程序与环境约定的协议，因此无需完全非确定地建模。它们属于“常规可观察行为”。）

messages.en:
@_**Julien Cretin (ia0)|117910** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628280909):
````quote
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628249377):
```quote
well technically it often does, e.g. on linux if you allocate too much memory your program will get killed and/or sent signals that it needs to reduce memory usage.
```

The environment aborting the program is very different from the program having UB in my opinion. Saying that OOM is UB amounts to say that a program may have UB at any time non-deterministically. I don't think that's a good property to have.
````

ok, maybe limit the UB to OOM caused by running out of address space (for whatever address space you're allocating in, e.g. on 64-bit it could be limited to 47-bits due to addressing limitations), so where `usize::BITS >= 32` you can't get UB from allocating 1GB of total memory, but if you try to allocate >4GB on a 32-bit target then that's UB because the compiler could optimize out some of those allocations so not all the allocations semantically performed by the unoptimized program can fit in 32-bits even though the optimized program can complete successfully -- those optimizations are valid even though they change the program from reporting OOM to running successfully because trying to allocate >4GB of total memory is UB
messages.zh:
@_**Julien Cretin (ia0)|117910** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628280909):
````quote
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628249377):
```quote
严格来说，它经常会。例如在 Linux 上，分配太多内存会导致程序被杀死，或者收到要求减少内存使用的信号。
```

我认为，环境终止程序与程序具有 UB 是非常不同的。说 OOM 是 UB，等于说程序随时可能非确定性地出现 UB。我不认为这是一个好性质。
````

好吧，也许只把地址空间耗尽造成的 OOM 视为 UB（具体是哪种地址空间，取决于分配位置；例如 64 位平台可能因寻址限制只能用 47 位）。这样，当 `usize::BITS >= 32` 时，总共分配 1GB 内存不会引起 UB；但若在 32 位目标平台尝试分配超过 4GB，就是 UB。因为编译器可能消除部分分配，导致未优化程序在语义上执行的所有分配无法装进 32 位地址空间，但优化后的程序却能成功运行。即使这些优化把报告 OOM 改成了成功运行，它们仍然有效，因为尝试总共分配超过 4GB 内存本来就是 UB。

messages.en: OOM caused by the OS not having enough free memory or just saying no even though there's enough address space available is not UB
messages.zh: 由操作系统空闲内存不足，或即使地址空间足够却仍拒绝分配而造成的 OOM，不是 UB。

messages.en: Ah ok, that's less worse then. The problem is only what Jules said: safe programs can have UB. I can see how this could be an option (I don't have opinion there).
messages.zh: 啊，好，那就没那么糟了。问题只剩 Jules 说的：safe 程序可能有 UB。我能理解这可以是一种选择（我对此没有倾向）。

messages.en: Besides breaking the key promise of safe Rust ("a program written fully in safe Rust does no exhibit UB"), that also means that you cannot do optimisations which increase the memory usage. And there definitely are optimisations that technically do.
messages.zh: 除了打破 safe Rust 的核心承诺——“完全用 safe Rust 编写的程序不会出现 UB”——这还意味着不能进行增加内存使用的优化。而确实存在严格来说会增加内存使用的优化。

messages.en: if variable creation can be UB then we have failed
messages.zh: 如果创建变量都可能是 UB，那我们就失败了。

messages.en: well, we can already miscompile creating a new local variable as a stack overflow instead of working, so we already have that problem where optimizations adding new local variables can cause a stack overflow changing the behavior of the program
messages.zh: 嗯，我们已经可能把本应成功的新局部变量创建错误编译成栈溢出，所以已经存在这种问题：添加新局部变量的优化可能导致栈溢出，改变程序行为。

messages.en: “Any program may randomly abort” is sad but not nearly as bad as “any program may randomly have UB”
messages.zh: “任何程序都可能随机中止”固然令人遗憾，但远没有“任何程序都可能随机产生 UB”那么糟糕。

messages.en: well, on most embedded platforms a stack overflow *is* UB since they have no way to detect you ran out of stack space and are now scribbling over the heap and/or global variables
messages.zh: 不过，在大多数嵌入式平台上，栈溢出本身*就是* UB，因为它们无法检测栈空间已经耗尽，此时程序已经在覆盖堆和／或全局变量了。

messages.en: a platform limitation is not the same as the language itself having a giant gaping hole on all platforms
messages.zh: 平台的局限，与语言本身在所有平台上都存在一个巨大的漏洞，是两回事。

messages.en: you can make a platform/compiler that automatically grows the stack (yes i know this is complicated with pinning) and avoids stack overflows reasonably well (and one without `/proc/self/mem`). you can't make the address space infinite
messages.zh: 你可以设计能够自动扩展栈的平台／编译器（对，我知道这会与 pinning 产生复杂交互），从而相当有效地避免栈溢出，也可以让平台没有 `/proc/self/mem`。但你无法让地址空间变成无限大。

messages.en: FWIW, some of us embedded folks are careful to put the stack in a location where a stack overflow will cause a hard fault instead of UB. It's not always possible (particularly if multiple threads are present), but e.g. Tock OS should catch stack overflow on the vast majority of its platforms.
messages.zh: 补充一点，我们有些做嵌入式的人会谨慎选择栈的位置，让栈溢出导致硬件故障而不是 UB。这并非总能做到，尤其在存在多个线程时；不过，例如 Tock OS 应该能在其绝大多数平台上捕获栈溢出。

messages.en:
Trying to wrap me head around this (as someone who is neither an expert on compilers or on opsem, but who would ideally like to learn enough to at least understand the opsem discussions):
The problem with the planes model proposed so far is that a ptr -> int transmute drops the plane ID, which breaks provenance monoticity.
The solution that seems obvious to me is to make `.addr()` and ptr->int transmutes force plane 0. That compromises on (1), and for (4) makes `ptr1 == ptr2` always compare equal to `ptr1.addr() == ptr2.addr()` but with different side effects. But as I understand the discussion, that is likely a no-go because of the optimization impacts?
My intuition has been that `.addr()` and ptr->int transmutes are only used in situations where you're already doing something that prevents the allocation from being optimized away, so the impact on real code is probably small. But perhaps my intuition is misguided.
messages.zh:
我想理清这里的思路（我既不是编译器专家，也不是操作语义专家，但希望至少能学到足以理解这些讨论的程度）：
目前提出的平面模型的问题在于，ptr -> int 的 transmute 会丢掉平面 ID，从而破坏 provenance 的单调性。
我觉得直观的解决办法是，让 `.addr()` 和 ptr->int 的 transmute 都强制进入平面 0。这会牺牲性质 (1)；对于 (4)，则使 `ptr1 == ptr2` 的比较结果始终与 `ptr1.addr() == ptr2.addr()` 相同，但副作用不同。不过，按照我对讨论的理解，这种做法可能因为对优化的影响而不可接受？
我的直觉是，使用 `.addr()` 和 ptr->int transmute 时，通常已经在做某些会阻止分配被优化掉的事情了，因此对实际代码的影响可能很小。但也许我的直觉有误。

messages.en: The problem is, if you do a load and then store with integer type from some pointer, LLVM doesn't necessarily know whether there was originally provenance there. Even if there "probably" wasn't, if the compiler can't *prove* it then it can't do the optimization.
messages.zh: 问题在于，如果你通过某个指针，先以整数类型加载，再存储，LLVM 不一定知道那里原来是否有 provenance。即使“很可能”没有，只要编译器无法*证明*这一点，就不能执行该优化。

messages.en: Ah I see, `core::ptr::read::<usize>()` would have a force-plane-0 operation iff `*ptr`is a pointer. Which the compiler doesn't know, because memory is untyped. So the actual opsem would probably have to make `core::ptr::read::<usize>()` *always* be a force-plane-0 on `*ptr`, which would scatter that operation everywhere.
messages.zh: 啊，我明白了：当且仅当 `*ptr` 是指针时，`core::ptr::read::<usize>()` 才会执行一次“强制进入平面 0”的操作。但内存没有类型，所以编译器不知道这一点。因此，实际操作语义可能不得不规定：`core::ptr::read::<usize>()` *总是*对 `*ptr` 强制使用平面 0，这样该操作就会散布得到处都是。

@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628128593):
```quote
I feel like there is an easy-to-teach semantics here:
- A pointer byte can store a value above 255
- But non-provenance-having types can't, so if you transmute such a byte to such a value, you get UB
- `addr()` OOMs if a pointer is outside the `0..=usize::MAX` range
```

The big question: what are the semantics of `<=`?
messages.zh:
@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628128593):
```quote
我觉得这里有一套容易讲明白的语义：
- 指针字节可以存储大于 255 的值。
- 但不具有 provenance 的类型不行，所以如果把这样的字节 transmute 为那样的值，就会触发 UB。
- 如果指针超出 `0..=usize::MAX` 范围，`addr()` 就会 OOM。
```

关键问题是：`<=` 的语义是什么？

messages.en: so then `let a = *(&&v as *const _ as *const usize)` can be UB even though all bytes are initialized?
messages.zh: 那么，即使所有字节都已经初始化，`let a = *(&&v as *const _ as *const usize)` 仍然可能是 UB？

messages.en: Yes
messages.zh: 是的。

messages.en: I'd call that extremely suspicious semantics
messages.zh: 我会说，这种语义非常可疑。

messages.en: imo it should always behave like some combination of `ptrtoint` and `ptrtoaddr`
messages.zh: 我认为它应该始终表现为 `ptrtoint` 与 `ptrtoaddr` 的某种组合。

messages.en:
> but (wrap) adding `addr` to both sides of the equation should not affect the result (reasonable semantics)

Is that necessary?  Why can't null be treated specially, where pointers with address 0 are guaranteed to equal null, but otherwise pointers with the same addresses don't necessarily compare equal?
messages.zh:
> 但是，给等式两边都以回绕方式加上 `addr`，不应改变结果（合理的语义）。

这一定有必要吗？为什么不能特殊对待 null：保证地址为 0 的指针等于 null，但除此之外，地址相同的指针不一定比较相等？

On another note.
@_**niluxv|401145** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628167132):
```quote
1. (3): integers have provenance; do something like in the paper, and accept that we emit bounds-checks in real world code.
```
After skimming the paper it seems suspicious to me.  They essentially introduce a new integer type where overflowing operations can either trap or act like a mathematical integer (resulting in values outside the normal range for the type).  But this couldn't really be retrofitted onto preexisting integer types.  Both LLVM optimizations and Rust programmers assume that arithmetic either traps or *wraps*.  If you do, say, `x * 32 / 32`, for `x: usize` (or any other integer type), then either the operation will trap or the result *must* have the top 5 bits clear.  Therefore this type from the paper would have to be a brand new integer type that is designed specifically to store addresses and isn't useful for anything else.  But at that point why even have an integer type?  Why not just stick to pointer types.
messages.zh:
另外说一点。
@_**niluxv|401145** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628167132):
```quote
1. (3)：整数具有 provenance；采用类似论文中的做法，并接受在现实代码中生成边界检查。
```
我粗读了这篇论文，感觉其方案有些可疑。他们实质上引入了一种新的整数类型：发生溢出的运算既可以陷入，也可以像数学整数那样计算，产生超出该类型正常范围的值。但这无法直接改造到现有整数类型上。LLVM 的优化和 Rust 程序员都假定，算术运算要么陷入，要么*回绕*。例如，对 `x: usize`（或其他整数类型）的值执行 `x * 32 / 32`，运算要么陷入，要么结果的最高 5 位*必须*为零。因此，论文中的类型必须是一种全新的整数类型，专门用于存储地址，除此之外没有别的用途。但既然如此，为什么还需要一种整数类型？为什么不直接使用指针类型呢？

messages.en: In any case, at the risk of pedantry, the paper does **not** have provenance for integers.  Its approach of allowing infinite integer range is essentially an alternative to provenance.  But provenance is arguably a better, less lossy model.  Maybe.
messages.zh: 无论如何，冒着显得咬文嚼字的风险，我还是要指出：论文**没有**给整数引入 provenance。允许整数取值范围无限大的方法，实质上是 provenance 的替代方案。不过，provenance 可以说是一个更好、信息损失更少的模型。也许吧。

@_**comex|198590** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628579382):
```quote
> but (wrap) adding `addr` to both sides of the equation should not affect the result (reasonable semantics)

Is that necessary?  Why can't null be treated specially, where pointers with address 0 are guaranteed to equal null, but otherwise pointers with the same addresses don't necessarily compare equal?
```

Yes, we could treat address 0 special; however, I think every programmer would assume that wrap adding on both sides doesn't change equality, and it seems like a useful optimisation that LLVM would want to do. If you don't find it a "reasonable" assumption, then read (8) as "`ptr.write::<usize>(n); ptr.read::<*const u8>() == null().wrapping_add(n)` evaluates to `true` (unless UB), for every `n`" instead.
messages.zh:
@_**comex|198590** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628579382):
```quote
> 但是，给等式两边都以回绕方式加上 `addr`，不应改变结果（合理的语义）。

这一定有必要吗？为什么不能特殊对待 null：保证地址为 0 的指针等于 null，但除此之外，地址相同的指针不一定比较相等？
```

是的，我们可以特殊处理地址 0；但我认为，每个程序员都会假定，在等式两边都执行回绕加法不会改变相等关系，而且这似乎也是 LLVM 会想采用的一项有用优化。如果你不认为这个假设“合理”，那么也可以把 (8) 改读为：“对于每个 `n`，`ptr.write::<usize>(n); ptr.read::<*const u8>() == null().wrapping_add(n)` 都求值为 `true`（除非发生 UB）。”

messages.en: FWIW many (if not most) optimizations LLVM does around pointer equality today are incorrect. See #162078, #163541
messages.zh: 补充一点，LLVM 目前围绕指针相等性所做的许多优化——即使不说大多数——都是不正确的。参见 #162078、#163541。

messages.en: But I think programmers would like to assume certain things about equality. Maybe `null` being special is okay?
messages.zh: 不过，我认为程序员会希望对相等性作出某些假设。也许特殊处理 `null` 是可以接受的？

注意，我们已经有一个“provenance”的定义，即：

@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/627851868):

messages.en: I'm not sure I really like that definition. Undef isn't "represented in the physical machine bits", but it's not provenance

messages.en: I would say that for something to be "provenance", there also needs to be a pure operation that strips it and gets only the "physical machine bits"

messages.en: Others could say that for something to be "provenance" it should represent something about the past or history of the thing it's attached to, as to match one possible meaning of "provenance" in English. But that's just terminology. I don't find that interesting and usually understand what people mean without it. I was just pointing out that there has been a claim for a definition.
messages.zh: 也有人可能会说，要把某种东西称为“provenance”，它应当表示所附着对象的过去或历史，以对应英文 provenance 的一种含义。但这只是术语问题。我觉得这没什么意思，通常也不靠这个就能理解大家的意思。我只是指出，已经有人声称给出过一个定义。

Well, the paper [(re-linking it for reference)](https://cambium.inria.fr/~yzakowsk/papers/vellvm-mm.pdf) *claims* to not have provenance for integers:
> Our implementation does not track provenance through integers, so our integer–pointer casts will always yield a pointer with a wildcard provenance, which is safe, but can limit optimizations in rare cases (see the discussion in [31]).

But sure, it depends on how you define 'provenance'.
messages.zh:
不过，这篇论文（[重新附上链接，便于参考](https://cambium.inria.fr/~yzakowsk/papers/vellvm-mm.pdf)）*声称*它不为整数保留 provenance：
> 我们的实现不会通过整数追踪 provenance，因此整数到指针的转换始终产生带通配 provenance 的指针；这虽然安全，但在少数情况下可能限制优化（参见 [31] 中的讨论）。

当然，这取决于你如何定义 provenance。

@_**niluxv|401145** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628607807):
```quote
If you don't find it a "reasonable" assumption, then read (8) as "`ptr.write::<usize>(n); ptr.read::<*const u8>() == null().wrapping_add(n)` evaluates to `true` (unless UB), for every `n`" instead.
```

Sure, but then, is there a consistent semantics that violates this version of (8) but not the original?

I think there might be.  After all, one of the existing behaviors we're trying to preserve is that this can be optimized to false:

```rust
pub fn compare_to_elided_allocation(ptr1: *const u8) -> bool {
    let i_will_be_elided = 42u8;
    let ptr2 = &i_will_be_elided as *const u8;
    ptr1 == ptr2
}
```

This optimization conflicts with your theorem's result; therefore, it conflicts with the modified (8) when combined with your other reasonable assumptions.  But it does not necessarily conflict with your original (8).  After all, one of the only things the optimizer knows in this situation is that `ptr2` is not null.  Therefore, optimizing to false does not necessarily conflict with a rule that requires 'equal address implies equal pointer' *only for null*.  (Perhaps there is some other proof that it conflicts, but this has not been established.)

To be fair, LLVM will currently optimize to false even if `ptr1 == ptr2` is replaced with `ptr1.wrapping_add(42) == ptr2.wrapping_add(42)`.  This does conflict, since `ptr2.wrapping_add(42)` might be 0.  But my guess is that this optimization would be easier to sacrifice than the original version.

~~edit: that said, I have no idea how to solve the more general provenance monotonicity issue in this model.~~ Actually, I think a possible solution may exist along the lines of Alice's idea that there is a different kind of 'provenance' for elided allocations that does get tracked through integers.  The key is that this is less harmful than general provenance for integers.  One of the big blockers for general integer provenance is wanting to preserve the optimization '`a == b` ==> replace `a` with `b`' for integers `a`, `b`.  But an elided allocation's address is guaranteed to never compare equal to anything other than itself.

@_**niluxv|401145** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/628607807):
```quote
如果你不认为这是“合理”的假设，那就把 (8) 理解为：“对每个 `n`，`ptr.write::<usize>(n); ptr.read::<*const u8>() == null().wrapping_add(n)` 的求值结果为 `true`，除非发生 UB。”
```

当然，不过，是否存在一种自洽的语义，它违反这个版本的 (8)，却不违反原来的版本？

我认为可能存在。毕竟，我们想保留的一种现有行为，就是可以把下面这段代码优化成 false：

```rust
pub fn compare_to_elided_allocation(ptr1: *const u8) -> bool {
    let i_will_be_elided = 42u8;
    let ptr2 = &i_will_be_elided as *const u8;
    ptr1 == ptr2
}
```

这个优化与定理的结论冲突；因此，结合其他合理假设，它也与修改后的 (8) 冲突。但它未必与最初的 (8) 冲突。毕竟，在这种情况下，优化器知道的少数事实之一，就是 `ptr2` 不是 null。因此，优化为 false 不一定违反一个*仅对 null* 要求“地址相等蕴含指针相等”的规则。（也许可以通过其他证明推出冲突，但这尚未得到证明。）

公平地说，LLVM 目前即使把 `ptr1 == ptr2` 换成 `ptr1.wrapping_add(42) == ptr2.wrapping_add(42)`，也会优化为 false。这确实存在冲突，因为 `ptr2.wrapping_add(42)` 可能是 0。不过我猜，相比原始版本，放弃这个优化可能更容易接受。

~~补充：不过，我仍不知道该如何解决这个模型中更一般的 provenance 单调性问题。~~ 实际上，沿着 Alice 的思路，也许存在一种解决方案：为被消除的分配引入另一种“provenance”，并让它通过整数传播。关键在于，这比给整数普遍引入 provenance 的影响更小。一般整数 provenance 的一大障碍，是希望保留针对整数 `a`、`b` 的优化：“`a == b` ==> 将 `a` 替换为 `b`”。但被消除分配的地址，保证只会与它自身比较相等。

messages.en:
--
One other random note! 
> Multi-stage optimisation sucks for engineering reasons (e.g. which stage IR is the input for LTO?

Keep in mind that *some* kinds of 'multi-stage optimisation' can be reformulated so that instead of literally having multiple global stages, individual allocations or operations can be marked as 'in the next stage' so that the set of allowed optimizations changes for those specific things.  That would be much easier in practice.

Of course it's not always possible to reformulate that way.  But for allocation elision specifically, it seems plausible that at some point an allocation can be marked 'do not elide'.  Perhaps this can be worked into your framework somehow?
messages.zh:
--
另外再随便提一点！
> 出于工程原因，多阶段优化很麻烦（例如，LTO 应当以哪个阶段的 IR 为输入？）

请注意，*某些*“多阶段优化”可以换一种表述：不是真的设置多个全局阶段，而是把单个分配或操作标记为“处于下一阶段”，从而只改变这些特定对象允许进行的优化。这在实践中会容易得多。

当然，并非总能这样改写。但就分配消除而言，在某个时刻把一个分配标记为“不可消除”，似乎是可行的。也许能把这个思路融入你的框架？

messages.en: I don't think "you can't check if a pointer is null by `== ptr:null()`" is at all tenable
messages.zh: 我认为，“你不能通过 `== ptr:null()` 来判断指针是否为 null”是完全站不住脚的。

messages.en: And I also agree that we shouldn't special-case the 0 address
messages.zh: 而且我也同意，不应该特殊处理地址 0。

messages.en:
> Yes, but I don't think that works for (7) -> (1) or (7) -> (2) (and the chain (1) -> (2) is useless unless we also break (10), at which point we could probably have all optimisations at a single stage anyway).

Perhaps it could work.  LLVM could track, for each alloca and each function argument (maybe other instructions as well?), a flag for whether there has been a removed integer-typed write that _might_ target a pointer based on that alloca or argument.  This would fit well with LLVM's recent move to track pointer capture in increasing detail - the new `captures()`attribute already has a bunch of flags (`address`, `address_is_null`, `provenance`, `read_provenance`), and this could be a new one.  It would propagate upon inlining.

Then there would be a second flag for whether a pointer might have been stored to an allocation that had the first flag.  Allocations could not be elided if they had this flag.
messages.zh:
> 是的，但我认为这对 (7) -> (1) 或 (7) -> (2) 并不成立；至于链条 (1) -> (2)，除非我们同时破坏 (10)，否则它没有用，而一旦也破坏了 (10)，我们大概又能在同一个阶段完成所有优化了。

也许可以成立。LLVM 可以为每个 alloca 和每个函数参数（也许还有其他指令）追踪一个标志：是否有某次已被删除的整数类型写入，*可能*指向基于该 alloca 或参数的指针。这也很符合 LLVM 最近更细致地追踪指针捕获情况的方向：新的 `captures()` 属性已经有一组标志（`address`、`address_is_null`、`provenance`、`read_provenance`），这可以再加一个。内联时，该标志会随之传播。

然后再设第二个标志，表示某个指针是否可能被存入了带第一个标志的分配。如果分配带有这个第二个标志，就不能将其消除。

messages.en: In order to handle pointers passed indirectly into a function rather than as an argument, the first flag probably needs to be recursive: not just 'a pointer based on that alloca or argument' but 'a pointer based on a pointer loaded from that alloca or argument', and so on recursively.  But still, it's a single flag, a conservative appproximation; you don't have to track arbitrarily complex metadata.
messages.zh: 为了处理不是作为参数、而是间接传入函数的指针，第一个标志可能需要递归定义：不仅包括“基于该 alloca 或参数的指针”，还包括“基于从该 alloca 或参数加载出来的指针的指针”，并以此类推。但它终究只是一个标志、一种保守近似；不需要追踪任意复杂的元数据。

messages.en: Hopefully not so conservative that it would end up unnecessarily preventing a lot of allocation elision in practice.
messages.zh: 希望它不会保守到在实践中不必要地阻止大量分配消除。

messages.en: Not being able to remove unused `<=` operations sounds bad.  But you could say the same about ptrtoint.
messages.zh: 无法移除未使用的 `<=` 操作，听起来不太好。不过，ptrtoint 也有同样的问题。

messages.en: What it would mean is, if the compiler removes an unused `<=`, and then also removes the allocation on one side, then it has to remove the allocation on the other
messages.zh: 这意味着，如果编译器删除了一个结果未使用的 `<=`，随后又移除了其中一侧的分配，那么它也必须移除另一侧的分配。

messages.en: In many cases you could use `offset_from` instead to recover optimization potential
messages.zh: 在许多情况下，可以改用 `offset_from`，以恢复优化空间。

messages.en:
Not removing unused `<=` operations is actually the status quo with LLVM. Essentially, if you observe the result of a pointer comparison in any way, LLVM already refuses to remove the allocations:
https://godbolt.org/z/Ye43Tnrdr
messages.zh:
实际上，LLVM 目前就不会移除未使用的 `<=` 操作。基本上，只要以任何方式观察到了指针比较的结果，LLVM 就已经会拒绝移除相关分配：

@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/630929373):
```quote
The alternative would be to say high planes are > `usize::MAX`, I guess
```

This would be annoying for Miri. We want to limit the number of situations where it has to commit to a pointer potentially having non-0 plane without triggering UB. Because if Miri chooses plane 0 at that point, it could miss potential UB, but if it chooses non-0 plane, it could be forced to OOM later. If `<` forces same plane, the only way that can happen is equality check against every other address.
messages.zh:
@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/630929373):
```quote
我想，另一种选择是规定较高平面大于 `usize::MAX`。
```

这会给 Miri 带来麻烦。我们希望限制这样一种情况的数量：Miri 必须在不触发 UB 的情况下，承认某个指针的平面可能非零。因为如果 Miri 此时选择平面 0，就可能漏掉潜在 UB；但如果选择非零平面，之后又可能被迫发生 OOM。如果 `<` 会强制平面相同，那么只有把它与其他所有地址逐个比较相等，才会遇到这种情况。

messages.en: I think the right way to handle the planes model in a simulator like miri is to track a set of constraints. The whole point of using a DLO is that any finite set of constraints is satisfiable even if you just greedily pick numbers consistent with the orderings you have so far. This is similar to Rocq's universe partial order graph if you've ever encountered it.
messages.zh: 我认为，在 Miri 这样的模拟器中处理平面模型，正确方法是追踪一组约束。采用 DLO（稠密线性序）的意义就在于，任何有限约束集都是可满足的，即使只是贪心地挑选与目前已知次序一致的数字也可以。如果你接触过 Rocq 的宇宙偏序图，这与它很相似。

messages.en:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/630929923):
```quote
I am getting caught up on this (long!) thread, but what's wrong with essentially @**niluxv** 's rational-planes proposal, plus the plane-0 behavior for escaped pointers? (So actually there would be nonnegative rational planes)
```

Yes, it is a monster thread. I want to update [github issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/163013) so that it properly represents the current status, but I won't have the time for this for a while.

The short version: any planes-like proposal without integer provenance has the issue that either (a) `if ptr != core::ptr::null() { f(ptr) }` does **not** guarantee that `f` is only ever called with a non-zero-address pointer, or (b) you need to special-case pointer comparison when the addresses are non-zero, so `ptr1 == ptr2` is not equivalent to `ptr1.wrapping_add(37) == ptr2.wrapping_add(37)`. This is just fundamental to choosing to break property (4) in the Impossibility Theorem.

I don't think anyone really likes (b), and Jules and several others object to (a). The problem is of course code checking for a null pointer before creating a `NonNull` becomes a bit subtle. Technically we could say that creating a `NonNull` from a zero-address non-zero-plane pointer is immediate UB but only violates the safety condition (not the validity condition). Also quite subtle. (I would argue that code which does `ptr == null()` is plain wrong, it should have been `ptr.addr() == 0`, and we could introduce a method `ptr.is_null()` which just does `ptr.addr() == 0`).

Jules proposal is make `addr` impure (force plane 0), and not have provenance-monotonicity, so `x.write::<*const u8>(ptr); x.read::<usize>()` invokes immediate UB. I think that is a worse overall trade-off though. The whole point of `addr` was that it would be a pure alternative to `expose_provenance`, so it would keep current optimisations, but now `addr` suddenly optimises worse than what we expected for `expose_provenance`.

A third approach would be to say that integers carry plane-provenance. This is not as bad as SB/TB provenance. I think I have a fairly decent proposal in this direction as well, but don't really like it myself. Alice has been advocating for this approach.
messages.zh:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/630929923):
```quote
我正在补看这个很长的话题。不过，基本采用 @**niluxv** 的有理数平面提案，再让已逃逸的指针使用平面 0，这样有什么问题？也就是说，平面编号实际使用非负有理数。
```

是的，这是个巨型讨论串。我想更新 [GitHub issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/163013)，让它准确反映现状，但接下来一段时间我还腾不出空。

简短总结是：任何不为整数保留 provenance 的类似平面方案，都会面临二选一的问题：(a) `if ptr != core::ptr::null() { f(ptr) }` **不能**保证调用 `f` 时传入的指针地址非零；或者 (b) 必须特殊处理非零地址的指针比较，使 `ptr1 == ptr2` 不再等价于 `ptr1.wrapping_add(37) == ptr2.wrapping_add(37)`。这正是选择破坏不可能性定理中性质 (4) 所必然带来的结果。

我想没有人真的喜欢 (b)，而 Jules 和其他几位又反对 (a)。问题当然在于：先检查空指针，再创建 `NonNull` 的代码会变得微妙。从技术上说，我们可以规定，从地址为零但平面非零的指针创建 `NonNull` 会立即产生 UB，但只违反安全性条件、不违反有效性条件。这也很微妙。（我会认为，执行 `ptr == null()` 的代码本身就不对，本来应该写成 `ptr.addr() == 0`；我们还可以引入一个 `ptr.is_null()` 方法，让它直接执行 `ptr.addr() == 0`。）

Jules 的提案是让 `addr` 成为非纯操作，强制使用平面 0，并且不保留 provenance 单调性，因此 `x.write::<*const u8>(ptr); x.read::<usize>()` 会立即触发 UB。不过，我认为这种整体取舍更差。`addr` 的意义本来就是作为 `expose_provenance` 的纯操作替代方案，从而保留现有优化；但现在，`addr` 的优化效果却突然比我们原本对 `expose_provenance` 的预期还差。

第三条路是规定整数携带平面 provenance。它的影响不像 SB／TB provenance 那么严重。我觉得自己也有一个相当不错的相关提案，但我本人并不太喜欢它。Alice 一直在提倡这条路线。

```quote
The short version: any planes-like proposal without integer provenance has the issue that either (a) `if ptr != core::ptr::null() { f(ptr) }` does **not** guarantee that `f` is only ever called with a non-zero-address pointer, or (b) you need to special-case pointer comparison when the addresses are non-zero, so `ptr1 == ptr2` is not equivalent to `ptr1.wrapping_add(37) == ptr2.wrapping_add(37)`. 我问了 Claude 关于这个讨论的看法，它基本上也赞同该模型，以及你最后提出的细化：把 `x.is_null()` 当作原语，而不认为它等同于 `x == null()`。我觉得你在这里提到的问题不算太严重，因为在实际检查中，`x == null()` 仍然是正确的：地址为零的指针不能属于任何分配，其他平面也不例外。因此，本来就没有什么合理理由去构造不在平面 0 上的空指针，空指针检查也就可以使用任意一种方式。
```

messages.en:
@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/631608426):
```quote
That's basically the same as saying it's OOM. Given that Rust allows a program to OOM at any time, NB and OOM are essentially equivalent
```
I think they are still quite different. there are reasonable (as in, practically implementable) semantics of Rust that only allow OOM in certain places (e.g. a compiler that fixes the size of each stack frame, and that doesnt do outlining, and some more constraints whose details dont matter, so OOM can only occur at function calls). NB would then still incur a meaningful proof obligation for that compiler. so conceptually I'd still prefer to keep these two apart, even if LLVM may OOM anywhere.
messages.zh:
@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/631608426):
```quote
这基本等同于规定它会 OOM。既然 Rust 允许程序随时 OOM，NB 与 OOM 就本质等价。
```
我认为两者仍然相当不同。Rust 可以有一些合理、也就是实际可实现的语义，只允许在特定位置 OOM。例如，某个编译器固定每个栈帧的大小，不做 outlining，再加上一些细节不重要的限制，那么 OOM 就只能发生在函数调用处。此时，NB 仍会给该编译器带来实质性的证明义务。所以从概念上，我还是倾向于把这两者分开，即使 LLVM 可以在任意位置 OOM。

messages.en:
@_**niluxv|401145** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/631081748):
```quote
so `ptr1 == ptr2` is not equivalent to `ptr1.wrapping_add(37) == ptr2.wrapping_add(37)`
```

the question of ptr arithmetic is an interesting one -- if ptr.addr() is usize::MAX - 2, what does `ptr.wrapping_add(4)` do? does it wrap around the edge of its current plane or does it move to the next plane?
I think the VeLLVM paper I mentioned does the equivalent of making it move to the next plane, which is why they need overflow checks in the generated code. so we probably should say that arithmetic is confided to a plane, as odd as that behavior is when viewing addresses as unbounded natural numbers.
messages.zh:
@_**niluxv|401145** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/631081748):
```quote
所以 `ptr1 == ptr2` 不等价于 `ptr1.wrapping_add(37) == ptr2.wrapping_add(37)`。
```

指针算术的问题很有意思：如果 ptr.addr() 是 usize::MAX - 2，那么 `ptr.wrapping_add(4)` 会做什么？它是在当前平面的边缘回绕，还是移动到下一个平面？
我提到的 VeLLVM 论文采用的行为，相当于让它移动到下一个平面，这也是它们需要在生成代码中插入溢出检查的原因。因此，我们大概应当规定算术被限制在一个平面内，尽管把地址看作无界自然数时，这种行为会显得奇怪。

messages.en:
you still have to make that fit into the opsem. we had proposals like that at the start, they all had some unfortunate side effects. In particular, the current optimizations keep the allocation if the address is observed (e.g. printed out), but treats `addr` as pure. 
But the address is just an integer without provenance, so it can't track how it's observed. Hence the only way to do something like this is to make `addr` itself have the side effect of forcing the allocation to be kept.
messages.zh:
你仍然必须让它与操作语义相容。我们一开始就有类似提案，但它们都有一些不幸的副作用。尤其是，目前的优化会在地址被观察到（例如被打印）时保留分配，却把 `addr` 当作纯操作。
但地址只是没有 provenance 的整数，无法追踪它是如何被观察的。因此，要做到类似的事，唯一的方法就是让 `addr` 本身具有强制保留该分配的副作用。

messages.en: in the impossibility theorem, this is the "`addr()` is pure" / "integers have no provenance" parts
messages.zh: 在不可能性定理中，这对应于“`addr()` 是纯操作”和“整数没有 provenance”这两部分。

messages.en: Dumb question from the ringside: is the idea to (in some sense) say in more concrete terms that when the compiler performs an allocation, it will allocate on plane 0 by default, and when it optimises an allocation out it promotes that allocation to some higher plane?
messages.zh: 一个旁观者的傻问题：其思路是否可以在某种意义上更具体地表述为：编译器执行分配时，默认在平面 0 分配；而当它优化掉某次分配时，就把该分配提升到某个更高的平面？

messages.en: (Though this is `t-opsem` and not `t-in-practice`.)
messages.zh: （不过这里是 `t-opsem`，不是 `t-in-practice`。）

messages.en: Not a dumb question, I assumed that as well, but now I'm not sure.
messages.zh: 这不是傻问题，我原先也是这么理解的，但现在不确定了。

messages.en: Essentially yes. If the optimiser removes a dead allocation from the program we justify that by saying that the demon could have chosen that allocation to be allocated in some higher plane. And the translation to assembly is justified by saying that every allocation (that is still around) would have been chosen in plane 0.
messages.zh: 基本上是的。如果优化器从程序中移除一次无用分配，我们就以“恶魔本可以选择在某个更高的平面进行该分配”来论证其合理性。而转换为汇编的合理性则来自：每次仍然保留的分配，都可以被选择在平面 0 进行。

topics.name: What is the type ABI compatible with C enums?
topics.name_zh: What is the type ABI compatible with C enums?
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：Rust 与 C 枚举进行 `extern "C"` ABI 交互时，应使用 `#[repr(i32)] enum`、`#[repr(transparent)] struct Foo(i32)`，还是直接使用 `i32`；目前 Miri 对 `#[repr(i32)] enum` 与后两者的兼容性判断并不一致。
- **重要观点**：Rust Nomicon 声明，`#[repr(i32)]` 等整数表示的类型，与具有相同符号性和大小的 C 枚举 ABI 兼容；但 C（尤其 C23 之前）的枚举底层整数类型由编译器决定。C 枚举通常可以包含未声明的整数值，而 Rust 枚举出现无效值会导致 UB，因此若 C/C++ 可以写入任意值，使用整数或透明包装类型更安全；表示 C `int` 时还应使用 `ffi::c_int` 而不是 `i32`。
- **讨论的方案**：可以让 `#[repr(i32)]` 枚举与 `i32` 等价，或引入 `#[repr(transparent)] struct` / `#[repr(c_enum)] struct` 作为 C 枚举的承载类型，也可以支持 open enum。另一个方向是利用 `#[cfi_encoding]` 为透明包装类型指定与 C 枚举相同的 CFI 标识；有人认为这正是该属性的用途，也有人担心将 ABI 语义绑定到 CFI。
- **仍未解决的问题**：C 与 Rust ABI 兼容规则文档十分有限，且兼容关系不具传递性，使 `repr(transparent)`、底层整数、C 枚举之间的关系难以推理。讨论倾向于未来提供专门定义类型“ABI 名称/等价类型”的属性（例如 `#[abi_is = ...]` 或 `#[repr(Equivalent = ...)]`），但尚未形成最终方案。

messages.en:
I see three valid options:
1. `#[repr(i32)] enum Foo { Variants }`
2. `#[repr(transparent)] struct Foo(i32)`
3. `i32`

Ideally, all these three should be ABI compatible, so there is no point in this question. But currently, according to miri, 1 is not compatible with others. 1 is used by bindgen, but 2 or 3 are needed in some cases if a Rust function wants to implement a C header. So which one is correct?
messages.zh:
我看到三个有效的选项：
1. `#[repr(i32)] enum Foo { Variants }`
2. `#[repr(transparent)] struct Foo(i32)`
3. `i32`

理想情况下，三者都应该 ABI 兼容，也就不存在这个问题。但目前按照 Miri 的判断，1 与其余选项不兼容。bindgen 使用 1，但 Rust 函数要实现 C 头文件中的声明时，有些情况下需要 2 或 3。那么哪一个才正确？

messages.en:
We promise that 1 is compatible with a C enum of the same size, though before C23, the size of an enum is pretty much "whatever integer type the compiler feels like".  

Common Wisdom is that you should use the integer of the same size directly (no enum), to reduce UB when new values are added, but that's even less well defined in terms of ABI compatibility.
messages.zh:
我们保证 1 与大小相同的 C 枚举兼容，不过在 C23 之前，枚举的大小基本就是“编译器想选哪种整数类型就选哪种”。

通常的建议是直接使用相同大小的整数类型，不要使用枚举，以便在添加新值时减少 UB；但就 ABI 兼容性而言，这种做法的定义反而更加不明确。

messages.en: Relevant: https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/628
messages.zh: 相关内容：https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/628

messages.en: also note that c enums can often hold integers that are not among their variants, but in rust this is ub
messages.zh: 还要注意，C 枚举通常可以容纳不属于其变体的整数，但在 Rust 中这属于 UB。

messages.en: The fact that C compatibility rules are non-transitive also makes reasoning about this weird
messages.zh: C 的兼容性规则不具有传递性，这也让相关推理很古怪。

messages.en: Also the docs on what is compatible between C and Rust are extremely limited
messages.zh: 另外，关于 C 与 Rust 之间哪些类型兼容，文档的说明极其有限。

messages.en: (also if you're using `i32` to mean `int`, you should be using `ffi::c_int` instead)
messages.zh: （另外，如果你用 `i32` 来表示 `int`，就应该改用 `ffi::c_int`。）

messages.en:
But my source for "1 is compatible with a C enum that *also* declares the backing integer" is https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/nomicon/other-reprs.html#repru-repri

> Note that the function call ABI for [`repr($int)`] types is still in general unspecified, except that across `extern "C"` calls they are ABI-compatible with C enums of the same sign and size.
messages.zh:
不过，我所说的“1 与同样声明了底层整数类型的 C 枚举兼容”的依据是 https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/nomicon/other-reprs.html#repru-repri

> 请注意，[`repr($int)`] 类型的函数调用 ABI 通常仍未指定；唯一例外是，在 `extern "C"` 调用中，它们与符号性和大小相同的 C 枚举 ABI 兼容。

messages.en: so a `enum Meow: int32_t` (C23 feature) is ABI compatible with a `#[repr(i32)] enum Meow`
messages.zh: 所以 `enum Meow: int32_t`（C23 特性）与 `#[repr(i32)] enum Meow` ABI 兼容。

messages.en: But doesn't the C enum let you assign invalid variants to it?
messages.zh: 但 C 枚举不是允许赋给它无效的变体值吗？

messages.en: Correct, they're ABI compatible, but there may be other ways to cause UB
messages.zh: 没错，它们 ABI 兼容，但仍可能以其他方式触发 UB。

messages.en:
If your enum is writable from C++, you need option 2 or 3, unless you are very very careful to always assign valid Rust values to the enum.

In the context of Zngur, you could use option 1 and a wrapper type that makes sure C++ always sets valid values. But at that point, you might as well use the wrapper type that is already in option 2.
messages.zh:
如果 C++ 可以写入你的枚举，就需要选项 2 或 3，除非你非常谨慎，始终只给枚举赋合法的 Rust 值。

对于 Zngur，你可以采用选项 1，再用一个包装类型确保 C++ 总是设置合法值。但这样一来，还不如直接使用选项 2 中已有的包装类型。

messages.en: The only way to do that is to mark the struct `#[repr(transparent)]` and to use `#[cfi_encoding]` to alter its name to that of the enum.
messages.zh: 唯一的办法是给结构体标记 `#[repr(transparent)]`，并使用 `#[cfi_encoding]` 将其名称改成枚举的名称。
